name: 45 Degree Hyperextension
description: A lower back exercise on a 45-degree hyperextension bench that targets the spinal erectors and posterior chain.
instructions: Position yourself on the 45-degree hyperextension bench with ankles secured.
Cross arms over chest or place hands behind head.
Lower your upper body forward at the hips.
Stop when your upper body is just below parallel to the floor.
Lift your torso back up in line with your legs.
breathingInstructions: Exhale as you rise, inhale as you lower.
attribution: Free Exercise DB with Videos (MIT License)

name: 45-Degree Bicycle Twisting Crunch
description: A twisting ab exercise performed at a 45-degree angle to target the abdominals and obliques.
instructions: Lie on your back with hands behind your head and knees bent.
Lift your shoulders and feet off the ground, creating a 45-degree angle with your torso and legs.
Bring your right knee in while twisting your left elbow towards it.
Switch sides, extending the right leg and bringing the left knee in as your right elbow moves towards it.
Continue alternating sides in a smooth, controlled motion.
formCues: Keep lower back pressed to ground
Move legs in a controlled fashion
breathingInstructions: Exhale as you crunch and twist, inhale as you return to center.
attribution: Free Exercise DB with Videos (MIT License)

name: All Fours Groin Stretch
description: A floor stretch on hands and knees targeting the adductors and groin area.
instructions: Start on hands and knees (quadruped position).
Slide knees apart, keeping shins and feet in line with knees.
Lower hips toward the floor, maintaining a flat back.
Move hips back gently until you feel a stretch in the groin.
Hold the position and breathe deeply.
breathingInstructions: Breathe slowly and deeply throughout the stretch.
attribution: Free Exercise DB with Videos (MIT License)

name: Band Assisted Pull-up
description: A vertical pulling exercise using a resistance band for assistance to build pull-up strength in the lats, biceps, and upper back.
instructions: Loop the band securely over a pull-up bar and place one foot or knee into the bottom of the band.
Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder width with your palms facing away from you.
Hang with straight arms, tighten your midsection, and pull your shoulders down away from your ears.
Pull yourself up by driving your elbows down and back until your chin clears the bar.
Lower yourself with control until your arms are straight again, keeping tension through your torso.
commonMistakes: Kicking or swinging to get up
Shrugging shoulders up toward the ears
Stopping short with the chin below the bar
Dropping quickly to the bottom without control
breathingInstructions: Inhale at the bottom before you pull, exhale as you pull up, and inhale again as you lower under control.
attribution: Free Exercise DB with Videos (MIT License)

name: Band Bent-Over Rear Lateral Raise
description: A rear shoulder and upper back exercise using a resistance band in a bent-over position.
instructions: Stand on a resistance band, feet shoulder-width apart.
Hinge forward at hips, keeping back flat.
Hold band with both hands, arms hanging down.
Raise arms out to sides until parallel with shoulders.
Lower arms back down with control.
breathingInstructions: Exhale during the raise, inhale during the lowering.
attribution: Free Exercise DB with Videos (MIT License)

name: Band Hip Abduction
description: A lateral leg movement with a resistance band to activate and strengthen the hip abductor muscles.
instructions: Place a resistance band around your thighs or ankles.
Stand tall with feet hip-width apart.
Shift weight to one leg.
Lift the other leg laterally against band resistance.
Return leg to start; repeat on both sides.
breathingInstructions: Exhale as you lift leg, inhale as you return.
attribution: Free Exercise DB with Videos (MIT License)

name: Band Hip Adduction
description: A resistance band exercise that strengthens the inner thigh muscles through hip adduction.
instructions: Secure a resistance band to a sturdy anchor at ankle height.
Loop the other end around your working ankle.
Stand tall and hold onto a support if needed.
Bring your working leg across your body, adducting at the hip.
Slowly return to the starting position and repeat.
breathingInstructions: Exhale as you pull leg inward, inhale as you return.
attribution: Free Exercise DB with Videos (MIT License)

name: Band Kneeling One Arm Pulldown
description: A kneeling single-arm band pulldown that trains the lats by pulling the elbow down from an overhead position.
instructions: Anchor the band overhead and kneel facing the anchor point.
Grab the band with one hand and extend that arm up and slightly forward.
Brace your torso and keep your chest tall without leaning back.
Pull your elbow down toward your side until your hand reaches about shoulder or rib level.
Squeeze your lat at the bottom while keeping your shoulder down.
Slowly straighten your arm back overhead under control.
Complete all reps on one side, then switch arms.
commonMistakes: Leaning the torso back to finish the pull
Shrugging the shoulder up toward the ear
Bending and straightening the wrist during the pull
Letting the band snap the arm back overhead
breathingInstructions: Inhale as your arm returns overhead, and exhale as you pull the band down to your side.
attribution: Free Exercise DB with Videos (MIT License)

name: Band One Arm Front Raise
description: Isolation shoulder exercise raising one arm forward against band resistance to target the anterior deltoid.
instructions: Stand with one foot on the band for resistance.
Hold handle in one hand at thigh level, palm facing down.
Keep arm straight, raise it forward to shoulder height.
Pause briefly at the top.
Lower arm back down slowly and repeat.
breathingInstructions: Exhale as you lift, inhale as you lower.
attribution: Free Exercise DB with Videos (MIT License)

name: Band One-Leg Kickback (Bent Position)
description: A glute-focused kickback performed from a bent-over position using a resistance band for added intensity.
instructions: Anchor the band and loop it around your working ankle.
Start on all fours with hands under shoulders and knees bent.
Engage your core and extend one leg backward against band resistance.
Pause and squeeze the glute at the top.
Return to starting position and repeat for desired reps, then switch legs.
breathingInstructions: Exhale as you kick back, inhale as you bring the knee in.
attribution: Free Exercise DB with Videos (MIT License)

name: Band Overhead Triceps Extension
description: A standing band triceps exercise where you extend your elbows overhead while keeping your upper arms mostly fixed.
instructions: Stand on the middle of the band with feet hip-width apart and hold one end in each hand.
Raise your hands overhead and bend your elbows so your hands move behind your head.
Keep your upper arms close to your ears and brace your midsection.
Straighten your elbows to press the band overhead until your arms are fully extended.
Pause briefly at the top, then bend your elbows slowly to return behind your head.
Repeat without letting your elbows flare wide.
commonMistakes: Elbows flare out to the sides
Lower back arches as the band goes overhead
Upper arms drift forward and backward
Only moving partway instead of fully extending
breathingInstructions: Inhale as you lower your hands behind your head, and exhale as you straighten your elbows overhead.
attribution: Free Exercise DB with Videos (MIT License)

name: Band Prone Leg Curl
description: A hamstring isolation exercise performed lying face down and flexing the knee using resistance from a band.
instructions: Anchor the band securely at ground level.
Lie face down with legs extended.
Loop the band around your ankle.
Flex your knee, bringing your heel toward your glutes.
Slowly return to the start; repeat and switch legs if desired.
breathingInstructions: Exhale as you curl, inhale as you lower.
attribution: Free Exercise DB with Videos (MIT License)

name: Band Pull Through
description: A banded hip hinge that trains the glutes and hamstrings by pulling the band through the legs as you stand tall.
instructions: Anchor the band at floor level and loop it between your legs.
Face away from the anchor and walk forward until the band is taut.
Stand with feet about hip-width apart and soften your knees.
Push your hips back and hinge forward, letting the band travel behind you.
Lower until you feel your hamstrings stretch while keeping your back flat.
Drive your hips forward to stand tall and squeeze your glutes at the top.
commonMistakes: Squatting down instead of hinging back
Rounding the lower back as you fold forward
Letting the band pull the hips backward at lockout
Bending the knees too much and shifting into the quads
breathingInstructions: Inhale as you hinge back and exhale as you drive your hips forward to stand.
attribution: Free Exercise DB with Videos (MIT License)

name: Band Resisted Decline Sit-Up
description: A decline sit-up performed with band resistance to increase tension on the abdominals.
instructions: Attach a resistance band securely behind the decline bench.
Lie on the bench with your feet anchored, holding the band at the chest or behind the neck.
Engage your core and perform a sit-up, raising your torso towards your knees.
Control the movement back down to starting position.
Repeat for the desired repetitions.
breathingInstructions: Exhale as you sit up, inhale as you lower down.
attribution: Free Exercise DB with Videos (MIT License)

name: Band Seated Leg Extension
description: A seated exercise using a resistance band to isolate and strengthen the quadriceps.
instructions: Sit upright on a sturdy chair with feet flat.
Anchor one end of a band behind the chair leg.
Loop the other end of the band around your ankle.
Raise your lower leg to extend the knee fully.
Lower the leg back down under control; repeat and switch legs.
formCues: Do not lock knee at top
commonMistakes: Allowing the knee to drift or twist
breathingInstructions: Exhale as you extend, inhale as you return.
attribution: Free Exercise DB with Videos (MIT License)

name: Band Seated Row
alternativeNames: band one arm twisting seated row
description: Seated row using resistance bands that targets the mid-back and lats.
instructions: Sit on the floor with legs straight and loop the band over your feet.
Grab the band handles or ends with both hands, arms extended.
Keep back straight and chest up.
Pull the handles back, driving elbows past your torso and squeezing shoulder blades.
Release slowly to the starting position.
breathingInstructions: Exhale as you row, inhale as you return to start.

name: Band Shoulder Warm-Up Stretch
description: A shoulder stretch and mobility drill using a resistance band to warm up the deltoids and rotator cuff.
instructions: Stand tall and grip band with hands wider than shoulders.
Hold arms straight, band in front of thighs.
Slowly raise band overhead while keeping arms straight.
Move band behind head and down to lower back.
Reverse the movement to bring band to starting position.
breathingInstructions: Breathe naturally throughout stretch.
attribution: Free Exercise DB with Videos (MIT License)

name: Band Side Bend
description: A standing lateral bend using a resistance band to target and strengthen the oblique muscles.
instructions: Anchor the resistance band securely at ground level.
Stand beside the anchor point, feet shoulder-width apart.
Hold the band handle with the outside hand, arm extended alongside your body.
Keeping your torso straight, bend sideways at the waist away from the anchor.
Return to the starting position and repeat for reps, then switch sides.

breathingInstructions: Exhale while bending, inhale on the return.

name: Band Standing Calf Raise
description: Standing calf raise performed with a resistance band to strengthen the calves.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width on the band.
Hold band handles by sides or at shoulders for resistance.
Keep torso upright and brace core.
Raise heels to stand on the balls of your feet, contracting calves.
Lower heels back to the floor slowly.
breathingInstructions: Exhale as you rise, inhale as you lower.
attribution: Free Exercise DB with Videos (MIT License)

name: Band Standing Crunch
description: A standing abdominal crunch using a resistance band to train the abs and obliques through spinal flexion.
instructions: Attach the band to an anchor around waist height and stand facing away from it.
Hold the band at your chest with both hands and step forward until the band is taut.
Set your feet about hip-width apart and soften your knees.
Brace your midsection and curl your ribs down, bending your torso forward.
Pause briefly at the bottom while keeping your hips mostly still.
Slowly uncurl your torso and return to an upright position under control.

Hinging at the hips like a bow instead of rounding into a crunch.

name: Band Standing Leg Curl
alternativeNames: band one arm standing low row
description: A standing hamstring curl variation using resistance from a band for leg flexion.
instructions: Anchor the resistance band behind you at ground level.
Loop the band around one ankle.
Stand on the opposite leg and balance.
Curl your heel toward your glutes by flexing your knee.
Lower leg slowly; repeat and switch sides.
breathingInstructions: Exhale as you curl, inhale as you return.
attribution: Free Exercise DB with Videos (MIT License)

name: Band Standing Lift
description: A diagonal band movement to train the obliques and core stabilizers.
instructions: Anchor the band low near the floor.
Stand side-on to the anchor, feet shoulder-width.
Hold the band handle with both hands at hip level.
Lift and rotate your torso diagonally to the opposite side and above shoulder.
Return to start; repeat, then switch sides.
breathingInstructions: Exhale as you lift/rotate, inhale as you return.
attribution: Free Exercise DB with Videos (MIT License)

name: Band Standing Rear Delt Row
description: A bent-over band row with elbows flared out to target the rear delts and upper back.
instructions: Stand on the middle of the band with feet about hip-width apart and hold one end in each hand.
Hinge forward at the hips with a soft bend in your knees until your torso leans forward and your arms hang below your shoulders.
Set your shoulders down and keep your chest open with your palms facing each other or slightly inward.
Pull your elbows out and back until your hands reach around lower chest to upper rib level.
Squeeze your rear shoulders and upper back at the top without shrugging.
Lower your hands back down under control until your arms are straight again.
commonMistakes: Standing too upright and turning it into a regular row
Shrugging the shoulders toward the ears at the top
Pulling the hands too low toward the waist
Rounding the upper or lower back while hinging
breathingInstructions: Inhale as you lower to the start, and exhale as you row the band up.

name: Band Straight-Back Seated Row
alternativeNames: resistance band seated straight back row
description: A banded rowing movement emphasizing the upper back and lats while seated with a straight torso.
instructions: Sit on the floor and extend your legs forward.
Loop the band around your feet securely.
Grip the band handles with both hands, arms extended.
Keeping your back straight, pull the handles toward your waist, elbows close to your body.
Pause, squeeze your shoulder blades, then slowly return to the starting position.
commonMistakes: Using momentum rather than back muscles
breathingInstructions: Exhale as you row, inhale as you return to start.

name: Band Triceps Pushdown
description: An isolation triceps exercise using an overhead-anchored band to straighten the elbows against resistance.
instructions: Anchor the band overhead and stand facing it with a handle or end in each hand.
Bend your elbows to about 90 degrees and pin your upper arms close to your sides.
Brace your torso and press your hands straight down until your elbows fully extend.
Pause briefly at the bottom and squeeze your triceps.
Slowly let the band rise back up until your forearms return to the start position.
Repeat without letting your elbows drift forward or outward.
commonMistakes: Upper arms swinging forward and back
Elbows flaring away from the torso
Leaning body weight onto the band
Stopping short of full elbow extension
breathingInstructions: Exhale as you press the band down, and inhale as you return to the start.

name: Barbell Back Squat
description: Classic compound lower body lift with barbell across traps, targeting quads and glutes.
instructions: Position barbell on upper traps, unrack.
Stand with feet shoulder-width apart.
Descend into squat keeping back neutral.
Lower until thighs parallel or below.
Drive up through heels to standing.
breathingInstructions: Inhale lowering, exhale rising.
attribution: Free Exercise DB with Videos (MIT License)

name: Barbell Bench Press
description: A flat bench press using a barbell to train the chest, triceps, and shoulders with a horizontal pressing motion.
instructions: Lie flat on the bench with your eyes under the bar and plant your feet firmly on the floor.
Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder width and straighten your arms to unrack it over your chest.
Lower the bar under control to your mid-chest while keeping your wrists stacked over your forearms.
Lightly touch your chest, then press the bar straight up until your arms are fully extended.
Guide the bar back into the rack once you finish the set.
commonMistakes: Bar drifts toward the neck or stomach
Elbows flare straight out from the shoulders
Wrists bend backward under the bar
Hips lift off the bench during the press
breathingInstructions: Inhale as you lower the bar to your chest, and exhale as you press it back up.
attribution: Free Exercise DB with Videos (MIT License)

name: Barbell Clean And Press
description: A full-body barbell lift that moves the bar from the floor to the shoulders, then presses it overhead.
instructions: Stand with your feet hip- to shoulder-width apart and place the barbell over your midfoot.
Bend at your hips and knees, grip the bar just outside your legs, and set your back flat with your chest up.
Push the floor away and lift the bar, keeping it close to your shins and thighs as you stand.
Explosively extend your hips, knees, and ankles, then shrug and pull yourself under the bar.
Catch the bar on the fronts of your shoulders with elbows forward and stand tall.
Press the bar straight overhead until your arms are locked out and the bar is over your shoulders.
Lower the bar back to your shoulders, then guide it down to the floor under control.
commonMistakes: Starting with the bar too far in front of the feet
Rounding the lower back when pulling from the floor
Catching the bar with elbows low and chest collapsed
Pressing the bar forward instead of overhead

name: Barbell Close Grip Bench Press
description: Bench press variation with close grip targeting triceps along with chest and shoulders.
instructions: Lie on bench and grasp barbell with close grip.
Unrack and position bar above lower chest.
Lower bar slowly, elbows close to sides.
Touch chest briefly, then press bar to starting position.
Repeat for reps.
breathingInstructions: Exhale pressing up, inhale lowering bar.
attribution: Free Exercise DB with Videos (MIT License)

name: Barbell Curl
description: A standing biceps exercise where you curl a barbell from your thighs to shoulder height with an underhand grip.
instructions: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart and hold the barbell at your thighs with an underhand grip.
Set your shoulders back, brace your torso, and keep your elbows pinned by your sides.
Curl the bar upward by bending your elbows until the bar reaches about shoulder height.
Pause briefly at the top and squeeze your biceps without letting your elbows drift forward.
Lower the bar slowly back to your thighs until your arms are straight.
commonMistakes: Swinging the torso to start the bar moving
Letting the elbows drift forward as the bar rises
Bending the wrists back instead of keeping them neutral
Dropping the bar quickly on the way down
breathingInstructions: Exhale as you curl the bar up, and inhale as you lower it back down under control.

name: Barbell Decline Bench Press
description: A decline barbell press done on a downward-angled bench to train the chest, triceps, and shoulders through a pressing pattern.
instructions: Lie on the decline bench and secure your legs under the pads with your eyes under the bar.
Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder width and pull your shoulder blades back into the bench.
Unrack the bar and hold it above your lower chest with straight wrists and locked elbows.
Lower the bar under control to your lower chest or upper sternum while keeping your elbows at about a 45-degree angle.
Press the bar straight up until your elbows are extended and the bar returns over your lower chest.
Repeat each rep with the same bar path and controlled tempo.
commonMistakes: Bouncing the bar off the chest
Flaring the elbows straight out to the sides
Letting the wrists bend back under the bar
Pressing the bar toward the face instead of over the chest
breathingInstructions: Inhale as you lower the bar to your chest, and exhale as you press it back up.
attribution: Free Exercise DB with Videos (MIT License)

name: Barbell Drag Curl
description: A barbell biceps curl variation where the bar stays close to the torso and the elbows move back as you lift.
instructions: Stand tall with feet about hip-width apart and hold the barbell with an underhand grip at your thighs.
Pull your shoulders slightly back and keep your elbows behind your torso.
Curl the bar upward by sliding it close along the front of your body as your elbows travel back.
Lift until the bar reaches your upper stomach or lower chest without letting it drift away from you.
Lower the barbell slowly along the same path until your arms are straight again.
commonMistakes: Letting the bar swing forward away from the body
Bending the wrists back as the bar rises
Rocking the torso to start the curl
Flaring the elbows out to the sides
breathingInstructions: Inhale at the bottom, exhale as you drag-curl the bar up, and inhale as you lower it back down.
attribution: Free Exercise DB with Videos (MIT License)

name: Barbell Front Raise
description: A shoulder isolation exercise where you lift a barbell straight in front of your body to train the front delts.
instructions: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart and hold the barbell against your thighs with an overhand grip.
Brace your core and keep a soft bend in your elbows.
Raise the barbell straight forward in front of you until it reaches shoulder height.
Pause briefly without shrugging your shoulders.
Lower the barbell back to your thighs with control.
Reset your posture and repeat the movement.
commonMistakes: Leaning back to start the lift.
Swinging the barbell with the hips.
Raising the barbell above shoulder height.
Shrugging the shoulders toward the ears.
breathingInstructions: Exhale as you raise the barbell, and inhale as you lower it back down.

name: Barbell Front Squat
description: Squat variation with barbell held at the front rack position, targeting the quadriceps.
instructions: Rack barbell at collarbone level, elbows up.
Stand with feet shoulder-width apart.
Descend into squat keeping torso upright.
Lower until thighs are parallel to floor.
Drive up through heels to stand.
breathingInstructions: Inhale when lowering, exhale standing up.
attribution: Free Exercise DB with Videos (MIT License)

name: Barbell Incline Bench Press
description: A pressing exercise on an incline bench using a barbell to train the upper chest, shoulders, and triceps.
instructions: Set an incline bench and lie back with your eyes under the bar and your feet flat on the floor.
Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder width with straight wrists and pull your shoulder blades down and back.
Unrack the bar and hold it above your upper chest with your arms straight.
Lower the bar under control to your upper chest, keeping your elbows slightly tucked from straight out.
Press the bar upward until your arms are straight again, keeping the bar path over your shoulders.
Rack the bar back onto the supports with control after your final rep.
commonMistakes: Flaring the elbows straight out to the sides
Bouncing the bar off the chest
Lifting the feet or shifting on the bench
Lowering the bar to the neck or stomach
breathingInstructions: Inhale as you lower the bar to your chest, and exhale as you press it back up.

name: Barbell Lunge
description: A lower-body lunge with a barbell on your upper back that trains the glutes, quads, and hamstrings one leg at a time.
instructions: Set the barbell across your upper back and stand tall with feet hip-width apart.
Brace your core and take a controlled step forward with one foot.
Lower your body until both knees bend and your back knee moves toward the floor.
Keep your front foot flat and your torso upright at the bottom position.
Push through the front foot to stand back up and bring your feet together.
Repeat on the other side, alternating legs each rep.
commonMistakes: Taking such a short step that the front knee shoots far past the toes.
Leaning the torso forward as you lower.
Letting the front knee cave inward.
Pushing off the back foot instead of driving through the front foot.
breathingInstructions: Inhale as you step forward and lower down, then exhale as you push back to standing.

name: Barbell Prone Incline Curl
description: A chest-supported biceps curl on an incline bench using a barbell to isolate elbow flexion with minimal body swing.
instructions: Set an incline bench and lie face down with your chest supported and your feet planted on the floor.
Hold the barbell with an underhand grip about shoulder-width apart and let your arms hang straight down.
Brace your torso against the bench and keep your upper arms still.
Curl the barbell upward by bending your elbows until the bar reaches near the front of your shoulders.
Squeeze your biceps briefly at the top without lifting your chest off the bench.
Lower the barbell under control until your elbows are fully extended again.

Using body swing or kicking the legs to create momentum
Dropping the bar quickly instead of lowering it under control

name: Barbell Rear Delt Raise
description: A bent-over barbell raise that targets the rear delts by lifting the arms out to the sides while holding a barbell.

Soften your knees and hinge at your hips until your torso is nearly parallel to the floor.
Let the bar hang below your chest with your arms straight and your neck neutral.
Raise the bar out and up by moving your upper arms to the sides until they reach shoulder height.

Lower the bar under control to the starting position.
commonMistakes: Rounding the lower back as you hinge forward
Swinging the torso to heave the bar upward
Shrugging the shoulders toward the ears

Rest your forearms on your thighs with wrists hanging just beyond your knees.
Begin with your wrists flexed downward.
Slowly curl your wrists upward, lifting the barbell.
Lower under control to the starting position.
commonMistakes: Letting the barbell roll in hands
breathingInstructions: Exhale as you curl the bar up, inhale as you lower.

name: Barbell Seated Behind-The-Neck Press

Unrack barbell and hold above your head.
Lower barbell behind your head to just below ear level.
Press barbell back up to the starting position.
Repeat for desired reps, keeping core engaged.
breathingInstructions: Exhale when pressing up, inhale when lowering the bar.
attribution: Free Exercise DB with Videos (MIT License)

name: Barbell Shrug
description: A standing trap exercise where you hold a barbell at your thighs and lift your shoulders straight up and down.
instructions: Stand tall with your feet hip- to shoulder-width apart and hold the barbell in front of your thighs with an overhand grip.
Let your arms hang straight, brace your torso, and keep your chest up.
Lift your shoulders straight up toward your ears without bending your elbows or leaning back.
Pause briefly at the top and squeeze your upper traps.
Lower your shoulders under control until they return to the starting position.
commonMistakes: Bending the elbows to curl the bar upward.
Rolling the shoulders forward or backward at the top.
Leaning back and swinging the torso to move the bar.
Letting the head jut forward as the shoulders rise.
breathingInstructions: Inhale before each rep, exhale as you shrug your shoulders up, and inhale as you lower back down.

name: Barbell Standing Back Wrist Curl
description: A standing forearm exercise where you hold a barbell behind your body and lift it by curling only your wrists.
instructions: Stand tall with your feet about hip-width apart and hold a barbell behind your hips with an overhand grip.
Let the bar rest across your fingers so your knuckles face the floor and your palms face behind you.
Keep your elbows close to your sides and straighten your wrists to lower the bar toward your fingertips.
Curl your wrists upward to roll the bar back into your hands and lift it as high as you can.
Pause briefly at the top, then lower the bar with control back to the starting position.
commonMistakes: Swinging the bar with the shoulders or torso
Bending the elbows to lift the bar
Letting the bar slip too far out of the hands
breathingInstructions: Inhale as you lower the bar toward your fingertips, and exhale as you curl your wrists up.
attribution: Free Exercise DB with Videos (MIT License)

name: Barbell Straight Leg Deadlift
description: A barbell hip hinge that trains the hamstrings and glutes by lowering the bar down the legs with minimal knee bend.
instructions: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart and hold the barbell in front of your thighs with straight arms.
Soften your knees slightly and brace your midsection.
Push your hips back and lower the bar down your legs while keeping your back flat and your legs nearly straight.
Lower until the bar reaches mid-shin or until you feel a strong hamstring stretch without losing your back position.
Drive your hips forward and stand tall, keeping the bar close to your legs the whole way up.
Finish with your hips locked out and shoulders stacked over your hips.
commonMistakes: Bending the knees into a squat as the bar lowers
Letting the bar drift forward away from the legs
Rounding the lower back near the bottom
Jerking the bar off the bottom instead of lifting smoothly

description: A standing biceps exercise where you curl weights from your sides up toward your shoulders with palms facing forward.
instructions: Stand tall with a weight in each hand at your sides and turn your palms forward.
Set your feet about hip-width apart and keep your elbows pinned near your ribs.
Curl the weights upward by bending your elbows until your hands reach shoulder height.
Pause briefly at the top without letting your elbows drift forward.
Lower the weights back down with control until your arms are fully straightened at your sides.
commonMistakes: Swinging the torso to lift the weights
Letting the elbows drift forward at the top
Dropping the weights quickly on the way down
Bending the wrists back instead of keeping them neutral
breathingInstructions: Exhale as you curl the weights up, and inhale as you lower them back down under control.

name: Wide Grip Cable Lat Pulldown

Lean back slightly, brace your core, and retract your shoulder blades.
Pull the bar down to your upper chest, driving elbows down and out.
Pause briefly, then slowly release the bar back to the starting position.

Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

instructions: Adjust the seat height and footrests to a comfortable position
Grasp the handles with an overhand grip, palms facing down
Sit up straight with your feet flat on the footrests
Extend your arms straight out in front of you, keeping your elbows slightly bent
Engage your triceps and push the handles down towards your thighs
Pause for a moment at the bottom, then slowly return to the starting position
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
breathingInstructions: Exhale on effort, inhale on recovery.

name: Ski step
description: ski step targets the Full Body using No Equipment.
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart
Bend your knees slightly and keep your back straight
Jump to the right, landing on your right foot while swinging your left leg behind your right leg
Immediately jump to the left, landing on your left foot while swinging your right leg behind your left leg
Continue alternating jumps from side to side, mimicking a skiing motion
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
breathingInstructions: Exhale on effort, inhale on recovery.

name: Skin the cat
description: skin the cat targets the Back using No Equipment.
instructions: Start by hanging from a bar with your arms fully extended and your body relaxed
Engage your core and lift your legs up, bringing your knees towards your chest
Continue to lift your legs up and over your head, allowing your body to pass through the arms
Once your legs are fully extended over your head, begin to lower them back down towards the starting position
As you lower your legs, allow your body to pass back through the arms until you are hanging with your arms fully extended again
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
breathingInstructions: Exhale on effort, inhale on recovery.

name: Sled 45 degrees one leg press

Sit on the sled machine with your back against the pad and your feet on the footplate
Place one foot on the footplate and extend your leg, pushing the sled away from you
Slowly bend your knee and lower the sled back to the starting position
Repeat with the other leg
Continue alternating legs for the desired number of repetitions.
breathingInstructions: Exhale on effort, inhale on recovery.

Pause for a moment at the top, then slowly lower the sled platform back to the starting position
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

Grasp the barbell with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart
Step back and position the barbell on your front shoulders, resting it on your collarbone and deltoids
Keep your chest up, back straight, and core engaged
Lower your body by bending at the knees and hips, as if sitting back into a chair
Continue lowering until your thighs are parallel to the ground or slightly below
Pause for a moment, then push through your heels to return to the starting position
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
breathingInstructions: Exhale on effort, inhale on recovery.

Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, toes slightly turned out
Step under the bar and position it across your upper back, resting on your traps
Grip the bar with your hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart
Unrack the bar and take a step back, maintaining a stable stance

Lower your body until your thighs are parallel to the ground, or as low as your flexibility allows
Pause for a moment at the bottom, then drive through your heels to return to the starting position
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
breathingInstructions: Exhale on effort, inhale on recovery.

name: Smith hack squat

Position yourself under the barbell, resting it on your upper traps and shoulders
Grasp the barbell with an overhand grip, slightly wider than shoulder-width apart
Engage your core and keep your chest up as you unrack the barbell
Take a step back and position your feet slightly wider than shoulder-width apart
Bend your knees and lower your body down, keeping your chest up and back straight
Continue descending until your thighs are parallel to the ground or slightly below
Pause for a moment at the bottom, then push through your heels to return to the starting position
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
breathingInstructions: Exhale on effort, inhale on recovery.

name: 90/90 Hold
description: A seated hip mobility hold: both knees are bent to about 90 degrees, one leg in front of you and turned out, the other out to the side and turned in. Holding the position with your trunk upright stretches the outer hip of the front leg and the front of the hip of the back leg.
instructions: Sit on the floor and bend your front leg in front of you so your shin runs across your body and your knee is bent to about 90 degrees.
Place your back leg out to the side with that knee also bent to about 90 degrees, shin pointing back.
Put your hands on the floor beside your hips for support.
Sit up tall, with your chest lifted and both sitting bones as close to the floor as you can manage.
Hold the position, breathing slowly, feeling the stretch in the outer hip of the front leg and the front of the hip of the back leg.
Hold for the planned time, then switch the legs and hold on the other side.
formCues: Keep the trunk upright; slumping takes the stretch out of the hips.
If the hips are tight, keep more weight on your hands or sit on a folded towel until you can sit taller.
Ease into the stretch and do not force the knees down; the position should feel strong, not painful.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: 90/90 Switch
description: A hip-mobility drill in which you sit with both knees bent at right angles and rotate your legs from one side to the other, keeping the 90/90 position on each side. It trains the internal and external rotation of both hips as you switch.
instructions: Sit on the floor with the front knee bent at 90 degrees and the back knee bent at 90 degrees, and place your hands behind you for support.
Sit tall and keep your trunk upright.
Lift both knees slightly and rotate your legs to the other side in a controlled movement, so that the front leg becomes the back leg.
Settle into the 90/90 position on the new side, using your hands for balance.
Switch back to the first side, and repeat for the planned repetitions.
Keep the movement slow and smooth, without forcing the hips.
formCues: Keep your trunk tall; leaning back too far takes the work out of the hips.
Do the 90/90 hold first if you cannot reach the position on both sides.
Move slowly and stop if you feel pinching in the hip or pain in the knee.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Ab Wheel Rollout
description: A core exercise rolling a wheel forward and back, training anti-extension of the spine.
instructions: Kneel on the floor and grip the ab wheel handles shoulder-width.
Brace the core hard so the lower back stays neutral.
Roll the wheel slowly forward, extending the body as far as you can control.
Stop before the hips sag or the back arches.
Pull the wheel back to the knees by contracting the abs.
formCues: Brace the core before each rep — do not let the lower back arch.
Build range gradually, stopping short of any hip sag.
Drop to a wall stop if you cannot control the bottom.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Archer Pull Ups
description: A unilateral pull-up shifting the body toward one hand while the other arm stays straight, building single-arm pulling strength.
instructions: Grip the bar wider than shoulder width with palms facing away.
Pull yourself up while shifting your body toward one hand.
Keep the opposite arm straight as a support.
Lower yourself under control back to the hang.
Alternate sides each rep or complete reps on one side first.
formCues: Keep the straight arm fully extended and use it only as a guide.
Pull your chin toward the working hand, not straight up.
Master wide-grip pull-ups before progressing to archers.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Archer Push Ups
description: A wide push-up lowering toward one hand while the opposite arm stays straight, loading one side at a time.
instructions: Set up in a wide push-up position with arms straight.
Lower yourself toward one hand while keeping the other arm straight.
Keep your core tight and body in a straight line.
Press back up to the start position.
Alternate sides each rep for the desired number of reps.
formCues: Keep your hips square to the floor as you shift sideways.
Let the straight arm assist as little as possible.
Start from wide push-ups and shift a little further each session.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Arnold Press
description: An overhead press variation rotating the palms from facing the body to facing forward, working the front and side deltoids.
instructions: Hold a pair of dumbbells at shoulder height with palms facing you.
Press the dumbbells overhead while rotating your palms to face forward.
Fully extend your arms at the top without locking the elbows.
Reverse the motion and rotate back to the start.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
formCues: Time the palm rotation evenly throughout the press, not all at once.
Avoid arching your lower back as the weight goes overhead.
Use a lighter load than a standard press to control the rotation.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Machine Assisted Dips
description: A beginner-friendly dip performed on an assisted machine that offsets body weight, training the chest and triceps.
instructions: Step onto the assisted dip machine with knees on the pad.
Grip the parallel bars and support your weight with straight arms.
Lower your body by bending your elbows until shoulders are below elbows.
Press back up to the start position.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
formCues: Keep your elbows tracking back rather than flaring out wide.
Stop the descent if you feel pinching in the shoulders.
Reduce the assistance gradually as pressing strength improves.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Assisted Pull Ups
description: A machine-assisted pull-up reducing the effective body weight, allowing beginners to train the lats through a full range.
instructions: Place your knees on the assisted pull-up machine pad.
Grip the bar with palms facing away, slightly wider than shoulders.
Pull your chest toward the bar by driving your elbows down.
Lower yourself under control to a full hang.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
formCues: Pull your shoulder blades down before bending your arms.
Avoid swinging or using momentum from the knee pad.
Decrease the assistance over time to progress toward unassisted reps.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Back Extension
description: An isolation movement targeting the lower back erector spinae on a hyperextension bench.
instructions: Lie face down on a hyperextension bench with hips at the pad edge.
Lower your upper body toward the floor.
Raise your torso back up until your body is straight.
Repeat.
formCues: Do not hyperextend beyond neutral spine.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Balance Dome Crunch
description: A crunch done lying with your lower back on the domed side of a balance dome. The dome lets you start the curl from a slightly extended position, which lengthens the abdominals, and its instability makes the trunk work to keep you steady.
instructions: Place the balance dome on the floor with the domed side up and sit on it, then lie back so your lower back rests on the dome.
Bend your knees and place your feet flat on the floor, about hip-width apart.
Put your hands behind your head with your elbows wide, without pulling on your neck.
Curl your shoulders and upper back up toward your hips by shortening the distance between your ribs and your pelvis.
Pause briefly at the top and keep your lower back on the dome.
Lower back slowly to the start and repeat for the planned repetitions.
formCues: Lead with the ribcage rather than the head; your hands only support your head.
Do not let the dome roll away; keep your feet planted and your hips still.
Start with a small range and extend further back over the dome as your control improves.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Balance Dome Glute Bridge
alternativeNames: Puente de Glúteos sobre Domo de Equilibrio
description: A glute bridge with both feet on a balance dome: lying on your back with your heels or soles on the domed top, you lift your hips until your body is straight from shoulders to knees. The unstable surface makes the glutes and hamstrings work harder to keep the hips level.
instructions: Lie on your back on the floor with your knees bent and place both feet on the top of a balance dome with the domed side up.
Rest your arms flat on the floor beside you with your palms down.
Brace your trunk and press through your feet to lift your hips off the floor.
Raise your hips until your body forms a straight line from your shoulders to your knees.
Squeeze your glutes at the top and keep your hips level while the dome moves under your feet.
Lower your hips slowly to the floor and repeat for the planned repetitions.
formCues: Press your whole foot into the dome rather than only the heel, which keeps the surface steadier.
Do not arch your lower back at the top; finish the lift with your glutes.
Master the floor glute bridge first and move your feet closer to the dome only when you can keep your hips level.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Balance Dome Plank
description: A forearm plank with the elbows on a balance dome. The unstable surface makes the shoulders and the whole trunk work harder to keep the body in a straight line from head to heels.
instructions: Place the balance dome on a flat floor with the domed side up and kneel behind it.
Put your forearms on the dome with your elbows under your shoulders.
Step your feet back into a plank with your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Squeeze your glutes and brace your abdominals, keeping your neck long.
Hold the position for the planned time while the dome moves under you.
Lower your knees to the floor to finish.
formCues: Do not let your hips sag or pike up; a straight line from head to heels is the target.
Press your forearms into the dome and keep your shoulders away from your ears.
Make it easier by widening your feet, or harder by bringing them closer together.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Balance Dome Push-Up
description: A push-up with the hands on a balance dome turned flat side up. The dome tilts under your hands, so the chest, shoulders and triceps press you up while the shoulder stabilisers and the trunk keep you steady.
instructions: Turn the balance dome over so that its flat platform faces up, and place your hands on the platform at about shoulder-width.
Step your feet back into a high plank with your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Brace your trunk and lower your chest toward the platform by bending your elbows.
Lower until your chest is just above the platform, keeping your elbows about 45 degrees from your body.
Press the platform away to straighten your arms, keeping the dome as level as you can.
Repeat for the planned repetitions.
formCues: Do plain push-ups first; the dome adds instability to a movement you should already control.
Keep your hips level and do not let the dome tilt to one side; look slightly ahead of your hands.
Place the dome on a non-slip floor and make sure the platform is flat before you put your weight on it.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Balance Dome Single-Leg Stand
alternativeNames: Equilibrio a Una Pierna sobre Domo de Equilibrio
description: A balance hold on one leg on a balance dome, with the other knee lifted in front of you. The ankle, calf and hip muscles of the standing leg constantly adjust to the tilting surface, which makes it a demanding balance and rehabilitation exercise.
instructions: Place the balance dome on a flat floor with the domed side up, next to a wall or a sturdy support.
Step onto the middle of the dome with one foot and stand tall with your knee slightly bent.
Shift your weight onto that leg and lift the other knee in front of you until the thigh is about hip height.
Keep your hips level, your chest tall and your eyes on a fixed point ahead.
Hold for the planned time, letting your ankle and calf make small corrections.
Lower the foot, rest and repeat on the other leg.
formCues: Learn the two-foot balance dome stand first and keep a wall within reach.
Press the whole foot into the dome and let your toes spread; do not grip the surface with them.
Do not look down at your feet; a fixed point ahead helps your balance.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Balance Dome Squat
description: A bodyweight squat done standing on the domed side of a balance dome. The surface moves under your feet, so the quadriceps and glutes lower and lift the body while the ankles and trunk work to keep you balanced.
instructions: Place the balance dome on a flat floor with the domed side up and step onto the middle of it with both feet, about hip-width apart.
Find your balance and reach your arms straight out in front of you.
Push your hips back and bend your knees, lowering until your thighs are close to parallel with the floor.
Keep your chest up and your knees in line with your toes.
Press through your whole foot to stand back up.
Repeat for the planned repetitions and step off one foot at a time.
formCues: Do the balance dome stand and squat hold first; the moving squat adds change of position to an unstable surface.
Keep your weight spread over the whole foot; heels lifting or knees caving inward are signs the surface is too hard for now.
Hold a wall or a rack with one hand until the movement feels steady.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Balance Dome Squat Hold
alternativeNames: Sentadilla Isométrica sobre Domo de Equilibrio
description: A static squat held on a balance dome: you stand on the domed top and lower into a partial squat with your arms reaching forward, then stay there while the unstable surface keeps shifting. The quadriceps and glutes hold the position and the ankles and trunk work to keep you balanced.
instructions: Place the balance dome on a flat floor with the domed side up and step onto the middle of it with both feet, about hip-width apart.
Stand tall and find your balance before you start to squat.
Push your hips back and bend your knees until your thighs are close to parallel with the floor.
Reach your arms straight out in front of you to counterbalance and keep your chest up.
Hold the position for the planned time, keeping your knees in line with your toes.
Stand up slowly and step off one foot at a time.
formCues: Master the plain balance dome stand first; the squat adds load to an unstable surface.
Spread your weight across the whole foot and do not let your heels lift or your knees cave inward.
Hold a wall or a rack with one hand while you learn the position.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Balance Dome Stand
description: A balance hold on a balance dome, the half-sphere trainer with a flat base: you stand on its domed top with both feet and keep your body steady while the surface moves under you. The calves and the small muscles around the ankles work constantly to hold you upright.
instructions: Place the balance dome on a flat floor with the domed side up and stand next to it.
Step onto the middle of the dome with one foot, then bring the other foot up beside it, about hip-width apart.
Stand tall with your arms relaxed at your sides and your knees slightly bent.
Keep your weight even across both feet and look at a point straight ahead.
Hold the position for the planned time, letting your ankles and calves make small corrections.
Step off one foot at a time to finish.
formCues: Stand next to a wall or a sturdy support the first few times so you can steady yourself.
Grip the dome with the whole foot and keep your toes relaxed; clenching them makes the balance harder.
Do not stare at your feet; a fixed point ahead of you helps your balance.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Balance Dome Step-Up
description: A single-leg step-up onto a balance dome: you place one foot on the domed top, stand up on it and then step back down. The surface tilts under your foot, so the quadriceps and glutes lift the body while the hips and ankle work to keep you steady.
instructions: Stand facing the balance dome, placed domed side up on a flat floor.
Place one foot flat in the middle of the dome.
Press through the whole foot and straighten that leg to stand up on the dome, bringing your other foot beside it.
Stand tall for a moment and keep your weight centred over the dome.
Step back down with the other foot first, then the working foot.
Complete the planned repetitions on one leg, then switch legs.
formCues: Put your foot in the middle of the dome; stepping near the edge makes it tip.
Push through the heel and the whole foot rather than hopping up from the back leg.
Hold a wall or a rack with one hand until you can step up and down smoothly.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Ball Pike
description: An advanced core exercise where the hips pike up while the feet roll a stability ball toward the chest.
instructions: Place the shins on a stability ball and hands on the floor in a high plank.
Brace the core and keep the legs straight.
Pike the hips up, rolling the ball toward the chest as the body forms an inverted V.
Pause briefly at the top.
Roll the ball back out to the starting plank.
formCues: Keep the legs straight throughout — no knee bend.
Move at the hips, not the lower back.
Build up with knee tucks first if the pike is too hard.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Band Assisted Pull Ups
description: A pull-up variation using a resistance band for assistance, reducing the load to build toward unassisted reps.
instructions: Loop a resistance band over the pull-up bar and step one foot into it.
Grip the bar with palms facing away, shoulder-width apart.
Pull your chest toward the bar by driving your elbows down.
Lower yourself under control to a full hang.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
formCues: Avoid letting the band's recoil bounce you out of the bottom.
Keep the banded foot steady so the band cannot slip off.
Progress to thinner bands as your pulling strength increases.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Band Pull Apart
description: A high-volume rear delt and scapular retractor exercise performed by pulling a resistance band apart at shoulder height.
instructions: Stand holding a light resistance band with both hands, arms extended straight in front at shoulder height.
Hands start shoulder-width apart, palms facing down.
Keeping arms straight, pull the band apart by driving the hands out to the sides.
Finish with the band touching your chest and the shoulder blades squeezed together.
Return slowly to the starting position and repeat.
formCues: Lead the movement with the little fingers — this externally rotates the shoulders.
Use a band light enough to do 15–30 clean reps; this is a high-rep prehab exercise.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Band Shoulder External Rotation
alternativeNames: Rotación Externa de Hombro con Banda
description: A rotator cuff exercise with a resistance band. With your elbow tucked against your side and bent to a right angle, you rotate your forearm outward against the pull of the band and then return slowly. It strengthens the small muscles at the back of the shoulder that turn the arm outward and keep the joint steady.
instructions: Anchor a resistance band at about elbow height and stand sideways to it, so that the arm you are training is on the side away from the anchor.
Hold the band in that hand, bend your elbow to 90 degrees and tuck it against your side; a small folded towel between elbow and ribs helps keep it there.
Start with your forearm pointing across your stomach and the band under light tension.
Rotate your forearm outward, away from your body and the anchor, keeping your elbow fixed at your side and your wrist straight.
Pause when your forearm points slightly outward, without leaning or twisting your trunk.
Return slowly to the start against the band, repeat for the planned repetitions, and then switch arms.
formCues: Use a light band and slow repetitions; these small muscles tire quickly.
Keep your elbow pinned to your side; if it drifts away, the larger shoulder muscles take over from the rotator cuff.
Stop if you feel a pinch at the front of the shoulder and keep the movement pain-free.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Banded Adductor Stretch
description: A lying stretch that uses a band to guide one straight leg out to the side and lengthen the inner thigh.
instructions: Lie on your back with a band looped around one foot.
Raise that leg and let it open out to the side.
Hold the band to control how far the leg lowers.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
Switch sides and repeat.
formCues: Keep your hips flat and both glutes on the floor.
Stretch to mild tension, never to pain.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Banded Ankle Stretch
description: A seated stretch that uses a band around the forefoot to flex the ankle and lengthen the calf.
instructions: Sit with one leg extended and a band around the forefoot.
Hold the band in both hands.
Pull so the toes draw back toward your shin.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
Switch sides and repeat.
formCues: Keep the leg straight and relaxed.
Stretch to mild tension, never to pain.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Banded Calf Stretch
description: A lying stretch that uses a band around the ball of the foot to flex the ankle and lengthen the calf.
instructions: Lie on your back and loop a band around the ball of one foot.
Raise the leg and keep it fairly straight.
Pull the band so your toes draw back toward your shin.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
Switch sides and repeat.
formCues: Keep the pull steady, not jerky.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Banded Chest Stretch
description: A standing stretch that opens the chest by holding a band behind the back and drawing the arms apart.
instructions: Hold a band behind your back with both hands.
Straighten your arms and draw them apart.
Lift your chest and squeeze your shoulder blades.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
formCues: Keep your shoulders down away from your ears.
Stretch to mild tension, never to pain.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Banded Clamshell
description: A clamshell hip-abduction performed with a loop band wrapped above the knees. The band adds constant tension on the gluteus medius — a small, focused isolation drill for hip stability.
instructions: Lie on your side with hips and knees bent to roughly 45 degrees, feet stacked.
Place a loop band around both legs above the knees.
Keep the feet pressed together and the pelvis stable — do not roll back as you move.
Open the top knee upward against the band, like a clamshell opening, until you feel the glute fire.
Pause briefly at the top, then lower under control to the start.
Complete all reps on one side, then switch.
formCues: The pelvis stays stacked — the moment you start rocking back, the glute disengages.
Slow controlled tempo beats heavy band; this is a stability drill, not a strength PR.
If you cramp in the side of the hip, that is exactly the right muscle. Shorten the set.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Banded Figure-4 Stretch
description: A lying glute stretch in a figure-4 position, using a band to draw both legs toward the chest.
instructions: Lie on your back and cross one ankle over the opposite thigh.
Loop a band around the supporting thigh.
Pull both legs toward your chest with the band.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
Switch sides and repeat.
formCues: Keep your head and shoulders relaxed on the floor.
Let the crossed knee fall open.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Banded Fire Hydrant
description: This isolation exercise uses a loop band to target and strengthen the gluteus medius and maximus, improving hip abduction and stability.
instructions: Place a loop band just above your knees and assume a quadruped position with hands under shoulders and knees under hips.
Keep your core engaged and back flat, maintaining a neutral spine throughout the movement.
Slowly lift one knee out to the side, keeping the knee bent at 90 degrees, until your thigh is parallel to the floor.
Hold briefly at the top, squeezing your glute, then slowly lower your leg back to the starting position with control.
Complete all repetitions on one side before switching to the other side.
formCues: Focus on controlled movement; avoid using momentum to lift your leg.
Keep your hips stable and prevent your torso from rotating or leaning.
Ensure the band stays taut throughout the entire range of motion.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Banded Glute Bridge
description: A glute bridge with a loop band placed above the knees. Driving the knees out against the band recruits the gluteus medius alongside the prime glute-max bridge — a cheap accessory that doubles as hip activation.
instructions: Lie on your back with the knees bent and feet flat on the floor, shoulder-width apart.
Place a loop band around both legs just above the knees.
Press the lower back into the floor and brace the core.
Drive through the heels and squeeze the glutes to lift the hips into a bridge — keep the band tension by pushing the knees outward.
At the top, the body forms a straight line from shoulders to knees. Pause briefly.
Lower under control to the start and repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.
formCues: The knees want to cave inward — that is the band telling you to push them out.
Stop the lift when your hips are level with your shoulders and knees; do not hyperextend the lower back.
Squeeze hard at the top — a fast, half-rep bridge feels easy because it is.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Banded Good Morning
description: A hip-hinge with a loop band over the upper back, targeting the hamstrings and glutes.
instructions: Stand on a loop band with both feet and pass it over the back of your neck.
Set feet hip-width with a soft bend in the knees.
Hinge at the hips, pushing them back with a flat back.
Lower until you feel a stretch in the hamstrings.
Drive the hips forward to return to standing.
formCues: Move from the hips, not the lower back.
Keep the chest up and the back flat throughout.
Use a band light enough to allow full range of motion.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Banded Hamstring Stretch
description: A lying stretch that uses a band around the foot to draw a straight leg toward the torso and lengthen the hamstring.
instructions: Lie on your back and loop a band around one foot.
Raise that leg straight up, holding the band in both hands.
Gently pull the band to draw the leg toward you.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
Switch sides and repeat.
formCues: Keep the raised leg as straight as you can.
Keep the other leg flat on the floor.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Banded Hip Thrust
description: This exercise uses a loop band to increase glute activation during a hip thrust, effectively targeting the gluteus maximus, hamstrings, and gluteus medius for improved lower body strength.
instructions: Place a loop band just above your knees and sit on the floor with your upper back against a bench.
Bend your knees, plant your feet hip-width apart, and position the band to create tension.
Drive through your heels, extend your hips, and lift your glutes off the floor until your body forms a straight line from shoulders to knees.
Squeeze your glutes forcefully at the top, ensuring your knees are pushed out against the band.
Slowly lower your hips back to the starting position with control.
formCues: Maintain constant tension on the band throughout the movement.
Focus on a strong glute contraction at the peak of the thrust.
Keep your chin tucked and gaze forward to maintain a neutral spine.
Ensure your shins are vertical at the top of the movement.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Banded IT-Band Stretch
alternativeNames: Estiramiento de Banda Iliotibial con Banda
description: A lying stretch that uses a band to draw one leg across the body and target the outer thigh and hip.
instructions: Lie on your back with a band around one raised foot.
Hold the band with the opposite hand.
Draw the straight leg across your body toward the floor.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
Switch sides and repeat.
formCues: Keep both shoulders down on the floor.
Stop when you feel a stretch along the outer thigh.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Banded Kneeling Hip Thrust
alternativeNames: Empuje de Cadera Arrodillado con Banda
description: This exercise strengthens the glutes and hamstrings by driving the hips forward against band resistance from a kneeling position.
instructions: Anchor a band low on a sturdy post, at the height of your hips when kneeling, and loop it around your hips. Kneel facing away from the post, torso upright and knees hip-width apart, far enough forward that the band is taut.
Sit your hips back toward your heels, leaning slightly forward with your back straight and core braced.
Initiate the movement by squeezing your glutes, driving your hips forward until your torso is upright.
Squeeze your glutes hard at the top, maintaining tension on the band.
Slowly reverse the movement, controlling the band's resistance as you return to the starting position.
formCues: Focus on a strong glute contraction at the top of the movement.
Keep your core engaged throughout to prevent arching your lower back.
Kneel far enough from the post that the band stays taut even at the bottom.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Banded Lat Stretch
description: A standing stretch that lengthens the lats by hinging forward while holding a band overhead under tension.
instructions: Hold a band overhead with both hands under light tension.
Hinge forward at the hips with your arms reaching ahead.
Let your chest sink to lengthen the sides of your back.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
formCues: Keep your arms straight and shoulders relaxed.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Banded Lateral Walk
description: A side-stepping movement performed with a loop band wrapped above the knees or around the ankles. Constant abduction tension fires the gluteus medius — a staple warm-up and rehab drill for hip stability.
instructions: Place a loop band around the legs above the knees (or around the ankles for a harder version).
Stand in a quarter-squat: feet shoulder-width, hips back, chest up, knees tracking over the toes.
Step one foot directly out to the side against the band tension.
Bring the trailing foot in toward the lead — keep tension on the band the entire time, do not let the feet snap together.
Continue side-stepping in one direction for the prescribed reps or distance, then reverse.
Stay low throughout; do not pop up between steps.
formCues: Keep the toes pointing straight forward — do not let the lead foot turn out.
Hips stay level; do not rock side-to-side as you step.
If the knees cave inward, the band is too strong — drop to a lighter one.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Banded Overhead Press
alternativeNames: Press por Encima de la Cabeza con Banda
description: A standing overhead press with a resistance band under your feet. You hold the band at shoulder height and press your hands overhead until your arms are straight, against the growing tension of the band. It trains the shoulders and the triceps without weights.
instructions: Stand on the middle of a resistance band with your feet about hip-width apart.
Hold the ends of the band at shoulder height with your palms facing forward and your elbows bent.
Brace your trunk and squeeze your glutes to keep your ribs down.
Press your hands straight up overhead until your arms are fully extended.
Pause briefly at the top, then lower your hands back to your shoulders under control.
Complete the planned repetitions.
formCues: Choose a band that lets you finish the set with a steady press and without arching your back.
Press in a straight line close to your face and finish with your arms next to your ears.
Wrap the ends of the band around your hands for more tension, or use a lighter band to make it easier.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Banded Pallof Press
description: An anti-rotation core exercise with a resistance band anchored beside you at chest height. You hold the band at your chest, press your hands straight out in front of you and resist the pull of the band that tries to turn your trunk, then bring your hands back. The abdominal muscles and obliques work to keep your body still.
instructions: Anchor a resistance band at chest height and stand sideways to it with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding the band with both hands at the centre of your chest.
Step away from the anchor until the band is under tension, with your knees slightly bent and your hips and shoulders facing forward.
Press your hands straight out in front of your chest until your arms are fully extended, without letting your trunk turn toward the anchor.
Hold for a moment with your body completely still.
Bring your hands back to your chest under control.
Complete the planned repetitions, then turn around and repeat on the other side.
formCues: The work is in keeping your torso still, not in the press itself; use a lighter band if your hips or shoulders twist.
Stand tall with your ribs down and your glutes lightly squeezed.
Step further from the anchor or use a thicker band to make it harder.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Banded Push-Up
description: A push-up with a resistance band stretched across your upper back and held under your hands. The band adds resistance that grows as you press up, so the top of the movement becomes the hardest part. It trains the chest, the front of the shoulders and the triceps.
instructions: Place a resistance band across your upper back, just below your neck, and hold each end under the palm of the same hand on the floor.
Start in a high plank with your hands slightly wider than your shoulders and your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Lower your chest toward the floor by bending your elbows, keeping them at about 45 degrees to your body.
Press the floor away and straighten your arms against the pull of the band until you are back in the plank.
Keep your core tight and your hips level during the whole repetition.
Complete the planned repetitions, or drop to your knees if you cannot keep your body in one line.
formCues: Start with a lighter band; its tension grows toward the top of the press, where a push-up is already hardest.
Keep the band across your shoulder blades and off your neck.
Do not let your hips sag or lift; your body should move as one plank.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Banded Rear Delt Stretch
alternativeNames: Estiramiento de Deltoides Posterior con Banda
description: A standing stretch that targets the rear shoulder by pulling one arm across the body against band tension.
instructions: Loop a band around one arm and hold the other end.
Draw that arm horizontally across your chest.
Use the band to deepen the pull gently.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
Switch sides and repeat.
formCues: Keep the working shoulder relaxed and down.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Banded Romanian Deadlift
description: A Romanian deadlift using a loop band, ideal for warm-ups and learning the hip-hinge pattern.
instructions: Stand on a loop band with both feet and grip the top of the band.
Set feet hip-width with a soft bend in the knees.
Hinge at the hips, sliding the hands down the legs.
Lower until you feel a stretch in the hamstrings.
Drive the hips forward to return to standing.
formCues: Keep the band close to the legs throughout.
Stop at the bottom of your clean range — no rounded back.
The movement is a hinge, not a squat — knees barely bend.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Banded Seated Hip Abduction
alternativeNames: Abducción de Cadera Sentado con Banda
description: This isolation exercise targets the gluteus medius and maximus by externally rotating the hips against band resistance while seated.
instructions: Sit on a bench or chair with a loop band around your knees.
Keep your feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart, and maintain an upright posture.
Push your knees outwards against the band, engaging your glutes.
Hold the peak contraction briefly, then slowly return your knees to the starting position.
Control the movement throughout the entire range of motion.
formCues: Focus on squeezing your glutes to initiate the movement.
Avoid leaning back or using momentum; keep your torso stable.
Choose a band resistance that allows for controlled movement.
Maintain tension on the band even in the starting position.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Banded Shoulder Stretch
description: A standing stretch that opens the shoulders and chest by holding a band behind the back, one hand high and one low.
instructions: Hold a band behind your back, one hand high and one low.
Keep light tension in the band.
Open your chest and draw your shoulders gently back.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
formCues: Keep your ribs down and avoid arching your back.
Move your hands farther apart to ease the stretch.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Banded Squat
description: A bodyweight squat with a loop band above the knees to teach knees-out tracking.
instructions: Place a loop band just above the knees.
Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, toes slightly out.
Push the knees out against the band as you squat down.
Descend until thighs are parallel or below.
Drive through the heels to stand back up.
formCues: Push the knees out against the band the whole rep.
Keep the chest up and the back flat.
Do not let the knees collapse inward.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Banded Standing Leg Curl
alternativeNames: Curl de Pierna de Pie con Banda
description: A standing hamstring curl using a loop band anchored around the ankle, useful for travel or as a low-load hamstring finisher.
instructions: Loop a resistance band around one ankle and anchor the other end under your standing foot or a fixed point in front of you.
Stand tall, holding onto something for balance if needed, with a slight bend in the standing knee.
Curl the banded heel up and back toward your glute, keeping the thigh still.
Squeeze the hamstring at the top, then lower under control to a full stretch.
Complete all reps on one side, then switch legs.
formCues: Keep the thigh stationary — only the lower leg should move.
Avoid swinging the hips to generate momentum.
Use a lighter band if you can't control the descent.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Banded Standing Hip Abduction
alternativeNames: Abducción de Cadera de Pie con Banda
description: This isolation exercise targets the gluteus medius and maximus, improving hip stability and strength by abducting the leg against band resistance.
instructions: Place a loop band around your ankles or just above your knees.
Stand tall with a slight bend in your knees and brace your core.
Shift your weight onto one leg, maintaining a stable torso.
Slowly abduct the free leg out to the side, feeling the glute contract.
Control the movement as you return the leg to the starting position.
Complete all reps per side before switching.
formCues: Keep your torso upright and avoid leaning to the side.
Focus on a controlled movement, not momentum.
Ensure the band maintains tension throughout the entire range of motion.
Initiate the movement from your hip, not your foot.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Banded Standing Hip Adduction
alternativeNames: Aducción de Cadera de Pie con Banda
description: A standing hip adduction with a loop band, isolating the inner thigh adductors.
instructions: Anchor a loop band to a sturdy upright at ankle height.
Step into the loop with the working leg facing the anchor side.
Stand a few feet away so the band has tension.
Sweep the working leg across the body toward the standing leg.
Return slowly to the start. Complete reps per side, then switch.
formCues: Keep the standing leg slightly bent for stability.
Move only the working leg — torso stays still.
Control the eccentric for full adductor stretch.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Banded Standing Row
description: A standing row with a resistance band anchored in front of you at about chest height. You pull your elbows back toward your ribs and squeeze your shoulder blades together, then return slowly. It trains the muscles of the upper back and the rear of the shoulders without gym equipment.
instructions: Anchor a resistance band at about chest height, stand facing it with one end in each hand, and step back until the band is under light tension.
Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart and your knees slightly bent, with your arms stretched out in front of you.
Pull your elbows back along your sides and bring your hands toward your lower ribs.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the end of the pull without shrugging.
Slowly stretch your arms forward again, resisting the band.
Complete the planned repetitions.
formCues: Lead with your elbows and keep your shoulders down, away from your ears.
Keep your trunk still; if you lean back to finish the pull, use a lighter band or step closer to the anchor.
Control the return; the slow release is half of the exercise.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Banded Sumo Walk
description: A wide-stance lateral walk with a loop band around the lower legs, targeting the glute medius and maximus.
instructions: Place a loop band around your lower legs, just above the ankles.
Drop into a quarter squat with feet wider than shoulder-width.
Step sideways in a wide stance, keeping tension on the band.
Bring the trailing foot in only partway so the band stays taut, and keep stepping for the prescribed distance before leading with the other leg.
Stay low throughout — do not stand up between steps.
formCues: Keep tension on the band the entire set.
Stay in a quarter-squat — do not stand tall between steps.
Take small, controlled steps with toes pointed slightly out.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Banded Terminal Knee Extension
alternativeNames: Extensión Terminal de Rodilla con Banda
description: An isolation drill that locks out the knee against band resistance, often used for VMO and knee rehab.
instructions: Anchor a loop band to a sturdy upright at knee height.
