Step into the loop so the band sits behind one knee.
Step back so the band pulls the knee into a slight bend.
Extend the knee fully against the band, contracting the quad.
Return slowly. Complete reps per side, then switch.
formCues: Squeeze the quadriceps hard at full extension.
Keep the foot flat — do not lift the heel.
Move only at the knee — the hip stays still.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Banded Triceps Stretch
description: A standing stretch that lengthens the triceps by reaching one hand behind the head against band tension.
instructions: Hold a band that runs down your back, top hand behind your head.
Anchor the lower hand at your lower back.
Reach the top hand down to feel the triceps lengthen.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
Switch sides and repeat.
formCues: Keep your head upright and ribs down.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Barbell Ab Rollout
description: A kneeling ab rollout using a loaded barbell with plates, giving smoother rolling and adjustable load compared to an ab wheel.
instructions: Load plates of equal size on both ends of a barbell and place it on the floor.
Kneel behind the bar and grip it shoulder-width, arms extended.
Brace the core hard, then roll the bar forward away from your body.
Go as far as you can keep a neutral spine — stop before the hips sag.
Pull the bar back to the starting position by contracting the abs and lats.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.
formCues: Start with small plates for a limited range; graduate to 45s for full rollouts.
The moment the lower back arches or drops, stop — you've exceeded your range.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Barbell Box Squat
description: A back squat with a barbell in which you sit back onto a box or bench at the bottom, pause for a moment and stand up again. The box fixes the depth and teaches you to sit back into the hips, and the brief pause removes the rebound out of the bottom.
instructions: Set a box or bench behind you at a height where your thighs end up about parallel to the floor when you sit on it.
Take the barbell on your upper back, step back and stand with your feet a little wider than shoulder-width.
Brace your trunk and push your hips back, then lower yourself under control toward the box.
Sit onto the box without dropping onto it, keeping your chest up and your shins close to vertical.
Pause briefly with your muscles still tight, without relaxing your back.
Drive through your whole foot to stand up, and repeat for the planned repetitions.
formCues: Sit back rather than down; the box should be touched with your hips, not rested on with your weight.
Keep the torso tight in the pause; relaxing on the box is where most back injuries happen.
Use a box that cannot slide, and lower it as you progress until you can squat to full depth.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Barbell Bulgarian Split Squat
description: A single-leg squat with the rear foot raised on a bench and a barbell held across the upper back. The heavy, unilateral load works the quadriceps and glutes of the front leg and challenges balance and hip mobility.
instructions: Set a barbell across the upper back and stand about two feet in front of a flat bench, facing away from it.
Place the top of one foot on the bench behind you, with the front foot far enough forward to keep the shin close to vertical when you lower.
Brace the trunk and lower the back knee toward the floor by bending the front hip and knee.
Descend until the front thigh is about parallel to the floor, keeping the chest up.
Drive through the middle of the front foot to return to the start.
Complete the repetitions on one leg, then switch.
formCues: Keep most of the weight on the front leg; the back foot is only there for balance.
Keep the front knee tracking over the toes and the torso upright.
Use a lighter load than in a regular back squat, and set up the bar and a safe way to drop it before you step into position.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Barbell Calf Raise
description: A standing calf raise loaded with a barbell across the upper back, using a raised platform for a deeper heel stretch.
instructions: Place a barbell across your upper back as in a squat.
Stand with the balls of your feet on a raised platform.
Push up onto your toes as high as possible.
Pause and squeeze your calves at the top.
Lower your heels below the platform and repeat.
formCues: Avoid bouncing out of the bottom stretch position.
Keep your knees straight but not locked throughout the set.
Move slowly to stay balanced under the bar.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Barbell Isometric Squat Hold
description: An isometric version of the barbell back squat: you squat down with the bar on your upper back and hold the bottom position. The quadriceps, glutes and the muscles that keep your back rigid stay under tension at the deepest, hardest point of the squat.
instructions: Set the bar on your upper back, grip it just outside your shoulders and step back from the rack with your feet about shoulder-width apart.
Take a big breath into your belly, brace your core and keep your chest tall.
Sit down and back until your thighs are about parallel to the floor or a little below, with your knees tracking over your toes.
Stop at the bottom and hold the position, with your weight over the middle of your feet.
Keep your back flat and your knees pushed out while you hold for the planned time.
Drive up through your feet to stand, then rack the bar.
formCues: Use safety arms or pins set just below your bottom position, since a long hold at depth is tiring.
Choose a lighter bar than your working squat weight; holding for time is harder than it looks.
Keep the knees pushed out over the toes instead of letting them collapse inward as you tire.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Barbell Overhead Extension
alternativeNames: Extensión de Barra por Encima de la Cabeza
description: This isolation exercise effectively targets the triceps brachii by extending the elbows overhead, promoting muscle hypertrophy and strength.
instructions: Load a barbell with an appropriate weight and stand or sit with a neutral spine.
Grip the barbell with an overhand, shoulder-width grip, and press it overhead.
Slowly lower the barbell behind your head by flexing your elbows, keeping your upper arms stable.
Extend your elbows to press the barbell back to the starting overhead position, squeezing your triceps.
Maintain control throughout the movement, avoiding momentum.
formCues: Keep your elbows tucked in and pointing forward to maximize triceps engagement and protect your shoulders.
Control the eccentric (lowering) phase to enhance muscle tension and growth.
Avoid arching your lower back excessively; brace your core to maintain stability.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Barbell Reverse Lunge
description: A barbell lunge stepping backward instead of forward, keeping the front shin vertical while loading the quads and glutes.
instructions: Place a barbell across your upper back and stand tall.
Step one foot backward into a long stride.
Lower your back knee toward the ground under control.
Drive through your front heel to return to standing.
Complete reps on one side, then switch.
formCues: Step back far enough to keep your front shin close to vertical.
Lower the back knee straight down rather than leaning forward.
Keep your chest tall and hips square throughout.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Bent-Over Barbell Row
description: A compound pulling movement that targets the upper and middle back.
instructions: Hinge at the hips with a slight knee bend.
Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Pull the bar to your lower chest, squeezing your shoulder blades.
Lower the bar under control.
Repeat.
formCues: Keep your torso at roughly 45 degrees.
Do not use momentum to swing the weight.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Barbell Zercher Hold
description: A standing hold with a barbell cradled in the crooks of your elbows against your abdomen. The abs and the trunk stabilizers resist the pull of the bar, while the biceps and the upper back keep it close to your body.
instructions: Set a barbell on a rack at about the height of your lower ribs and place the crooks of your elbows under the bar.
Fold your arms and clasp your hands together in front of your chest to lock the bar against your body.
Lift the bar off the rack and step back, standing with your feet about shoulder-width apart.
Stand tall, brace your abs and keep your ribs down, so that the bar rests against your abdomen without pulling you forward.
Hold the position for the planned time, breathing slowly and keeping your elbows pressed together.
Return the bar to the rack, or lower it to the floor with control.
formCues: Wrap a towel or a barbell pad around the bar, since it presses into the elbows and the abdomen.
Keep the bar close to your body and do not lean back to carry it; if you do, the weight is too heavy.
Start with a bar a little lighter than your Zercher squat load, since the bar rests on your arms for the whole hold.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Barbell Zercher Squat Hold
description: An isometric version of the Zercher squat: you squat down with the barbell in the crooks of your elbows and hold the bottom position. The quadriceps, glutes and the trunk stay under tension at the deepest point, while the arms and upper back keep the bar close to you.
instructions: Set a barbell on a rack at about the height of your lower ribs, place the crooks of your elbows under the bar and clasp your hands in front of your chest.
Lift the bar off the rack, step back and stand with your feet about shoulder-width apart.
Brace your abs and keep your chest tall, then sit down and back until your thighs are about parallel to the floor.
Stop at the bottom and hold, with your elbows resting inside your knees and your knees pushed out over your toes.
Keep the bar close to your abdomen and your back straight while you hold for the planned time.
Drive up through your feet to stand and return the bar to the rack.
formCues: Wrap a towel or a barbell pad around the bar, since it presses into the elbows and the abdomen.
Use safety pins set just below your bottom position, since a long hold at depth is tiring.
Keep the chest tall; if the bar pulls you forward and your back rounds, the weight is too heavy.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Battle Rope Double Slam
alternativeNames: Golpe Doble con Cuerdas de Batalla
description: A conditioning movement in which both rope ends are driven up and slammed down together, producing one large wave per rep instead of the alternating waves of the standard battle rope drill.
instructions: Take one rope end in each hand and face the anchor, standing far enough back that the ropes have a slight slack.
Set your feet slightly wider than your hips and sit into a quarter squat with your chest up.
Swing both arms up together, letting the ropes rise in front of you as you extend through the hips.
Slam both ends down to the floor at the same time, hinging at the hips and driving through your lats.
Ride the rebound straight back into the next slam, keeping both arms moving in unison rather than alternating.
Keep slamming for the desired time or number of reps.
formCues: Both arms move together — the moment they start alternating you are doing the standard wave drill, which is a different exercise.
Drive the slam with your hips and lats rather than your arms, or your shoulders will burn out long before your lungs do.
Stand at the right distance from the anchor: too close and the rope goes slack, too far and you cannot get a wave into it at all.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Battle Ropes
description: A high-intensity conditioning movement using thick ropes, training the upper back, shoulders, and grip.
instructions: Anchor the ropes to a fixed point and grab one end in each hand.
Step back so the ropes have moderate slack.
Drop into a quarter squat with feet shoulder-width.
Drive each arm up and down rapidly to send waves through the ropes.
Continue for the prescribed work interval.
formCues: Stay in the quarter-squat the entire interval.
Drive force from the legs and hips, not just the arms.
Keep the waves consistent and tight.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Bear Plank Hold
description: A static core hold on hands and knees in which the knees hover just above the floor while the back stays flat. It trains the abdominals and shoulders to stabilise the trunk and is a stepping stone to the full plank.
instructions: Start on hands and knees with the hands under the shoulders and the knees under the hips.
Tuck the toes under and brace the abdominals so the back is flat.
Press into the hands and lift the knees a couple of inches off the floor.
Hold the position with the hips level and the head in line with the spine.
Breathe steadily, then lower the knees to rest.
formCues: Keep the knees close to the floor; lifting them higher turns the hold into a pike.
Spread the fingers and push the floor away so the shoulders do not collapse.
Keep the neck long and look at the floor slightly ahead of the hands.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Behind the Back Barbell Shrug
alternativeNames: Encogimiento de Hombros con Barra Detrás de la Espalda
description: A shrug variation with the barbell held behind the body, targeting the trapezius.
instructions: Stand holding a barbell behind your back with an overhand grip.
Keep your arms straight and chest up.
Shrug your shoulders straight up toward your ears.
Pause and squeeze at the top.
Lower under control and repeat.
formCues: Lift straight up and down without rolling the shoulders.
Avoid bending your elbows to heave the weight higher.
Stand tall with a neutral neck and look straight ahead.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Behind-the-Neck Lat Pulldown
alternativeNames: Jalón al Cuello Detrás de la Cabeza
description: A wide-grip lat pulldown taken behind the head, targeting the upper lats and traps — requires full overhead shoulder mobility.
instructions: Sit at a lat pulldown station with thighs secured under the pad.
Grip the bar with a wide, overhand grip — wider than shoulder-width.
Keep the torso upright and tuck the chin slightly forward.
Pull the bar down behind the head until it touches the base of the neck.
Return under control to the full overhead stretch.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.
formCues: Only perform this if you have full, pain-free overhead shoulder mobility.
Use a moderate load — this is not a strength lift, it's a hypertrophy accessory.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Behind the Neck Press
description: An overhead press performed with the barbell starting behind the neck, emphasizing the front and side deltoids.
instructions: Sit or stand with a barbell resting on your upper traps behind your neck.
Grip the bar wider than shoulder width.
Press the bar straight up overhead until your arms are extended.
Lower the bar back to the starting position under control.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
formCues: Lower the bar only as far as your shoulders allow comfortably.
Keep your forearms vertical under the bar throughout the press.
Brace your core to avoid arching the lower back overhead.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Behind-the-Neck Pull-Up
description: A wide-grip pull-up pulled high enough that the bar passes behind the head at the top instead of under the chin, which forces the shoulders into end-range external rotation.
instructions: Grip the pull-up bar with an overhand grip wider than shoulder-width and hang at full arm extension with your legs together.
Keep your torso vertical rather than leaning back, and pull your elbows down and out to the sides.
Continue pulling until the bar passes behind your head and the back of your neck comes level with it, without letting the bar touch your neck.
Lower yourself under control back to a full dead hang, keeping your head still rather than letting it snap forward.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
formCues: This variation is widely discouraged. Finishing behind the head loads the shoulder at the end of its external rotation, where the joint has the least capacity to protect itself, and any contact between the bar and the neck puts that load through the cervical spine.

A standard or wide-grip pull-up trains the same muscles through the same shoulder range — nothing about back development requires the bar to travel behind the head, so there is no benefit here to trade the risk against.

If you perform it anyway, stop well short of touching the bar to your neck and leave it out entirely if you lack full pain-free overhead shoulder mobility or have any history of shoulder or neck problems.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Bench Adductor Stretch
description: A standing stretch with one straight leg resting on a bench out to the side to lengthen the inner thigh.
instructions: Stand side-on to a bench.
Rest one straight leg up on the bench out to the side.
Keep your torso upright and shift gently toward the bench.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
Switch sides and repeat.
formCues: Keep the standing foot pointing forward.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Bench Ankle Stretch
description: A standing stretch with the foot flat on a bench, driving the knee forward over the toes to flex the ankle.
instructions: Place one whole foot flat on top of a bench.
Keep your torso upright.
Drive that knee forward over your toes.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
Switch sides and repeat.
formCues: Keep your heel down on the bench.
Move slowly and keep the foot flat.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Bench Bulgarian Split Stretch
description: A split-stance stretch with the rear foot on a bench, sinking the hips to open the hip flexors and quad.
instructions: Rest the top of your rear foot on a bench behind you.
Set the front foot flat and bend that knee.
Sink your hips straight down.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
Switch sides and repeat.
formCues: Hold a wall for balance if needed.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Bench Calf Stretch
description: A standing stretch with the ball of the foot on a bench edge, dropping the heel to lengthen the calf.
instructions: Place the ball of one foot on the edge of a bench.
Keep that knee straight.
Let your heel drop down below the toes.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
Switch sides and repeat.
formCues: Hold the bench or a wall for balance.
Keep the movement slow and controlled.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Bench Chest Stretch
description: A kneeling stretch with the hands behind on a bench, sinking the hips to open the chest and shoulders.
instructions: Kneel with your back to a bench.
Place both hands behind you on the edge of the bench.
Sink your hips down to open the chest.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
formCues: Keep your shoulders down away from your ears.
Stretch to mild tension, never to pain.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Bench Child's Pose
alternativeNames: Stellung des Kindes an der Bank
description: A kneeling stretch with the arms resting on a bench, sitting the hips back to lengthen the lats and lower back.
instructions: Kneel on the floor in front of a bench.
Extend both arms forward and rest them on the bench.
Sit your hips back toward your heels and let the chest sink.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
formCues: Keep your arms straight and relax your neck.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Bench Couch Stretch
description: A deep quad and hip-flexor stretch with the rear shin running up the front of a bench.
instructions: Kneel with your rear shin against the front of a bench.
Place the front foot flat on the floor.
Bring your torso upright until the front of the thigh stretches.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
Switch sides and repeat.
formCues: Squeeze the rear glute to protect your lower back.
Pad the rear knee on a cushion for comfort.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Bench Decline Plank Hold
alternativeNames: Plank-Halt mit erhöhten Füßen auf der Bank
description: A plank with your hands on the floor and your feet on a bench behind you, so that your body slopes downward toward your hands. The raised feet shift more of your weight onto the shoulders and make the abdominal muscles work harder than in a normal plank.
instructions: Place a bench behind you and put the tops of your feet on it, then put your hands on the floor under your shoulders with your arms straight.
Walk your hands to a position where your body is in one straight line from your head to your heels.
Squeeze your glutes, brace your abs and push the floor away so that your shoulders do not sink between your shoulder blades.
Keep your neck in line with your spine and look at the floor between your hands.
Hold the position for the planned time, breathing slowly.
Lower your knees to the floor and rest.
formCues: Do not let the hips sag or rise above the line; stop the set when the line breaks.
Keep your hands directly under your shoulders so that the weight is carried by the skeleton, not by sore wrists.
Use a lower step if the bench is too high to keep a straight line.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Bench Figure-4 Glute Stretch
alternativeNames: Estiramiento Figura 4 de Glúteos en Banco
description: A seated stretch on a bench with one ankle crossed over the knee, hinging forward to target the glute.
instructions: Sit on the end of a bench.
Cross one ankle over the opposite knee.
Keep your back flat and hinge forward over the crossed leg.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
Switch sides and repeat.
formCues: Let the crossed knee fall open.
Hinge from the hips, keeping the chest open.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Bench Hamstring Stretch
description: A standing stretch with the heel on a bench, hinging forward over the straight raised leg to lengthen the hamstring.
instructions: Place one heel on a bench with that leg straight.
Stand tall on the supporting leg.
Hinge forward from the hips over the raised leg.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
Switch sides and repeat.
formCues: Keep your back flat as you fold forward.
Keep the raised leg straight, toes up.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Bench Hollow Hold
alternativeNames: Hollow Body Hold auf der Bank
Mantenimiento del Cuerpo Hueco en Banco
description: A static core hold performed lying on a flat bench: the arms reach overhead and the shoulders and straight legs are lifted into a shallow hollow shape while the lower back stays pressed into the bench.
instructions: Lie on your back on a flat bench with the glutes and lower back on the pad and the legs extended.
Reach the arms overhead beside the ears.
Brace the abdominals and press the lower back into the bench.
Lift the shoulders and the straight legs a few inches to form a shallow hollow.
Hold the position while breathing steadily, then lower to rest.
formCues: If the lower back arches off the pad, raise the legs higher or bend the knees slightly.
Keep the ribs pulled down and the neck relaxed.
Hold only as long as you can keep the lower back flat.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Bench Lat Stretch
description: A kneeling stretch with the hands on a bench, sinking the chest toward the floor to lengthen the lats.
instructions: Kneel on the floor in front of a bench.
Place both hands on top of the bench.
Sit your hips back and let your chest sink down.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
formCues: Keep your arms straight and head between your arms.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Bench Leg Pull-In
description: A seated core exercise on a flat bench: leaning back with your hands on the bench, you pull the knees toward the chest to train the rectus abdominis.
instructions: Sit on a flat bench, grip its edges beside or just behind your hips and lean your torso back slightly.
Extend your legs out in front of you with your feet off the floor.
Pull your knees toward your chest, bringing the torso slightly forward to meet them.
Extend the legs back out under control without letting your feet touch the floor.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
formCues: Keep your chest lifted and your back straight; do not round forward.
Control the eccentric; do not let gravity drop the legs.
Squeeze the abs at the top of each rep for a stronger contraction.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Bench Pull
description: A rowing exercise performed lying face down on an elevated bench, eliminating body momentum to target the lats and rhomboids.
instructions: Lie face down on an elevated bench with arms hanging straight down.
Grip a barbell or dumbbells below you.
Row the weight up to the underside of the bench.
Squeeze your shoulder blades at the top.
Lower under control and repeat.
formCues: Keep your chest glued to the bench to prevent cheating.
Reach a full stretch at the bottom before each pull.
Drive your elbows up and back rather than curling the weight.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Bent Arm Barbell Pullover
alternativeNames: Pullover con Barra y Brazos Flexionados
description: A pullover variation performed with elbows bent, lowering a barbell behind the head to stretch the lats and chest.
instructions: Lie on a bench holding a barbell above your chest with bent elbows.
Keep your elbows bent throughout the movement.
Lower the barbell behind your head in an arc.
Pull the barbell back over your chest using your lats.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
formCues: Keep your ribs down and avoid arching your lower back.
Limit the stretch to a range your shoulders can control.
Breathe in deeply as the bar lowers behind your head.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Bent-Arm EZ-Bar Pullover
alternativeNames: Pullover con Barra Z y Brazos Flexionados
description: A bent-arm pullover on a flat bench using an EZ-bar — wrist-friendlier than the straight barbell version while keeping the deep lat and pec stretch.
instructions: Lie on a flat bench holding an EZ-bar with a narrow overhand grip on the inner bends.
Start with the bar above your chest, elbows bent to roughly 90 degrees.
Keep the elbow angle fixed and lower the bar back in an arc overhead until a deep stretch is felt in the lats and pecs.
Pull the bar back over the chest along the same arc, without straightening the elbows.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.
formCues: The elbow angle stays fixed — only the shoulder moves.
Bent elbows shorten the lever, so you can usually handle a little more weight than in a straight-arm pullover.
If the lower back arches, plant the feet more firmly and brace the abs.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Bent-Knee Copenhagen Raises
alternativeNames: Elevaciones en Plancha Copenhague con Rodilla Flexionada
description: A shorter-lever version of the Copenhagen plank raise. In a side plank with your top leg on a flat bench, you bend the knee of your lower leg and lift it up toward the bench, then lower it again. The inner thigh muscles and the obliques work as in the straight-leg version, with less load on the lower leg.
instructions: Lie on your side next to a flat bench and place the inside of your top leg or foot on it, with the top knee slightly bent or straight.
Prop yourself up on the elbow of your lower arm, directly under your shoulder.
Lift your hips so that your body forms a straight line from your head to your top leg, and bend the knee of your lower leg under you.
Raise the bent lower knee up toward the bench, keeping your hips high.
Lower the knee slowly without letting your hips drop, and repeat for the planned repetitions.
Rest, then switch sides.
formCues: Use this version to build up to the straight-leg Copenhagen raise; the bent knee shortens the lever and lowers the load.
Keep your hips high and your body in one line; dropping the hips takes the load off the inner thighs.
Move slowly and stop if you feel a sharp pull in the groin; the adductors need a gentle build-up.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Bent-Over Dumbbell Row
description: A two-arm bent-over row with a dumbbell in each hand. The free movement of independent dumbbells lets the elbows track natural and adds a stability demand that a barbell row hides.
instructions: Stand with feet hip-width, holding a dumbbell in each hand at the sides, palms facing in.
Hinge at the hips with a flat back until the torso is roughly 30–45 degrees from horizontal, dumbbells hanging directly below the shoulders.
Brace the core and pull both dumbbells up and slightly back, driving the elbows past the ribs.
Squeeze the upper back at the top, keeping the elbows tucked.
Lower under control to the starting position with the arms fully extended.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.
formCues: The torso angle stays fixed throughout — no rocking up to help the dumbbells.
Pull to the lower ribs/belly, not to the chest; that line keeps the lats loaded.
If the lower back rounds, hinge less and reset before the next set.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Bent-Over EZ-Bar Row
description: A horizontal pulling movement with an EZ-bar for a wrist-friendly back rowing exercise.
instructions: Hold an EZ-bar with an overhand grip, hinge at the hips to 45 degrees.
Pull the bar to your lower ribcage.
Lower under control.
Repeat.
formCues: Initiate with the elbows, not the hands.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Dumbbell Bicep Curl
description: An isolation exercise targeting the biceps.
instructions: Stand holding dumbbells at your sides, palms forward.
Curl the weights up toward your shoulders.
Squeeze at the top, then lower under control.
Repeat.
formCues: Keep your elbows pinned to your sides.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Bicycle Crunch
description: A dynamic crunch variation targeting both the rectus abdominis and obliques.
instructions: Lie on your back with hands behind your head and legs raised.
Bring one knee toward your chest while rotating your torso to meet it with the opposite elbow.
Extend that leg while bringing the other knee in.
Continue alternating in a pedaling motion.
Repeat.
formCues: Avoid pulling on your neck with your hands.
Lead the rotation with your shoulder, not your elbow.
Move slowly and deliberately rather than racing through reps.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Bird-Dog
description: A core stability exercise extending opposite arm and leg to challenge the erector spinae and deep core.
instructions: Start on all fours with a neutral spine.
Extend your right arm forward and left leg back simultaneously.
Hold for a moment, then return.
Repeat on the other side.
Alternate.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Bird Dog Hold
description: A static core hold balancing on all fours with one arm and the opposite leg extended, training spinal stability.
instructions: Start on all fours with hands under shoulders and knees under hips.
Extend one arm forward and the opposite leg back.
Keep your core tight and body level.
Hold the position without rotating your torso.
Hold for time. Complete on one side, then switch.
formCues: Reach long through your fingertips and heel in opposite directions.
Push the floor away with your supporting hand to stay stable.
Breathe steadily instead of holding your breath.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Boat Pose
description: A seated balance on the sit bones with the legs lifted and the chest tall, holding a V shape that loads the hip flexors and the whole front of the trunk.
instructions: Sit on the floor with the knees bent and the feet flat, hands resting behind the thighs.
Lean back until you balance just behind the sit bones and lift the chest so the spine stays long.
Lift the shins until they are parallel to the floor, then straighten the legs as far as the back stays flat.
Reach the arms forward beside the legs and hold the position for the prescribed time.
Lower the feet under control to finish.
formCues: Keep the chest lifted; the moment the back rounds, bend the knees again.
Hold behind the thighs if the hamstrings limit you more than the core does.
Breathe steadily instead of bracing against a held breath.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Bodyweight Calf Raise
alternativeNames: Elevación de Talones con Peso Corporal
description: A beginner-friendly calf raise using body weight only on flat ground, strengthening the gastrocnemius and soleus.
instructions: Stand with feet hip-width apart on a flat surface.
Push up onto the balls of your feet as high as possible.
Squeeze your calves at the top.
Lower your heels back to the floor under control.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
formCues: Use light fingertip support for balance if needed.
Control the lowering phase instead of dropping your heels quickly.
Keep your ankles from rolling outward as you rise.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Bodyweight Good Morning
description: A bodyweight hip hinge with hands behind the head, strengthening the hamstrings and spinal erectors.
instructions: Stand with feet hip-width apart and hands behind your head.
Keep a slight bend in your knees and brace your core.
Hinge at the hips and lower your torso toward parallel.
Drive your hips forward to return to standing.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
formCues: Push your hips back as if closing a door behind you.
Keep your spine neutral from head to tailbone throughout.
Stop the descent when your hamstrings reach their stretch limit.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Bodyweight Lateral Raise
description: A shoulder isolation movement performed without equipment to develop lateral deltoid width.
instructions: Stand upright with arms hanging at your sides.
Raise both arms out to the sides with a slight elbow bend until parallel with the floor.
Pause briefly at the top.
Lower slowly back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired reps.
formCues: Lead with your elbows, not your hands.
Avoid shrugging your shoulders at the top.
Control the descent to maximize time under tension.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Bodyweight Overhead Press
alternativeNames: Press por Encima de la Cabeza con Peso Corporal
description: An unloaded standing overhead press: the arms press up from the shoulders until they are straight overhead, rehearsing the pressing pattern for the shoulders and triceps without any equipment.
instructions: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart and your hands in loose fists at shoulder height, palms facing forward and elbows under the wrists.
Brace your core and squeeze your glutes so your ribs stay down.
Press both arms straight up until the elbows are fully extended and the upper arms are beside your ears.
Lower your hands back to shoulder height under control.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
formCues: Finish with your hands directly over your shoulders, not in front of your face.
Do not lean back or arch your lower back to get the arms higher.
Once the pattern feels smooth, hold light dumbbells or a band to add load.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Bodyweight Reverse Lunge
description: A lunge variation using only body weight, stepping backward for better knee stability than a forward lunge.
instructions: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart.
Step one leg back and lower your knee toward the floor.
Lower until your front thigh is parallel to the floor.
Push through your front heel to return to standing.
Repeat on both sides.
formCues: No weight needed -- focus on balance and a controlled descent.
Keep your torso upright instead of leaning forward.
Step back far enough that your front knee stays behind your toes.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Bodyweight Squat
description: A foundational lower-body exercise squatting with body weight only, developing the quadriceps, glutes, and basic movement mechanics.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and arms extended forward.
Sit back and down by bending your hips and knees.
Lower until your thighs are parallel to the floor.
Drive through your heels to return to standing.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
formCues: Keep your weight spread across your whole foot.
Track your knees in line with your toes.
Keep your chest up to avoid rounding the upper back.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Bow Pose
description: A prone backbend in which the hands hold the ankles and the legs press away, lifting the chest and thighs off the floor and loading the whole back line.
instructions: Lie face down with the arms beside the body and the forehead resting on the mat.
Bend the knees and take hold of the outside of both ankles.
Press the shins back into the hands so the chest and thighs lift away from the floor.
Hold the lifted position for the prescribed time, keeping the neck long and the gaze forward.
Release the ankles and lower down under control.
formCues: Drive the lift from the legs pressing into the hands, not from pulling with the arms.
Keep the knees roughly hip-width apart rather than letting them splay.
If the shoulders feel pinched, lift less and keep the chest open instead.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Box Jump
description: A plyometric jump from a quarter-squat onto a stable box, training lower-body power.
instructions: Stand a foot in front of a sturdy box with feet shoulder-width.
Drop into a quarter-squat and swing the arms back.
Drive the arms up and explode off the floor onto the box.
Land softly with both feet flat and knees bent.
Step down — do not jump down — and reset.
formCues: Always step down — repeated drop-landings stress the Achilles.
Land softly with the whole foot, knees tracking over the toes.
Pick a box height you can clear cleanly without piking the hips.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Box Squat
description: A squat performed to a box or bench, which fixes the depth and teaches sitting back into the hips.
instructions: Stand in front of a box or bench, feet shoulder-width apart, with your arms extended forward for balance.
Push your hips back and bend your knees, sitting back toward the box rather than straight down.
Touch the box lightly with your glutes without collapsing onto it.
Drive through your feet to stand back up, squeezing your glutes at the top.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
formCues: Use a box height that lets your thighs reach about parallel to the floor and lower it as mobility improves.
Keep your weight through the middle of your feet — do not rock onto your toes.
Touch and go: fully relaxing onto the box loses core tension and stresses the spine.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Bulgarian Split Squat
description: A single-leg squat variation with the rear foot elevated.
instructions: Stand in front of a bench, place one foot behind you on the bench.
Hold dumbbells at your sides.
Lower your body until your front thigh is parallel to the floor.
Push through your front heel to stand back up.
Repeat on both sides.
formCues: Keep most of your weight on the front leg.
Track your front knee over your toes without letting it cave inward.
Square your hips forward and avoid rotating toward the bench.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Burpees
description: A full-body conditioning movement combining a squat, plank, push-up, and jump.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart.
Squat down and place the hands on the floor in front of you.
Jump or step the feet back into a plank, then perform a push-up.
Jump or step the feet forward to the hands.
Stand up and jump explosively, reaching the arms overhead.
formCues: Keep the back flat in the plank — do not let the hips sag.
Scale by stepping the feet back instead of jumping.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Butterfly Stretch
description: A seated stretch for the inner thighs, pressing the soles of the feet together with the knees dropped out.
instructions: Sit tall and press the soles of your feet together.
Let your knees drop out toward the floor.
Hold your feet and sit up tall.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
formCues: Gently press the knees down with your elbows for more stretch.
Bring your heels closer to your body to increase intensity.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Cable Bent-Over Row
description: A cable rowing variation providing constant tension throughout the movement.
instructions: Attach a straight or V-bar to a low cable pulley.
Hinge at the hips with knees slightly bent.
Pull the handle toward your lower chest.
Squeeze your shoulder blades at the top.
Lower with control and repeat.
formCues: Hold the hinge position steady instead of standing up as you pull.
Keep your back flat from head to hips throughout.
Resist the cable's pull on the way back to full stretch.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Cable Chest Press
description: A standing chest press on the cable machine, providing constant tension while the staggered stance demands core stability.
instructions: Set the cables to chest height and face away from the machine.
Grip a handle in each hand and step forward into a staggered stance.
Press the handles forward until your arms are extended.
Squeeze your chest at the top.
Return under control and repeat.
formCues: Press both handles evenly to avoid twisting your torso.
Brace your core against the backward pull of the stack.
Step forward enough that the cables stay taut throughout each rep.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Cable Crunch
description: A kneeling abdominal exercise flexing the spine against cable resistance, allowing progressive loading of the rectus abdominis.
instructions: Kneel in front of a cable machine with a rope attachment at the top.
Hold the rope near your forehead with elbows bent.
Crunch down by flexing your spine and bringing your elbows to your thighs.
Squeeze your abs hard at the bottom.
Return to the start position and repeat.
formCues: Avoid pulling the rope down with your arms.
Keep your hips fixed so movement comes from the spine.
Exhale fully as you crunch down.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Cable External Rotation
description: A cable exercise rotating the forearm outward with the elbow pinned at the side, strengthening the rotator cuff's external rotators with the rear delts assisting.
instructions: Set a cable pulley to elbow height and grip the handle.
Stand side-on to the machine with your working elbow bent at 90 degrees.
Keep your elbow glued to your side and rotate your forearm outward.
Pause at the end of the movement.
Return under control. Complete reps on one side, then switch.
formCues: Use a light weight to keep the rotation strict and controlled.
Keep your wrist straight and in line with your forearm.
Avoid shrugging your shoulder or twisting your torso during the movement.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Cable Fly
description: An isolation movement for the chest using cable resistance for constant tension.
instructions: Stand between two cable columns with handles attached to high pulleys.
With a slight bend in your elbows, open your arms wide.
Bring your hands together in front of your chest in a hugging motion.
Slowly return to the starting position.
Repeat.
formCues: Maintain the same elbow bend throughout; do not press the weight.
Step one foot forward for a stable, balanced stance.
Control the stretch; do not let the cables yank your arms back.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Cable Hammer Curl
description: A cable curl using a rope attachment with a neutral grip to target the brachialis and brachioradialis with constant tension.
instructions: Attach a rope to a low cable pulley and stand facing the machine.
Grip the rope with a neutral (hammer) grip, palms facing each other.
Curl the rope upward toward your shoulders, keeping elbows pinned at your sides.
Squeeze at the top, then lower slowly to full extension.
Repeat for the desired reps.
formCues: Keep your elbows stationary throughout the movement.
Pull the rope ends apart slightly at the top to increase contraction.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Cable Glute Kickback
alternativeNames: Patada Trasera de Glúteos en Cable
description: A cable isolation exercise for the glutes, extending the hip back against constant resistance.
instructions: Attach an ankle cuff to a low cable pulley and fasten it around one ankle.
Stand facing the machine, holding the frame lightly for balance, and hinge slightly forward at the hips.
Kick the cuffed leg straight back, extending the hip fully while keeping the knee nearly straight.
Squeeze the glute at full hip extension, then return the foot slowly to the start.
Complete all reps on one side before switching.
formCues: Lead with the heel to maximize glute activation over hamstrings.
Keep the hips square; avoid rotating the pelvis as the leg kicks back.
The movement comes entirely from the hip — keep the back and torso still.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Cable Overhead Tricep Extension
alternativeNames: Extensión de Tríceps por Encima de la Cabeza con Cable
description: A cable triceps exercise: facing away from the weight stack, you hold a rope behind your head and straighten your elbows to push it up and overhead. The overhead position stretches the long head of the triceps, and the cable keeps tension on the muscle through the whole movement.
instructions: Attach a rope to the low pulley and select a light weight.
Take the rope in both hands, turn away from the stack and step forward into a staggered stance so the cable pulls you back.
Raise the rope overhead with your elbows bent and your upper arms close to your ears, so your hands are behind your head.
Brace your trunk and keep your upper arms still, then straighten your elbows to push the rope up until your arms are fully extended overhead.
Pause briefly at the top, then bend your elbows to lower the rope back behind your head under control.
Repeat for the planned repetitions.
formCues: Keep the elbows pointing forward and the upper arms still; letting them flare out or drift turns the extension into a press.
Step far enough forward that the cable holds you steady, and avoid arching your lower back as the arms go overhead.
Use a weight you can control through the full stretch; heavy loads pull the elbows apart.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Cable Pallof Press
description: An anti-rotation core exercise in which a cable pulls you sideways while you press a handle straight out from your chest and refuse to let your torso turn.
instructions: Set a cable at chest height and take the handle in both hands, standing side-on to the machine.
Step away until there is real tension on the cable, with your feet about shoulder-width apart and knees softly bent.
Bring the handle to the centre of your chest and brace your trunk and glutes.
Press the handle straight out in front of you until your arms are extended, resisting the pull that wants to rotate you toward the machine.
Hold the extended position for a moment, then bring the handle back to your chest under control.
Complete the desired reps, then turn around and repeat facing the other way.
formCues: Nothing should rotate. If your shoulders turn toward the cable as you press, reduce the weight — the point is the rotation that does not happen.
The further you step from the machine, the longer the lever and the harder it gets, so you can change difficulty without touching the weight stack.
Keep your arms level with your chest and your shoulders down; letting the handle drift up turns it into a front raise.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Cable Pull-Through
description: A cable-resisted hip hinge performed facing away from a low pulley, loading the glutes and hamstrings without placing a bar across the spine.
instructions: Attach a rope to the low pulley and stand facing away from the machine with the rope between the legs.
Step forward until the cable is taut, then brace the trunk and soften the knees.
Push the hips back while keeping the spine neutral and the arms long.
Drive the hips forward and squeeze the glutes to stand tall.
Reverse into the next hinge without letting the weight stack slam down.
formCues: Think hips back and hips through; the arms only hold the rope.
Keep the shins nearly vertical so the movement stays a hinge rather than a squat.
Finish tall without leaning backwards at lockout.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Cable Reverse Fly
description: A standing cable exercise for the rear deltoids: facing the space between two cable towers, you hold the opposite handles with the cables crossed in front of you and sweep your arms out and back until they are level with your shoulders. The cables keep tension on the back of the shoulders through the whole arc.
instructions: Set both pulleys at about shoulder height and stand centred between the two cable towers.
Take the left handle in your right hand and the right handle in your left hand, so the cables cross in front of you.
Stand tall with your arms reaching forward at shoulder height and a slight bend in the elbows.
Sweep your arms out and back in a wide arc, leading with the elbows, until they are in line with your shoulders.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together briefly without arching your lower back.
Bring the handles back to the crossed start position slowly and repeat for the planned repetitions.
formCues: Keep the elbows soft and fixed; bending and straightening them turns the fly into a row.
Keep your shoulders down and your neck relaxed so the rear deltoids do the work, not the upper trapezius.
Use a light weight and a slow return; the cables pull hardest at the end of the arc, so control that position.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Cable Tricep Kickback
description: An isolation movement performed hinged forward, extending the elbow against cable resistance to work the triceps.
instructions: Attach a handle to a low cable and hinge forward at the hips.
Tuck your upper arm against your side with elbow bent 90 degrees.
Extend your elbow to push the handle back behind you.
Squeeze your triceps at the end of the movement.
Return under control. Complete reps on one side, then switch.
formCues: Move only your forearm; keep the upper arm completely still.
Avoid rounding your back while holding the hinged position.
Use a light weight to reach full lockout without swinging.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Calf Raise Hold
description: An isometric calf exercise: you rise onto the balls of your feet with the knees straight and hold the top position. The gastrocnemius and the soleus stay under constant tension at the point where a calf raise is hardest, with no movement to hide behind.
instructions: Stand tall with your feet about hip-width apart and your arms relaxed at your sides.
Push through the balls of your feet and rise onto your toes as high as you can.
Keep your knees straight and your weight over the middle of your feet, not rolling out to the little toes.
Stop at the top and hold the position, heels as high as possible.
Keep your hips level, your chest tall and your breathing slow while you hold for the planned time.
Lower your heels slowly to the floor and rest.
formCues: Hold on to a wall or a rack with one hand if you wobble; the aim is the calf contraction, not the balance.
Do not let the heels sink during the hold; if they drop, end the set instead of bouncing back up.
Add a pair of dumbbells or a loaded backpack once you can hold bodyweight for a full minute.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Camel Pose
description: A kneeling backbend that opens the front of the hips, the abdomen and the chest while the hands support the position on the heels or the lower back.
instructions: Kneel with the knees hip-width apart and the hips stacked over the knees.
Place the hands on the back of the pelvis with the fingers pointing down and lift the chest.
Press the hips forward and arch back, reaching for the heels if the position stays comfortable.
Hold the pose for the prescribed time, keeping the neck in line with the spine.
Bring the hands back to the pelvis and come up chest-first.
formCues: Keep the hips over the knees; letting them travel back turns the pose into a collapse.
Tuck the toes under and rest the hands on raised heels if the full reach is too deep.
Come out slowly: lifting the head first is what usually makes people dizzy.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Captain's Chair Knee Raise
alternativeNames: Elevación de Rodillas en Silla Romana
description: A bodyweight core exercise performed on a captain's chair that targets the lower abs and hip flexors.
instructions: Position yourself in the captain's chair with your back flat against the pad and forearms on the armrests.
Let your legs hang straight down.
Engage your core and raise your knees toward your chest.
Hold briefly at the top, then lower slowly to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired reps.
formCues: Avoid swinging the legs for momentum.
Exhale as you raise your knees.
Keep your back pressed against the pad throughout.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Captain's Chair Leg Raise
alternativeNames: Elevación de Piernas en Silla Romana
description: A bodyweight core exercise on a captain's chair that targets the lower abs and hip flexors with straight legs for greater difficulty.
instructions: Position yourself in the captain's chair with your back flat against the pad and forearms on the armrests.
Let your legs hang straight down.
Keeping your legs straight, raise them until parallel with the floor or higher.
Hold briefly at the top, then lower slowly.
Repeat for the desired reps.
formCues: Keep your legs as straight as possible throughout.
Avoid swinging — control the movement with your core.
For less difficulty, bend the knees slightly.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Cat-Cow
description: A kneeling flow that alternates between rounding the spine towards the ceiling and letting it sag while the chest opens, moving every segment of the back through its range.
instructions: Start on all fours with the hands under the shoulders and the knees under the hips.
Exhale and round the spine towards the ceiling, tucking the tailbone and letting the head drop.
Inhale and reverse it: let the belly sink, lift the chest and tailbone, and look slightly forward.
Move between the two shapes slowly, one breath per position.
Finish in a neutral spine and sit back onto the heels.
formCues: Let the breath set the tempo rather than rushing between the two positions.
Keep the hands pressing evenly so the shoulders do not collapse towards the floor.
Move the whole spine, including the neck, instead of hinging only at the lower back.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Cat Stretch
description: A kneeling stretch that rounds the spine upward to lengthen the back muscles.
instructions: Start on all fours, hands under shoulders and knees under hips.
Round your spine up toward the ceiling.
Tuck your chin toward your chest.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
formCues: Push the floor away with your hands to spread the shoulder blades.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Chair Pose
description: A standing hold with the hips sunk back and the arms overhead, so the quadriceps and the upper back work isometrically against bodyweight.
instructions: Stand with the feet together or hip-width apart and the weight in the heels.
Bend the knees and send the hips back as if sitting down onto a chair.
Raise the arms overhead beside the ears, keeping the ribs from flaring.
Hold the position for the prescribed time with the chest lifted and the knees tracking over the toes.
Press through the heels to stand back up.
formCues: Keep enough weight in the heels that you could lift the toes.
Take the arms slightly forward if raising them fully makes the lower back arch.
Sink lower for more quadriceps work, but only while the heels stay down.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Cheat Curl
description: A momentum-assisted bicep curl using slight hip drive on the way up and a slow, controlled lowering phase.
instructions: Stand holding weight at thigh level with an underhand grip.
Use a slight hip drive to start the curl.
Curl the weight up toward your shoulders explosively.
Lower the weight slowly under control through the full range.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
formCues: Keep the hip drive small so your biceps still do most of the work.
Avoid leaning back excessively to protect your lower back.
Keep your elbows close to your torso throughout the curl.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Machine Chest Press
description: A machine-based pressing movement for the chest, ideal for beginners.
instructions: Sit in the machine with your back flat against the pad.
Grip the handles at chest level.
Push the handles forward until your arms are fully extended.
Slowly return to the starting position.
Repeat.
formCues: Adjust the seat so the handles line up with mid-chest.
Keep your shoulder blades pulled back against the pad as you press.
Press to full extension without forcefully locking your elbows.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Chest-Supported Dumbbell Row
alternativeNames: Remo con Mancuernas con Apoyo en el Pecho
description: A dumbbell row with chest support to eliminate lower back strain and isolate the back muscles.
instructions: Lie face-down on an incline bench with dumbbells hanging beneath.
Row the dumbbells up to your sides.
Squeeze at the top, then lower.
Repeat.
formCues: The chest support eliminates back fatigue.
Focus on squeezing the shoulder blades together.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Chest Supported Dumbbell Shrug
alternativeNames: Encogimiento de Hombros con Mancuernas y Apoyo en el Pecho
description: A shrug performed face-down on an incline bench, the chest support isolating the traps and removing momentum.
instructions: Set an incline bench to about 30 degrees.
Lie face down on the bench holding dumbbells at arm's length.
Shrug your shoulders up and back toward your ears.
Squeeze your upper traps at the top.
Lower under control and repeat.
formCues: Shrug up and back toward your ears rather than straight up.
Keep your chest pinned to the pad so you cannot use body english.
Pause and squeeze at the top before lowering under control.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Chest-Supported Kettlebell Row
alternativeNames: Remo con Kettlebell Apoyado en el Pecho
description: This exercise targets your back muscles, primarily the latissimus dorsi and rhomboids, by rowing a kettlebell in each hand towards your hips while your torso is supported on an incline bench.
instructions: Lie face down on an incline bench, allowing your arms to hang freely with a kettlebell in each hand.
Brace your core and retract your shoulder blades.
Pull the kettlebells towards your hips, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause briefly at the top, feeling the contraction in your back.
Slowly lower the kettlebells back to the starting position with control.
formCues: Maintain a stable torso throughout the movement; avoid rocking.
Focus on initiating the pull with your back muscles, not just your arms.
Keep your elbows close to your body to emphasize the lats.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Chest-Supported Machine Row
alternativeNames: Remo en Máquina con Apoyo en el Pecho
description: A seated rowing machine exercise with a chest pad that supports the torso, so the lats and the muscles between the shoulder blades do the pulling and the lower back stays out of it. You pull the handles back by driving the elbows behind you, then let them return forward with control.
instructions: Adjust the seat so the handles sit at lower-chest height, then sit with your chest against the pad and your feet planted.
Reach forward and take the handles with your arms extended and your shoulders relaxed.
Brace your trunk, then pull the handles back by driving your elbows behind you.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the end of the pull without lifting your chest off the pad.
Pause briefly, then extend your arms to return the handles forward under control.
Repeat for the planned repetitions, keeping your chest on the pad throughout.
formCues: Pull with the elbows rather than the hands, so the lats and mid-back lead and the biceps assist.
Keep the chest on the pad and the shoulders down; shrugging or leaning back turns the row into an upper trapezius pull.
Let the shoulder blades spread forward at the start of each repetition to get a full stretch before the next pull.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Chest-Supported Smith Machine Row
alternativeNames: Remo con Apoyo en el Pecho en Máquina Smith
description: A row performed against an inclined pad inside the Smith machine, where the chest support removes the lower back from the movement and the guided bar keeps the pull in one line.
instructions: Set an incline bench inside the Smith machine facing the bar, and set the bar low enough that your arms hang straight when you lean on the pad.
Stand astride the bench with your feet planted and your chest resting against the top of the pad.
Take an overhand grip a little wider than shoulder-width and unhook the bar with your arms extended.
Pull the bar up to your lower chest, leading with your elbows and squeezing the shoulder blades together at the top.
Lower the bar under control until your arms are straight again, and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
formCues: Keep your chest on the pad for every repetition. The moment you push off it to move the weight you have turned this back into a bent-over row and given up the reason for the setup.
Lead with the elbows and stop when they pass your torso. Pulling further only rolls the shoulders forward and the fixed bar path leaves nowhere for them to go.
Because your lower back is doing nothing here, this is the row to use on a day when a bent-over row is not an option -- match the weight to what your back can pull, not to what your legs could brace.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Child's Pose
description: A kneeling rest stretch that lengthens the lats, lower back and shoulders with the arms reaching forward.
instructions: Kneel and sit your hips back toward your heels.
Fold your torso forward over your thighs.
Reach both arms out long on the floor in front.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
formCues: Spread your knees wider to rest your chest lower.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Chin Tuck Hold
description: A static neck drill that retracts the head straight back to strengthen the deep neck flexors and counter forward-head posture.
instructions: Stand or sit tall with your shoulders relaxed.
Pull your chin straight back, creating a double chin.
Keep your head level without tilting.
Hold the position for the desired duration.
Release and repeat for multiple sets.
formCues: Imagine sliding your head back over your spine, not nodding down.
Keep your gaze level and your breathing relaxed.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Chin-Ups
description: A supinated-grip pull-up that strongly activates the biceps alongside the lats.
instructions: Hang from a bar with a shoulder-width underhand grip.
Pull yourself up until chin is above the bar.
Lower under control.
Repeat.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Clamshells
description: A side-lying hip exercise opening the top knee against gravity to activate the gluteus medius.
instructions: Lie on your side with knees bent and stacked on top of each other.
Keep your feet together and hips stacked.
Open your top knee toward the ceiling without rotating your hips.
Squeeze your outer glute at the top.
Lower under control. Complete reps on one side, then switch.
formCues: Place a hand on your top hip to check for unwanted rolling.
Keep the movement small and controlled rather than forcing the knee high.
Rest your head on your lower arm to keep your spine neutral.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Clamshell Hold
description: The top position of the clamshell held for time: lying on one side with the knees bent and stacked, the upper knee lifted and the pelvis square, so the glute medius works isometrically instead of through repetitions.
instructions: Lie on one side with the hips and knees bent about 45 and 90 degrees, heels together and knees stacked.
Stack the shoulders and hips vertically and brace the trunk so the pelvis cannot roll backwards.
Open the upper knee as far as it goes without the pelvis rotating, keeping the heels touching.
Hold that open position for the prescribed time, breathing normally.
Lower the knee under control and repeat on the other side.
formCues: Stop the lift where the pelvis starts to roll back; the range is smaller than most people expect.
Keep the heels pressed together so the movement stays in the hip rather than the ankle.
Add a loop band above the knees only once the pelvis stays perfectly still.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Clap Push-Ups
description: An explosive plyometric push-up developing chest power and fast-twitch muscle fibers.
instructions: Begin in a standard push-up position.
Lower your chest to the floor.
Explosively push up so hands leave the ground.
Clap your hands together and land softly, returning to start.
Repeat.
formCues: Land with soft elbows to absorb impact.
Ensure you have enough upper body strength before attempting.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Clean
description: An Olympic lift pulling a barbell explosively from the floor to the front-rack position on the shoulders.
instructions: Stand over a loaded barbell with feet hip-width apart.
Grip the bar just outside your knees with an overhand grip.
Drive explosively through your legs and extend your hips.
Pull yourself under the bar and catch it on your front deltoids.
Stand fully upright to complete the lift.
formCues: Keep the bar close to your body as it travels up.
Finish your leg drive fully before pulling under the bar.
Catch with your elbows high so the bar rests on your shoulders.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Clean and Jerk
description: A two-part Olympic lift cleaning a barbell to the shoulders, then driving it overhead.
instructions: Pull a loaded barbell from the floor to your shoulders as in a clean.
Stand fully with the bar racked on your front delts.
Dip slightly and drive the bar overhead explosively.
Drop into a partial squat under the bar as your arms lock out overhead, feet staying about hip-width apart.
Stand up fully and hold the bar steady overhead before lowering it.
formCues: Stand fully and reset your position before starting the jerk.
Drive the bar up with your legs, not just your arms.
Lock your arms out as you drop under the bar, then stand and hold the finish briefly.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Close-Grip Barbell Curl
alternativeNames: Curl de Barra con Agarre Cerrado
description: A standing barbell curl with a narrow grip, biasing the long head of the biceps and the brachialis.
instructions: Stand holding a barbell with an underhand grip, hands closer than shoulder-width apart.
Start with the bar at the thighs, arms extended, elbows tucked to the sides.
Curl the bar up to the shoulders by flexing the elbows.
Squeeze the biceps at the top, then lower under control.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.
formCues: Keep the elbows pinned to the sides — do not let them drift forward.
If the narrow grip bothers your wrists, use an EZ-bar.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Close-Grip Bench Press
alternativeNames: Press de Banca con Agarre Cerrado
description: A bench press variation with a narrow grip that shifts the emphasis to the triceps.
instructions: Lie on a flat bench and grip the barbell with hands shoulder-width apart.
Lower the bar to your lower chest keeping elbows close to your sides.
Press back up to full extension.
Repeat.
formCues: Keep elbows tucked to maximize triceps activation.
Avoid too-narrow a grip to prevent wrist strain.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Close-Grip Dumbbell Bench Press
alternativeNames: Press de Banca con Mancuernas y Agarre Cerrado
description: A dumbbell bench press with dumbbells held together to increase triceps involvement.
instructions: Lie on a flat bench and hold two dumbbells together over your chest.
Lower them to your chest keeping elbows close.
Press back up.
Repeat.
formCues: Press the dumbbells together throughout the movement.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Close-Grip EZ-Bar Bench Press
alternativeNames: Press de Banca con Barra Z y Agarre Cerrado
description: A triceps-focused press using an EZ-bar with a narrow grip for wrist comfort.
instructions: Lie on a flat bench and grip the inner curves of the EZ-bar.
Lower the bar to your chest with elbows tucked.
Press back up to full extension.
Repeat.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Close-Grip EZ-Bar Curl
alternativeNames: Curl con Barra Z y Agarre Cerrado
description: An EZ-bar biceps curl with hands close together, biasing the long head of the biceps.
instructions: Stand holding an EZ-bar with hands on the inner bends, palms up.
Keep the elbows tucked at the sides.
Curl the bar up to shoulder level, squeezing the biceps.
Lower under control to a full stretch.
Repeat for the prescribed reps.
formCues: Keep the elbows pinned — do not let them flare forward.
Avoid swinging the torso for momentum.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Close-Grip Incline Bench Press
alternativeNames: Press de Banca Inclinado con Agarre Cerrado
description: An incline bench press with a close grip targeting the triceps and upper chest.
instructions: Set bench to an incline. Grip the barbell with hands shoulder-width or closer.
Lower the bar to your upper chest.
Press back up.
Repeat.
formCues: The incline increases the stretch on the long head of the triceps.
Tuck elbows to keep the focus on triceps.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Close Grip Lat Pulldown
alternativeNames: Jalón al Pecho con Agarre Cerrado
description: A lat pulldown variation using a close, parallel-grip handle to emphasize the lower lats and biceps.
instructions: Sit at a lat pulldown machine and secure your thighs under the pad.
Grip the close-grip handle with palms facing each other.
Pull the handle down to your upper chest.
Squeeze your lats at the bottom.
Return under control and repeat.
formCues: Lean back only slightly, not excessively.
Avoid using momentum to pull the handle down.
Drive your elbows down and back, not just your hands.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Close-Grip Pull-Ups
description: A pull-up with a narrow overhand grip that increases biceps and inner-back activation.
instructions: Hang from a pull-up bar with hands shoulder-width or narrower, palms away.
Pull yourself up until chin clears the bar.
Lower under control.
Repeat.
formCues: The narrow grip increases biceps involvement.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Close Grip Push Ups
description: A push-up variation with hands placed close together to emphasize the triceps.
instructions: Assume a push-up position with hands directly under your shoulders.
Keep your elbows tucked close to your ribs.
Lower your chest toward the floor.
Press back up to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
formCues: Keep your elbows tracking backward, not flared out.
Maintain a rigid plank position throughout.
Slow the descent for greater triceps activation.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Close-Stance Leg Press
alternativeNames: Prensa de piernas con postura cerrada
description: A leg press with the feet set close together, increasing knee flexion and keeping the quadriceps prominent while the back remains supported against the pad.
instructions: Set the seat and back pad so your lower back stays supported throughout the repetition.
Place your feet close together near the middle of the platform, with the toes and knees pointing along the same line.
Lower the sled by bending the knees and hips while keeping both feet flat and the knees tracking over the toes.
Press the platform away through the whole foot until the legs are extended without snapping the knees straight.
Return under control and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
formCues: Use only as narrow a stance as lets the knees track comfortably over the toes.
Keep the heels down and avoid letting the knees collapse inward as the sled descends.
Do not trade pelvic position for depth; stop before the lower back starts to round off the pad.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Cobra Stretch
description: A prone backbend that stretches the abdominals and front of the torso by lifting the chest.
instructions: Lie face down with your hands under your shoulders.
Press through your hands to lift your chest off the floor.
Keep your hips and legs on the floor, shoulders relaxed.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
formCues: Keep your elbows slightly bent — do not force full extension.
Draw your shoulders down away from your ears.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Concentration Curl
description: An isolation curl performed seated for peak bicep contraction.
instructions: Sit on a bench with legs spread, holding a dumbbell in one hand.
Brace your elbow against the inside of your thigh.
Curl the dumbbell up toward your shoulder.
Lower with control.
Repeat on both sides.
formCues: Keep your upper arm vertical and let only the forearm move.
Avoid swinging your torso to help the weight up.
Match the reps on each arm to avoid muscle imbalances.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Copenhagen Plank
description: A demanding side plank in which the top leg rests on a flat bench and the lower leg is held off the floor. The inner thigh muscles of the top leg and the obliques hold the body in a straight line, which makes it a classic exercise for the adductors and the trunk.
instructions: Lie on your side next to a flat bench and place your top leg on it, with the inside of the foot or the lower part of the leg resting on the bench.
Prop yourself up on the elbow of your lower arm, directly under your shoulder.
Lift your hips so that your body forms a straight line from your head to your top foot, and let the lower leg hang or lift it toward the bench.
Keep your hips high and your trunk steady, and breathe evenly.
Hold for the planned time, then lower your hips back to the floor.
Rest, then switch sides.
formCues: Start with the top knee on the bench and a short lever; move the foot of the top leg onto the bench only when the hold feels easy.
Press your forearm into the floor and keep your shoulder away from your ear.
Stop if you feel a sharp pull in the groin; the adductors need a gentle build-up.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Copenhagen Plank Raises
description: A dynamic version of the Copenhagen plank: you hold a side plank with the top leg resting on a flat bench and lift the lower leg up to meet it, then lower it again. The inner thigh muscles of both legs and the obliques work together, and the movement is demanding for the adductors.
instructions: Lie on your side next to a flat bench and place your top leg on it, with the knee or the inner foot resting on the bench.
Prop yourself up on the elbow of your lower arm, directly under the shoulder.
Lift your hips so that your body forms a straight line from your head to your top foot, with the lower leg hanging underneath.
Raise the lower leg up toward the bench until it nearly touches the top leg, keeping your hips high.
Lower the lower leg slowly without letting your hips drop, and repeat for the planned repetitions.
Rest, then switch sides.
formCues: Start with the top knee on the bench and a short lever; move the foot of the top leg onto the bench only when the raises feel easy.
Keep your hips high and your body in one line; dropping the hips takes the load off the inner thighs.
Move slowly and stop if you feel a sharp pull in the groin; the adductors need a gentle build-up.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Cossack Squat
description: A wide-stance lateral squat that sinks the body deep over one bent leg while the other stays straight, training single-leg strength, hip mobility, and adductor flexibility.
instructions: Stand in a wide stance with toes turned slightly out.
Shift your weight to one side, bending that knee and sinking into a deep squat.
Keep the trailing leg straight with the heel down and toes up.
Sink as low as your mobility allows, keeping the chest tall.
Drive through the bent leg back to center, then repeat to the other side.
formCues: Keep the working heel planted -- do not roll onto the toes.
Point the straight leg's toes up to keep tension in the adductors.
