Placing the feet higher on the platform shifts emphasis to the glutes and hamstrings.
Control the descent; do not bounce out of the bottom position.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Hack Squat Calf Raise
alternativeNames: Elevación de Talones en Máquina Hack Squat
description: A calf raise performed in the hack squat machine, loading the calves heavily without balancing a bar.
instructions: Load yourself into a hack squat machine with shoulders under the pads.
Place the balls of your feet on the platform with heels hanging off.
Keep your legs straight with a slight knee bend.
Press through the balls of your feet to raise your heels.
Lower your heels back below the platform for a stretch.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
formCues: Rise as high onto the balls of your feet as possible.
Pause in the bottom stretch instead of bouncing out of it.
Keep your knees straight but not locked to keep tension on the calves.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Half-Kneeling Hip Flexor Rock
alternativeNames: Balanceo de Flexor de Cadera en Media Rodilla
description: The dynamic version of the kneeling hip-flexor stretch: from a half-kneeling stance the hips rock forward into the stretch and back out of it, repeated instead of held.
instructions: Kneel on one knee with the other foot flat on the floor in front of you.
Tuck the tailbone slightly and brace the trunk so the lower back stays neutral.
Rock the hips forward until you feel the front of the back thigh lengthen.
Rock back out of the position under control and repeat rhythmically.
Switch sides and repeat for the same number of repetitions.
formCues: Keep the movement in the hips; if the lower back arches, shorten the range.
Squeeze the glute of the kneeling leg during the forward rock.
Pad the down knee with a folded mat if the floor is hard.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Half Moon Pose
description: A standing side balance on one leg and one hand, with the top leg lifted to hip height and the chest turned open towards the ceiling.
instructions: From a wide standing stance, bend the front knee and place the bottom hand on the floor or a block ahead of the front foot.
Shift the weight forward and lift the back leg until it is parallel to the floor.
Straighten the standing leg and stack the top hip over the bottom one, reaching the top arm to the ceiling.
Hold the balance for the prescribed time with the lifted foot flexed.
Lower the back foot down and repeat on the other side.
formCues: Use a block under the bottom hand; reaching the floor is not the point of the pose.
Press the lifted heel towards the wall behind you to keep the leg switched on.
Look at the floor instead of up if the balance keeps breaking.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Handstand Hold
description: A freestanding static hold balanced upside down on the hands with the body stacked in a straight line. It builds shoulder strength, wrist and trunk stability and balance.
instructions: Place the hands about shoulder-width apart on the floor and kick up into an inverted position, one leg after the other.
Press tall through the shoulders and keep the arms locked.
Squeeze the glutes and abdominals so the body forms one straight line from the hands to the toes.
Keep the gaze between the hands and hold the position, making small corrections with the fingers.
Come down under control, one leg at a time, or step out of the hold.
formCues: Practise against a wall until you can hold the line without leaning on it.
Push the floor away so the shoulders stay elevated, and pull the ribs in to avoid arching the back.
Warm up the wrists before holding.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Handstand Push Ups
description: An inverted press in a freestanding handstand on parallettes, lowering the head between the handles and pressing back up to straight arms.
instructions: Set two parallettes shoulder-width apart and kick up into a freestanding handstand on them.
Brace your core and keep your body straight, legs together.
Bend your elbows to lower your head between the handles.
Go down until your head is about level with the handles.
Press through the handles back to straight arms, keeping your balance.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
formCues: Lower under control instead of dropping into the bottom position.
Keep the ribs down and the body stacked over the hands so the back does not arch.
Learn it against a wall and through pike push-ups before going freestanding.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Hang Clean
description: A clean variation starting with the barbell at the thighs, training explosive triple extension and a fast catch.
instructions: Stand holding a barbell with a shoulder-width grip at your thighs.
Hinge at the hips to lower the bar just above your knees.
Explosively extend your hips, knees, and ankles.
Shrug your shoulders and pull the bar up.
Pull yourself under the bar and catch it on your front shoulders in a full squat.
Stand up tall, then return to the hang position.
formCues: Hinge to just above the knees before exploding upward.
Shrug and pull the bar up close to your body.
Catch the bar on your shoulders as you sit into the squat.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Hang Power Clean
description: A clean from the hang caught in a partial squat, building explosive power without dropping into a full squat.
instructions: Stand with feet hip-width apart holding a barbell at your thighs.
Hinge at the hips to lower the bar to just above the knees.
Drive through your hips and legs explosively.
Pull the bar up and catch it on your front shoulders in a partial squat.
Stand tall with the bar racked on your shoulders.
Lower the bar back to the hang position.
formCues: Drive through your hips and legs before the arms pull.
Receive the bar with your thighs above parallel.
Keep your back flat as you hinge to the start position.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Hang Snatch
description: An Olympic lift in which a barbell is pulled from the hang position, just above the knees, to overhead in one explosive movement and caught in a squat. It builds power through the hips, back and shoulders.
instructions: Stand with a wide snatch grip on a barbell held at the thighs and the feet about hip-width apart.
Hinge at the hips to lower the bar to just above the knees, keeping the back flat and the shoulders over the bar.
Explosively extend the hips, knees and ankles, shrugging as the bar rises.
Pull yourself under the bar and catch it overhead with locked arms in a squat.
Stand up fully with the bar overhead and stable.
Lower the bar under control back to the thighs and reset.
formCues: Keep the bar close to the body throughout the pull.
Finish the pull with full extension before dropping under the bar.
Learn the movement with a light bar or a dowel; the wide overhead catch needs good shoulder and hip mobility.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Hanging Knee Raise
description: A hanging core exercise on a pull-up bar that targets the lower abs and hip flexors with bent knees.
instructions: Hang from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip, arms fully extended.
Engage your core and raise your knees toward your chest.
Hold briefly at the top.
Lower your legs slowly back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired reps.
formCues: Avoid swinging — initiate the movement from your core.
Exhale as you raise your knees.
Progress to straight-leg raises when this feels easy.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Hanging L-Sit
description: A static core hold hanging from a bar with the legs extended straight in front of the body at hip height, forming an L shape. It demands strong abdominals, hip flexors and grip.
instructions: Hang from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip, arms straight and the shoulders pulled down.
Brace the abdominals and lift the straight legs until they are parallel to the floor.
Keep the knees locked and the toes pointed, with the legs together.
Hold the position without swinging, breathing steadily.
Lower the legs under control to a dead hang.
formCues: If the legs drop below parallel, bend the knees (a tuck hold) and build up from there.
Keep the shoulders active; do not hang passively from the joints.
Squeeze the legs together and point the toes to keep the line tight.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Hanging Tuck Hold
description: A static core hold hanging from a bar with the knees pulled up toward the chest. It trains the abdominals and hip flexors and is a step toward the hanging L-sit.
instructions: Hang from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip and the arms straight.
Brace the abdominals and pull the knees up toward the chest, rounding the lower back slightly.
Keep the knees together and the thighs at or above hip height.
Hold the tucked position without swinging and breathe steadily.
Lower the legs under control to a full hang.
formCues: Curl the pelvis up rather than just lifting the knees; the abdominals should do the work.
Keep the shoulders pulled away from the ears.
End the set when the knees start to drop or the body starts to swing.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Happy Baby Pose
description: A supine hip opener in which the knees are drawn towards the armpits and the feet are held from the outside, releasing the inner thighs and lower back.
instructions: Lie on your back and draw both knees towards the chest.
Take hold of the outside edges of the feet, or the shins if the feet are out of reach.
Open the knees wider than the ribs and stack the ankles above the knees, soles facing up.
Press the feet gently into the hands and hold for the prescribed time with the lower back on the floor.
Release the feet and lower the legs.
formCues: Keep the tailbone heavy on the floor rather than rolling onto the upper back.
Hold the shins or use a strap around the feet if the grip forces the shoulders off the mat.
Rock gently side to side to massage the lower back if it feels tight.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Head-to-Knee Pose
alternativeNames: Postura de Cabeza a la Rodilla
description: A seated one-legged fold: one leg stays straight while the other foot rests against the inner thigh, so the hamstring of the straight leg lengthens one side at a time.
instructions: Sit with one leg straight in front of you and the other knee bent out to the side, that foot at the inner thigh.
Turn the chest towards the straight leg so the navel lines up with the thigh.
Hinge from the hips and reach forward along the straight leg with a long spine.
Hold the fold for the prescribed time, breathing into the back of the leg.
Come up with a flat back and repeat on the other side.
formCues: Sit on a folded blanket so the pelvis can tip forward instead of the back rounding.
Keep the toes of the straight leg pointing up rather than rolling out.
Use a strap around the foot when the hands do not reach it comfortably.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Heel-Elevated Squat
description: A squat variation with heels raised on plates or a wedge to shift emphasis onto the quadriceps and improve depth.
instructions: Place weight plates or a wedge under your heels, feet shoulder-width apart.
Hold a barbell across your upper back or hold dumbbells at your sides.
Brace your core and descend into a squat, keeping your torso upright.
Squat until thighs are parallel to the floor or lower.
Drive through your feet to return to the starting position.
formCues: The elevated heels allow a more upright torso and greater knee travel.
Keep your knees tracking over your toes throughout.
Start with a small heel elevation and increase as mobility improves.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Heel Flicks
description: A running warm-up drill that alternates the heels towards the glutes, raising the cadence while dynamically flexing the knees and preparing the hamstrings.
instructions: Stand tall with the feet under the hips and the arms bent as for running.
Begin jogging lightly in place.
Flick one heel up towards the same-side glute without driving the knee forward.
Switch feet quickly and continue alternating at an even rhythm.
Stay light on the forefeet and keep the torso upright for the full interval.
formCues: Aim for quick relaxed contacts rather than forcing the heel into the glute.
Keep the knees pointing down instead of lifting them like high knees.
Start slowly and increase cadence only after the rhythm feels smooth.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Heel-to-Toe Walk
description: A balance and coordination drill walked along an imaginary line, placing the heel of each step directly against the toes of the other foot so the base of support narrows to almost nothing.
instructions: Pick a straight line on the floor and stand on it with your arms out to your sides at shoulder height.
Step forward and place your heel directly in front of — and touching — the toes of the standing foot.
Shift your weight onto the front foot under control, pausing for a moment before the next step.
Bring the back foot through and place it heel to toe again, staying on the line rather than stepping around it.
Look ahead at a fixed point instead of down at your feet, and use your arms to correct any wobble.
Walk the desired number of steps, then turn around and walk back.
formCues: Go slowly. Rushing turns it into ordinary walking on a narrow line and removes the balance demand entirely.
If you cannot hold the line, walk beside a wall and touch it only when you need it — that is a regression, not a failure.
Make it harder by folding your arms across your chest, and harder again by doing it with your eyes closed near a wall.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Heel Touches
description: A lying core exercise in which you crunch slightly to one side and reach the hand toward the heel, then alternate sides. It trains the obliques and the upper abdominals with the lower back kept on the floor.
instructions: Lie on your back with the knees bent and the feet flat on the floor, about hip-width apart.
Lift the head and shoulders slightly off the floor and reach the arms down along your sides.
Crunch to one side and reach that hand toward the heel on the same side.
Return to the center and reach toward the opposite heel.
Keep alternating sides in a smooth rhythm while the lower back stays on the floor.
Continue for the desired number of repetitions.
formCues: Keep the neck long and the chin off the chest; lead with the ribcage, not the head.
Keep each reach small and controlled; the shoulder blades only just clear the floor.
Keep the feet planted and the lower back pressed into the floor throughout.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Hero Pose
description: A kneeling seat with the hips settling between the heels, which lengthens the quadriceps and the front of the ankles while the spine stays tall.
instructions: Kneel with the knees together and the feet slightly wider than the hips, tops of the feet flat.
Sit the hips back and down between the heels, using a block or cushion if the floor is out of reach.
Stack the ribs over the pelvis and rest the hands on the thighs.
Hold the seat for the prescribed time, keeping the weight even on both sit bones.
Come out by pressing into the hands and straightening one leg at a time.
formCues: Sit on a block whenever the knees complain; the height is a normal part of the pose.
Roll a towel under the ankles if the front of them feels strained.
Keep the feet pointing straight back rather than flaring out to the sides.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Hex Bar Deadlift
description: A deadlift standing inside a hex (trap) bar, keeping the load centered for a more upright, back-friendly pull.
instructions: Stand inside a loaded trap bar with feet shoulder-width apart.
Hinge at the hips and knees to grip the handles.
Brace your core and set your back flat.
Drive through your heels and extend hips and knees to stand up.
Lock out at the top with shoulders pulled back.
Lower the bar back to the floor under control.
formCues: Keep your chest up and back flat as you set your grip.
Push the floor away rather than yanking the bar with your back.
Stand fully upright at the top without leaning back.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: High-Foot Leg Press
alternativeNames: Prensa de piernas con pies altos
description: A leg press with the feet placed high on the platform, shifting more of the movement toward hip extension and the gluteus maximus while the back stays supported.
instructions: Set the back pad and seat so your lower back stays supported and your knees can bend without your pelvis rolling under.
Place both feet high on the platform at about shoulder width, with the toes tracking in the same direction as the knees.
Lower the sled by bending the hips and knees until you reach a comfortable depth without the lower back lifting from the pad.
Press through the whole foot and extend the hips and knees without locking the knees aggressively.
Lower the sled under control and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
formCues: Keep the pelvis heavy against the pad; a high foot position does not justify rounding the lower back at the bottom.
Keep the heels and the whole foot planted rather than letting the toes carry the sled.
Use a depth that preserves pelvic position instead of chasing a deeper range with a tucked pelvis.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: High Knees
description: A bodyweight cardio drill where the knees are driven up to hip height in rapid alternation.
instructions: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart.
Drive one knee up toward the chest while pumping the opposite arm.
Quickly switch legs, mirroring the arm action.
Continue alternating at a fast pace.
Continue for the prescribed work interval.
formCues: Drive the knees up to at least hip height.
Stay light on the balls of the feet.
Keep the torso upright — do not lean back.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: High Plank
description: A plank variation with arms fully extended in a push-up position.
instructions: Start in a push-up position with arms fully extended.
Keep your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Brace your core and hold the position.
Breathe steadily throughout.
formCues: Stack your shoulders directly above your wrists.
Squeeze your glutes to keep your hips from sagging.
Push the floor away to avoid sinking between your shoulder blades.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Machine Hip Abduction
description: A machine exercise targeting the outer hip muscles.
instructions: Sit in the hip abduction machine with pads against your outer thighs.
Push your legs apart against the resistance.
Hold briefly at the widest point.
Return to the starting position with control.
Repeat.
formCues: Sit tall and keep your back against the pad.
Don't let the weight stack slam down between reps.
Choose a resistance that allows a full range of motion.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Hip Adduction
description: A machine exercise pressing the legs together against resistance, isolating and strengthening the inner-thigh adductors.
instructions: Sit on the hip adduction machine with your back against the pad.
Place your legs against the pads with the machine set to a comfortable stretch.
Squeeze your legs together until the pads meet in the middle.
Hold the squeeze briefly in the fully closed position.
Let your legs open back out under control to the start.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
formCues: Choose a start width that stretches without straining your groin.
Move through the whole range at an even, controlled speed.
Do not let the weight stack slam down as your legs open back out.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Barbell Hip Thrust
description: A compound glute exercise using a barbell across the hips.
instructions: Sit on the floor with your upper back against a bench, barbell across your hips.
Drive your hips up until your thighs are parallel to the floor.
Squeeze your glutes at the top.
Lower your hips back down with control.
Repeat.
formCues: Tuck your chin and keep your ribs down at the top.
Finish with your shins vertical, driving through your heels.
Reach full hip extension without arching your lower back.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Hollow Body Hold
description: An isometric core hold borrowed from gymnastics, training total-body tension with the spine in a slight C-shape.
instructions: Lie on your back with arms extended overhead and legs straight.
Press the lower back firmly into the floor.
Lift the shoulders, head, and legs slightly off the floor.
Hold the position with arms and legs extended, body in a shallow banana shape.
Hold for the prescribed time.
formCues: Keep the lower back glued to the floor — if it lifts, raise the legs higher.
Tuck the chin slightly to engage the upper abs.
Bend the knees to scale if the position breaks.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Horizontal Leg Press
description: A machine leg press performed horizontally, targeting quads, glutes, and hamstrings.
instructions: Sit in a horizontal leg press with your back against the pad and your feet shoulder-width apart on the footplate.
Press through your feet to straighten your legs, stopping just short of locking the knees.
Bend your knees under control until they come toward your chest.
Repeat.
formCues: Do not let your lower back lift off the seat.
Avoid locking out the knees completely.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Human Flag
description: An advanced calisthenics isometric hold with the body horizontal on a vertical pole, parallel to the ground.
instructions: Stand close to a sturdy vertical pole.
Grip the pole high with the top hand (overhand) and lower with the bottom hand (underhand).
Kick the legs up and out while pressing the bottom arm hard against the pole.
Extend the body horizontally so it forms a straight line parallel to the ground.
Hold the position with the body rigid for the target time.
Lower under control.
formCues: Build up to the full flag with tucked and straddle progressions first.
The bottom arm pushes; the top arm pulls — they balance the lever.
Engage the lats, obliques, and glutes hard to stay rigid.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Hyperextension Bench Hold
description: An isometric hold on a hyperextension bench: you lift your torso until your body forms one straight line from the heels to the head and hold it there. The erector spinae and the glutes stay under tension without the swinging of the dynamic back extension.
instructions: Adjust the bench so that the pad sits just below your hip bones and your heels are hooked firmly behind the roller or pad.
Cross your arms over your chest and lower your torso toward the floor with a straight back.
Raise your torso until your body is in one straight line from your head to your heels.
Stop in that line and hold, with your glutes squeezed and your neck in line with your spine.
Keep your breathing slow and do not arch your lower back past the straight line while you hold for the planned time.
Lower your torso under control and rest.
formCues: Stop at a straight line; leaning back past it hands the work to your lower back joints instead of the muscles.
Squeeze the glutes during the whole hold, so that the hips stay extended and the lower back is not doing the job alone.
Hold a weight plate against your chest only after you can hold bodyweight for a full minute.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Incline EZ-Bar Bench Press
alternativeNames: Press en banco inclinado con barra Z
description: An incline press with an EZ-bar targeting the upper chest with a joint-friendly grip.
instructions: Set bench to 30–45 degrees. Grip the EZ-bar with hands on the angled sections.
Lower the bar to your upper chest.
Press back up to full extension.
Repeat.
formCues: The incline shifts emphasis to the upper pectorals.
Control the descent to avoid shoulder strain.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Incline Barbell Bench Press
alternativeNames: Press en banco inclinado con barra
description: A barbell pressing movement on an incline bench targeting the upper chest.
instructions: Lie on an incline bench set to 30-45 degrees.
Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width and unrack.
Lower the bar to your upper chest.
Press the bar back up to full extension.
Repeat.
formCues: Keep your shoulder blades pinched together against the bench.
Lower the bar without bouncing it off your chest.
Keep your feet planted and your glutes on the bench.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Incline Dumbbell Curl
alternativeNames: Curl con mancuernas en banco inclinado
description: A bicep curl on an incline bench for a deeper stretch of the long head.
instructions: Sit on an incline bench set to 45 degrees, holding dumbbells at your sides.
Let your arms hang straight down with palms forward.
Curl the dumbbells up toward your shoulders.
Lower with control to full extension.
Repeat.
formCues: Keep your head and shoulders against the bench throughout.
Don't let your elbows drift forward as you curl.
Avoid shrugging your shoulders forward as you lift the weight.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Incline Dumbbell Press
alternativeNames: Press con mancuernas en banco inclinado
description: An incline pressing movement emphasizing the upper chest.
instructions: Set bench to 30-degree incline and sit back with dumbbells at shoulder level.
Press dumbbells up and together until arms are fully extended.
Lower dumbbells back to shoulder level with control.
Repeat.
formCues: Keep your wrists stacked directly over your elbows.
Press up without banging the dumbbells together at the top.
Keep your shoulder blades pulled back against the bench.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Incline Dumbbell Fly
alternativeNames: Apertura con mancuernas en banco inclinado
description: An incline isolation exercise opening dumbbells in a wide arc, stretching and targeting the upper chest.
instructions: Lie back on an incline bench holding dumbbells above your chest.
Press the dumbbells up with palms facing each other.
Maintain a slight bend in your elbows throughout.
Lower the dumbbells in a wide arc until you feel a chest stretch.
Squeeze your chest to bring the dumbbells back together.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
formCues: Keep a fixed slight bend in your elbows throughout.
Lower only as far as a comfortable chest stretch allows.
Squeeze your chest to bring the dumbbells back together.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Incline Hammer Curl
description: A hammer curl performed on an incline bench for increased stretch and biceps long-head activation.
instructions: Sit on an incline bench holding dumbbells with a neutral grip.
Allow arms to hang straight.
Curl the dumbbells up in a hammer motion.
Lower slowly.
Repeat.
formCues: The incline provides a greater stretch.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Incline Plank Hold
description: An easier version of the plank: with your forearms resting on a flat bench and your feet on the floor, you hold your body in a straight line from head to heels. The raised hands reduce the load on the shoulders and make it a good starting point for the full plank.
instructions: Place your forearms on a flat bench, with your elbows directly under your shoulders.
Step your feet back until your body forms a straight line from head to heels.
Squeeze your glutes and pull your belly button toward your spine to keep your hips level.
Keep your neck long and look at a point on the bench slightly ahead of your hands.
Hold the position for the planned time while breathing steadily.
Step your feet in to finish.
formCues: Do not let your hips sag toward the bench or pike up; your body should stay in one straight line.
Press your forearms into the bench and push the bench away to keep your shoulder blades wide.
Step your feet further back to make it harder, or closer to make it easier; make sure the bench cannot slide.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Incline Treadmill Walk
description: A steady uphill walk on an inclined treadmill belt, keeping one foot in contact with the belt throughout so the glutes and hamstrings work hard with almost no impact.
instructions: Start the belt at a slow walking speed and step on, then raise the incline to your target gradient.
Walk with a long, deliberate stride, rolling from heel to toe and pushing the belt away behind you with each step.
Stand tall and lean from the ankles with the hill rather than folding forward at the waist.
Keep at least one foot on the belt at all times — walk the hill, do not break into a jog.
Let your arms swing naturally, or rest them lightly on the rails for balance without carrying your weight on them.
Hold the gradient for the desired time, then lower the incline and walk level for a few minutes to finish.
formCues: Pick a speed you can still walk at. As soon as you need a flight phase to keep up, drop the speed or the incline — it is a walk, not a run.
Hanging your bodyweight off the handrails removes most of the work the hill is there to create; touch them for balance only.
The steep grade is what moves the effort from the quads into the glutes and hamstrings, so raise the incline before you raise the speed.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Isometric Neck Lateral Flexion
description: A static side-neck drill using the hand as resistance against the head, training the sternocleidomastoid and scalene without hardware.
instructions: Sit or stand tall. Place the palm of one hand against the side of the head, above the ear.
Press the head into the hand while resisting equally with the hand — the head does not move.
Hold the isometric contraction for 5 to 10 seconds.
Release slowly, then repeat on the same side for the set.
Switch sides and repeat.
formCues: Match the pressure; this is 50% effort, not a wrestling match.
Keep the jaw relaxed and the shoulders down.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Isometric Split Squat
description: A held version of the split squat: you stand in a long lunge stance and stay in the bottom position with your front thigh near parallel to the floor. The continuous tension builds strength and control in the quadriceps and glutes of the front leg.
instructions: Stand with one foot well forward and the other foot back, about a long stride apart, with your hands on your hips.
Keep your torso upright and lower straight down by bending both knees.
Lower until your front thigh is close to parallel with the floor and your back knee hovers just above the ground.
Keep your front heel flat and your front knee tracking over your toes.
Hold this position for the planned time, keeping your trunk tall and your weight spread through the front foot.
Press up to the top, then repeat on the other leg.
formCues: Keep the back knee just off the floor so the front leg keeps working the whole time.
Do not let the front knee cave inward; push it gently over the middle toes.
Hold a lighter position higher up if the bottom is too intense; the quads should burn, not the knee joint.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Jefferson Curl
description: A loaded spinal-flexion drill: standing tall with a light weight, you round the spine one vertebra at a time and restack it, building segmental control and hamstring/spinal-erector flexibility under load.
instructions: Stand tall holding a light dumbbell with straight arms, feet roughly hip-width.
Tuck your chin and begin rounding the spine from the top, one vertebra at a time.
Curl down slowly, letting the weight hang and keeping the legs mostly straight.
Reach the bottom with the back fully rounded and a stretch through the hamstrings.
Reverse it, restacking the spine from the bottom up back to standing.
formCues: Use a very light weight -- this is a controlled mobility drill, not a heavy lift.
Round segment by segment; do not hinge at the hips like a stiff-leg deadlift.
Move slowly and never bounce at the bottom.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Jumping Jacks
description: This classic full-body dynamic exercise elevates heart rate and targets the calves, shoulders, quads, and glutes, making it an excellent warm-up or conditioning movement.
instructions: Stand tall with feet together and arms at your sides.
Simultaneously jump your feet out wide and raise your arms overhead.
Ensure your arms meet or nearly meet above your head.
Jump your feet back together while lowering your arms to your sides.
Maintain a continuous, rhythmic motion.
formCues: Land softly on the balls of your feet to absorb impact.
Keep your core engaged throughout the movement.
Control your breathing; inhale as you jump out, exhale as you jump in.
Increase speed for a greater cardiovascular challenge.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Kettlebell Step-Up to Balance
alternativeNames: Step-Up con Equilibrio y Pesas Rusas
description: A loaded version of the step-up to balance: holding a kettlebell in each hand, you step onto a low platform, drive the free knee up in front of you and stand tall on the working leg before stepping back down. The quadriceps and glutes lift the body and the weights while the hips and ankle keep you steady.
instructions: Stand facing a low, stable step or bench with a kettlebell in each hand, arms hanging at your sides.
Place one foot flat on top of the step.
Press through the whole of the front foot and straighten that leg to lift your body onto the step.
As you rise, drive the other knee up in front of you until the thigh is about hip height.
Stand tall on the working leg and hold the knee-up position for a moment without leaning back.
Lower the free foot back to the floor under control, then step the working leg down as well and repeat; switch legs after the planned repetitions.
formCues: Keep the weights hanging at your sides and still; swinging them or pulling them up with your arms takes the work away from the legs.
Keep your trunk upright and your hips level during the balance hold rather than tilting toward the lifted knee.
Start with light weights and a low step; add load only when you can hold the balance position without wobbling.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Kettlebell Bottoms-Up Hold
alternativeNames: Sostén con Pesa Rusa Boca Abajo
description: A one-arm hold in which the kettlebell is held upside down by the handle at shoulder height, with the bell above your hand. Keeping the bell level demands a very firm grip and constant work from the forearm and the shoulder, which makes this a strong test of wrist and shoulder stability.
instructions: Clean a kettlebell to your shoulder and flip it so that the bell points up and the handle sits in your fist.
Stand with your feet about shoulder-width apart and your free arm relaxed at your side.
Keep your forearm vertical and your elbow close to your ribs, with the bell directly above your hand.
Grip the handle firmly and keep your wrist straight, as if you were balancing a cup.
Hold the bell steady for the planned time, breathing slowly and keeping your shoulder down.
Lower the kettlebell with control, turn it the right way up and switch arms.
formCues: Start with a very light bell; a weight that feels easy when held the normal way can be hard to keep level.
Keep the shoulder down and the wrist stacked over the forearm; if the bell tips, reset the position before it falls.
Stand in a clear space, away from people and furniture, in case the bell tips.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Kettlebell Bulgarian Split Squat
description: This unilateral squat variation builds lower body strength, muscle, and stability by elevating the rear foot and holding a kettlebell in each hand, primarily targeting the quadriceps and glutes.
instructions: Stand facing away from a bench, placing one foot on it behind you, laces down. Hold a kettlebell in each hand at your sides.
Maintain an upright torso and engage your core.
Lower your body by bending both knees, allowing your front knee to track over your toes.
Descend until your front thigh is parallel to the floor or slightly below, keeping your rear knee close to the ground.
Drive through your front heel to return to the starting position, extending your hips and knees.
Complete all reps per side before switching.
formCues: Ensure your front foot is far enough from the bench to allow a full range of motion without discomfort.
Keep your torso upright throughout the movement to maximize glute and quad engagement.
Control the eccentric (lowering) phase to build strength and stability.
With only one kettlebell, hold it in the hand opposite the front leg for an extra balance challenge.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Kettlebell Close-Grip Floor Press
alternativeNames: Press de Suelo con Agarre Cerrado con Pesa Rusa
description: A floor press performed with a single kettlebell gripped close together with both hands. The narrow grip and the floor stop on the elbows shift emphasis off the chest and onto the triceps, with no shoulder hyperextension.
instructions: Lie on your back on the floor with the knees bent and feet flat.
Hold a single kettlebell by the handle with both hands, close together, the bell resting on the chest with elbows tucked tight to the ribs.
Brace the core and press the kettlebell straight up until the arms are fully extended.
Lower under control until the upper arms touch the floor and pause briefly.
Press back up to lockout.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.
formCues: Keep the elbows tucked at roughly 30–45 degrees from the torso — wide elbows turn it into a chest press.
The brief pause when the elbows touch the floor kills the bounce and forces a clean concentric.
Pick a bell you can control with two hands; the narrow grip is unforgiving if it tips.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Kettlebell Concentration Curl
description: A seated single-arm bicep isolation move: the elbow braces against the inner thigh while curling a kettlebell, keeping the upper arm still so the bicep does all the work.
instructions: Sit on a bench with your feet wide, holding a kettlebell in one hand.
Brace the back of your upper arm against the inside of your thigh, letting the kettlebell hang.
Curl the kettlebell up toward your shoulder, keeping the elbow pinned against your leg.
Squeeze the bicep at the top, then lower slowly under control.
Finish all reps on one side, then switch arms.
formCues: Keep the upper arm braced and still -- only the forearm moves.
Rotate the wrist slightly as you curl for a stronger peak contraction.
Use a lighter weight than a standard curl -- strict form matters more here.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Kettlebell Curl
description: A biceps curl with one kettlebell held by the handle in both hands. The kettlebell hangs in front of your thighs and you curl it up toward your chest, keeping the elbows close to your sides; sharing the load between two hands makes it an easy way to start training the biceps.
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder-width apart and hold the kettlebell by its handle with both hands, so it hangs in front of your thighs.
Keep your elbows close to your sides, your chest tall and your shoulders relaxed.
Bend your elbows and curl the kettlebell up toward your chest without letting your upper arms swing forward.
Squeeze your biceps at the top, with the kettlebell close to your chest.
Lower the kettlebell slowly until your arms are straight again, keeping control of the swing of the bell.
Repeat for the planned repetitions.
formCues: Hold the handle firmly with both hands and keep your wrists straight, so the kettlebell does not roll or tilt.
Do not lean back or swing your hips to lift the kettlebell; if you have to, the weight is too heavy.
Take about twice as long to lower the kettlebell as to lift it, so the biceps work through the whole descent.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Kettlebell Curl Iso Hold
description: An isometric version of the kettlebell curl: you curl a kettlebell held by the handle in both hands until your forearms are level with the floor and hold it there. The biceps and the brachialis stay under constant tension at the point where the lift is hardest.
instructions: Stand with your feet about shoulder-width apart and hold the kettlebell by its handle with both hands, so it hangs in front of your thighs.
Keep your elbows close to your sides and your shoulders relaxed.
Curl the kettlebell up until your forearms are level with the floor and the elbows are bent to about 90 degrees.
Stop there and hold the kettlebell steady, hanging in front of your body.
Keep your upper arms still, your chest tall and your breathing slow while you hold for the planned time.
Lower the kettlebell under control and rest.
formCues: Keep the kettlebell steady; swaying or letting it drop toward your thighs takes the load off the biceps.
Do not lean back to hold the weight; your trunk stays upright and your elbows stay close to your sides.
Choose a lighter kettlebell than for the curl itself, since the hold is hard at the halfway point.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Kettlebell Farmer's Walk
alternativeNames: Paseo del Granjero con Pesa Rusa
description: A loaded carry with heavy kettlebells at the sides, building grip strength and full-body stability.
instructions: Stand between two heavy kettlebells.
Hinge and grip the handles firmly with a neutral grip.
Stand tall with shoulders back and core braced.
Walk forward with short, controlled steps.
Maintain an upright posture throughout the walk.
Set the weights down at the end of the distance.
formCues: Keep your shoulders level and avoid leaning to either side.
Breathe steadily rather than holding your breath under load.
If your grip fails, set the weights down away from your feet.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Kettlebell Floor Press
alternativeNames: Press de suelo con pesas rusas
description: A two-arm chest press performed lying on the floor with a kettlebell in each hand. The floor caps the ROM (triceps hit the floor before full stretch), making it shoulder-friendly and a great home option.
instructions: Lie on your back on the floor with knees bent, feet flat.
Hold a kettlebell in each hand at the chest, bells resting on the outer forearms.
Press both kettlebells straight up until the arms are fully extended.
Lower under control until the triceps touch the floor — do not bounce.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.
formCues: Elbows stay about 45 degrees from the torso; do not flare.
The grip matters: keep the bells stable against the outside of the forearms.
The floor limits ROM by design — this is the feature, not the bug.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Kettlebell Goblet Lunge
description: This unilateral compound exercise strengthens the quadriceps, glutes, and hamstrings by performing a lunge while holding a kettlebell in the goblet position, improving lower body strength and stability.
instructions: Stand tall holding a kettlebell by its horns at chest height, elbows tucked, in the goblet position.
Take a controlled step forward with one leg, lowering your hips until both knees are bent at approximately 90 degrees.
Ensure your front knee is stacked over your ankle and your rear knee hovers just above the floor.
Drive through your front heel to return to the starting position, maintaining balance and core tension.
Complete all repetitions on one side before switching, or alternate legs per set.
formCues: Keep your chest upright and core braced throughout the movement to protect your spine and maintain stability.
Focus on a controlled descent and a powerful drive up, engaging your glutes and quads.
Avoid letting your front knee collapse inward; keep it aligned with your toes.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Kettlebell Halo
description: A shoulder-mobility drill where a kettlebell is circled around the head. Warms up the rotator cuff, thoracic spine, and shoulder girdle with minimal load.
instructions: Stand tall, core braced, holding a light kettlebell by the horns (upside down) at chest height.
Raise the bell to one side of your head and pass it around the back in a smooth circle.
Bring it back to the starting position in front of your face.
Reverse direction every few reps.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions or time.
formCues: Light weight only — this is mobility, not strength.
Keep the head stationary; the bell goes around, not the head.
If the bell drifts wide, shrink the circle — tight orbit, close to the skull.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Kettlebell Hammer Curl
description: A neutral-grip curl with a kettlebell in each hand, gripping the handles with the bells hanging below the hands. The offset mass and neutral grip bias the brachialis and brachioradialis.
instructions: Stand holding a kettlebell in each hand, gripping the handles in a neutral position (palms facing the body).
Let the bells hang below your hands.
Keep the elbows tucked to the sides and curl both bells up toward the shoulders.
Squeeze at the top, then lower under control.
Repeat for the planned number of reps.
formCues: Control the offset mass — the bells want to rotate at the bottom of the ROM.
Elbows stay still; only the forearms move.
Light load — this biases brachialis, not peak bicep size.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Kettlebell Hip Thrust
description: This exercise effectively targets the gluteus maximus and hamstrings, using a kettlebell to add resistance for powerful hip extension and glute development.
instructions: Sit on the floor with your upper back against a bench, knees bent, and feet flat.
Place a kettlebell across your hips, holding it securely with both hands.
Drive through your heels, lifting your hips off the floor until your body forms a straight line from shoulders to knees.
Squeeze your glutes forcefully at the top of the movement.
Slowly lower your hips back down to the starting position with control.
formCues: Keep your chin tucked towards your chest to maintain a neutral spine.
Focus on pushing through your heels to maximize glute activation.
Ensure your knees track in line with your toes throughout the movement.
Control the eccentric phase, resisting the weight as you lower your hips.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Kettlebell Kickstand Deadlift
description: A staggered-stance hip hinge with one kettlebell that loads the front leg while the back foot lightly stabilizes.
instructions: Set a kettlebell on the floor beside the front foot and step the other foot back so only its toes touch the floor.
Hinge at the hips with a flat back and grip the kettlebell handle with one hand.
Drive through the front heel and extend the hips to stand tall, the kettlebell at your side.
Keep most of your weight on the front foot throughout.
Hinge back down, lowering the kettlebell toward the floor with a flat back. Switch sides after all reps.
formCues: Keep the kettlebell close to the shin on the descent.
Stop at the point of hamstring stretch in the front leg.
Complete all reps on one side before switching.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Kettlebell Lunge Press
alternativeNames: Zancada con press de pesa rusa
description: A combination exercise pressing a kettlebell overhead with one arm while lunging, training legs, shoulders, and core.
instructions: Hold a kettlebell at shoulder height with one arm.
Step forward into a lunge with the opposite leg.
As you lunge, press the kettlebell overhead.
Lock out the arm at the top of the press.
Step back to standing while lowering the kettlebell.
Complete reps on one side, then switch.
formCues: Brace your core to resist leaning toward the loaded side.
Keep your front knee tracking in line with your toes.
Avoid arching your back as you lock out overhead.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Kettlebell Offset Reverse Lunge and Press
alternativeNames: Zancada inversa con press desequilibrado de pesa rusa
description: A reverse lunge with a single kettlebell pressed overhead, the offset load challenging balance and core stability.
instructions: Hold a kettlebell at shoulder height on one side.
Step backward into a reverse lunge with the opposite leg.
As you reach the bottom of the lunge, press the kettlebell overhead.
Drive through your front heel to return to standing.
Lower the kettlebell back to shoulder height.
Complete reps on one side, then switch.
formCues: Keep your hips square as you step back into the lunge.
Brace your trunk to resist bending toward the loaded side.
Lower your back knee with control instead of dropping into the bottom.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Kettlebell Overhead Carry
alternativeNames: Paseo con Kettlebell sobre la Cabeza
description: A loaded walk with a single kettlebell locked out overhead, where the bell hangs behind the wrist and pulls the arm backwards, making it harder to hold still than a dumbbell.
instructions: Clean and press a kettlebell to lockout, letting the bell settle on the back of your forearm.
Straighten the elbow fully and turn the arm so the bell sits behind and above your wrist rather than off to the side.
Keep the shoulder active: push the weight up toward the ceiling and let the shoulder blade rotate up with it rather than forcing it down.
Brace your trunk and walk forward with even strides, keeping the bell stacked over your shoulder and hip.
Keep your wrist straight; letting it bend back is what makes an overhead bell feel unstable.
Carry for the desired distance, lower under control, then repeat on the other side.
formCues: Go lighter than you would with a dumbbell. The offset mass makes the same weight noticeably harder to keep still.
A bent wrist is the usual failure point. If it keeps collapsing, drop the weight rather than fighting it for the whole distance.
Do both sides for the same distance — the unilateral load is the point of the exercise.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Kettlebell Overhead Hold
alternativeNames: Sostén con Pesa Rusa sobre la Cabeza
description: A one-arm isometric hold with the kettlebell locked out overhead. The shoulder, the upper back and the trunk work together to keep the bell steady over your head, which trains shoulder stability and the finish position of the press.
instructions: Clean or press a kettlebell up so that your arm is straight overhead with the bell resting against the back of your forearm.
Stand with your feet about shoulder-width apart and your free arm relaxed at your side.
Lock out your elbow and push your hand up toward the ceiling so that your upper arm stays next to your ear.
Squeeze your glutes and brace your core so that your ribs do not flare and your lower back stays neutral.
Hold the bell steady over your shoulder for the planned time, breathing slowly.
Lower the kettlebell back to the rack position with control and switch arms.
formCues: Keep the wrist straight and the bell over your shoulder joint; if it drifts forward, your shoulder will tire quickly.
Do not lean away from the bell; stay tall and let your trunk muscles hold you upright.
Start with a light kettlebell, since holding it overhead for time is a lot harder than pressing it once.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Kettlebell Overhead Tricep Extension
alternativeNames: Extensión de tríceps por encima de la cabeza con pesa rusa
description: An overhead tricep extension holding a kettlebell by the horns with both hands. The offset load pulls the bell behind the head for a deep long-head stretch.
instructions: Stand or sit holding a kettlebell by the horns (upside down) with both hands overhead.
Arms fully extended, bell above the head.
Bend only the elbows to lower the bell behind the head in a controlled arc.
Keep the upper arms vertical and close to the head; only the forearms move.
Extend the elbows to return the bell overhead.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.
formCues: Grip the horns firmly — the bell wants to rotate at the bottom.
Elbows stay narrow; if they flare, drop the load.
A seated version on a bench with a back rest is easier on the lumbar.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Kettlebell Pullover
description: A pullover on a flat bench with a kettlebell held by the horns. The deep overhead stretch hits the lats, long-head triceps, and serratus.
instructions: Lie on a flat bench holding a kettlebell by the horns with both hands above the chest, arms nearly straight (slight elbow bend).
Keeping the elbow angle fixed, lower the bell overhead in an arc until the upper arms are in line with the torso.
Pull the bell back above the chest along the same arc.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.
formCues: Keep the lower back pressed into the bench — do not arch to steal ROM.
Grip the horns hard; the bell will try to flip over at the bottom.
Go only as deep as your shoulder mobility allows without pain.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Kettlebell Rack Hold
alternativeNames: Sostén con Pesa Rusa en Posición de Rack
description: A one-arm hold with the kettlebell resting in the rack position, against your chest and the back of your forearm at the shoulder. The shoulder, the upper back and the trunk work to carry the bell comfortably, which is the starting position of the press, the squat and many other kettlebell lifts.
instructions: Clean a kettlebell to your shoulder so that the bell rests against the back of your forearm and your upper arm, with the handle in your palm.
Stand with your feet about shoulder-width apart and your free arm relaxed at your side.
Keep your elbow close to your ribs and your wrist straight, so that the bell sits on your chest and shoulder, not on your wrist.
Stand tall, squeeze your glutes and brace your core without leaning away from the bell.
Hold the position for the planned time, breathing slowly.
Lower the kettlebell to the floor with control and switch arms.
formCues: Let the bell rest on your forearm and chest rather than gripping it hard, so that your forearm does not tire first.
Keep the elbow tucked and the wrist straight; a bent wrist is the most common cause of a sore forearm.
Do not lean back or shift your hips sideways to counter the weight; stay tall.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Kettlebell Reverse Lunge
description: This compound unilateral exercise builds lower body strength and stability, primarily targeting the glutes and quads while engaging hamstrings, glute medius, and obliques.
instructions: Stand tall holding a kettlebell by the horns at your chest, elbows tucked in (goblet hold).
Step one leg straight back, lowering your hips until both knees are bent at approximately 90 degrees.
Keep your front shin vertical and your chest upright, ensuring your back knee hovers just above the floor.
Drive through your front heel to return to the starting position.
Complete all reps per side before switching to the other side.
formCues: Maintain a stable core throughout the movement to protect your spine.
Focus on a controlled descent and a powerful ascent.
Keep your front foot flat and distribute weight evenly through the heel and midfoot.
Avoid letting your front knee collapse inward; keep it tracking over your toes.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Kettlebell Reverse Wrist Curl
alternativeNames: Curl de Muñeca Inverso con Kettlebell
description: A reverse wrist curl holding one kettlebell by the handle with both hands, training the forearm extensors.
instructions: Sit on a bench with your forearms on your thighs, palms down.
Hold one kettlebell by the handle with both hands, with the wrists hanging off the knees.
Let the wrists drop, lowering the kettlebell.
Lift the backs of the hands by extending the wrists.
Lower under control and repeat for the planned reps.
formCues: Use a very light kettlebell — extensors fatigue quickly.
Hold the handle, not the bell.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Kettlebell Rotational Lunge
description: A reverse lunge holding a kettlebell at the chest, adding a torso rotation toward the front leg to work the legs and obliques together.
instructions: Hold a kettlebell with both hands at your chest.
Step back into a lunge, lowering until both knees are bent.
Rotate your torso toward the front leg.
Move the kettlebell to that side at chest to shoulder height, arms almost straight.
Rotate back to the center and push through the front foot to return to standing.
Complete reps on one side, then switch.
formCues: Keep the front knee over the ankle as you lower into the lunge.
Rotate from your torso and hips, not your knees.
Keep your chest tall as you rotate.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Kettlebell Russian Twist
description: A seated rotational core exercise twisting a kettlebell from side to side with the feet lifted.
instructions: Sit on the floor with your knees bent and feet lifted off the ground.
Hold a kettlebell with both hands in front of your chest.
Lean back slightly to engage your core.
Rotate your torso to one side, bringing the kettlebell next to your hip.
Rotate to the opposite side in a controlled motion.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
formCues: Rotate your whole torso, not just your arms.
Keep your spine tall instead of slumping as you twist.
Keep your legs still as your torso moves side to side.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Kettlebell Shrug
description: This isolation exercise targets the upper trapezius muscles by elevating the shoulders, enhancing shoulder stability and neck strength.
instructions: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart, holding a kettlebell in each hand with palms facing your body.
Keep your arms straight and shoulders relaxed.
Elevate your shoulders straight up towards your ears, squeezing your traps at the top.
Hold the contraction briefly.
Slowly lower your shoulders back to the starting position with control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
formCues: Focus on moving only your shoulders, keeping your arms straight throughout the movement.
Avoid rolling your shoulders; move them straight up and down.
Maintain a neutral spine and engaged core to prevent lower back strain.
Use a weight that allows for full range of motion and controlled execution.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Kettlebell Single Leg Deadlift
alternativeNames: Peso muerto a una pierna con pesa rusa
description: A single-leg hip hinge holding a kettlebell, training the hamstrings and glutes while challenging balance.
instructions: Hold a kettlebell in one hand and stand on the opposite leg.
Hinge at the hip and lower the kettlebell toward the floor.
Extend your free leg straight back for balance.
Lower until your torso is parallel to the floor.
Drive through your standing heel to return to standing.
Complete reps on one side, then switch.
formCues: Keep your hips square to the floor as you hinge.
Keep a soft bend in your standing knee.
Fix your eyes on one spot to steady your balance.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Kettlebell Skull Crusher
description: A skull crusher lying on the floor, holding a kettlebell by the horns with both hands. The offset mass hangs below the wrists, adding a grip and control challenge.
instructions: Lie on your back on the floor with your knees bent and feet flat, holding a kettlebell by the horns with both hands, arms extended above the chest.
Bend the elbows to lower the bell in a controlled arc past your forehead to behind your head, until it nearly touches the floor.
Keep the upper arms still, angled slightly back toward your head; only the forearms move.
Extend the elbows to press the bell back up.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.
formCues: Grip the horns firmly — the bell tries to rotate forward at the bottom.
Elbows stay narrow — if they flare, the load is too heavy.
Angle the upper arms slightly back toward the head to keep tension on the triceps at lockout.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Kettlebell Squat
description: A squat variation holding a kettlebell with both hands hanging low between the legs, adding load to a standard bodyweight squat pattern.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a kettlebell with both hands in front of you.
Let the kettlebell hang naturally between your legs as you brace your core.
Bend your hips and knees to squat down, keeping the kettlebell close to your body.
Drive through your feet to stand back up to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
formCues: Keep your chest up and back flat throughout the movement.
Let the kettlebell act as a counterbalance to help you sit deeper into the squat.
Push your knees out in line with your toes as you descend.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Kettlebell Sumo Deadlift
alternativeNames: Peso muerto sumo con pesa rusa
description: A wide-stance deadlift with a single kettlebell between the feet. The wide stance and close-to-body load make this a quad-and-glute-dominant pattern that is easy to learn.
instructions: Stand in a wide stance with toes pointed slightly out, a kettlebell on the floor between the feet.
Hinge down with a flat back, knees tracking over the toes, and grip the handle with both hands.
Drive through the floor and extend the hips and knees together to stand up.
Squeeze the glutes at the top.
Lower the bell under control back to the floor by pushing the hips back.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.
formCues: Knees track out over the toes — do not let them cave in.
Shoulders stay above the hips at the bottom; if the shoulders drop, narrow the stance.
Keep the bell close to the body throughout the lift.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Kettlebell Svend Press
description: A standing chest exercise pressing one kettlebell forward from the chest, held by the handle with both hands; squeezing the hands together on the handle keeps the pecs under tension.
instructions: Stand holding one kettlebell by the handle with both hands at chest height, the bell hanging below your hands.
Squeeze your hands together on the handle to tense the chest.
Press the kettlebell forward until your arms are almost straight.
Pull it back to the chest under control.
Repeat for the prescribed reps.
formCues: Keep pushing the hands toward each other on the handle throughout; without that squeeze it turns into a front-shoulder raise.
Use a light kettlebell — the long lever of straight arms dictates the load.
Keep the elbows slightly bent at the lockout.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Kettlebell Swing Clean
alternativeNames: Swing y cargada con pesa rusa
description: A hip-driven clean swinging the kettlebell from between the legs up to the shoulder rack position.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, kettlebell between your feet.
Hinge at the hips and grip the handle with one hand.
Swing the kettlebell back between your legs.
Drive your hips forward to pull the kettlebell up to your shoulder.
Catch the kettlebell in the rack position on your shoulder.
Complete reps on one side, then switch.
formCues: Keep the kettlebell close to your body on the way up.
Let the kettlebell roll around your wrist rather than flipping over it.
Relax your grip slightly at the top for a soft catch.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Kettlebell Tibialis Raise
alternativeNames: Elevación de Tibial con Pesa Rusa
description: A shin exercise performed seated on a bench with a kettlebell hanging from the front of one foot. Lifting the toes toward the shin against the weight strengthens the muscles at the front of the lower leg.
instructions: Sit at the end of a flat bench with one leg extended and the heel resting on the floor.
Hang a kettlebell by its handle from the front of the foot, over the toes.
Pull the toes up toward the shin as far as is comfortable while the heel stays on the floor.
Hold briefly at the top.
Lower the foot slowly until the toes point toward the floor.
Complete the repetitions, then switch legs.
formCues: Keep the movement at the ankle; the knee and thigh stay still.
Start with a light kettlebell and increase gradually; the shin muscles tire quickly.
Lower slowly rather than letting the weight drop.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Kettlebell Turkish Get Ups
description: A full-body kettlebell exercise that moves from lying to standing while holding the weight locked out overhead, training total-body strength, stability, and mobility.
instructions: Lie on your back holding a kettlebell pressed overhead in one hand.
Bend the knee on the same side and plant the foot flat.
Roll up onto your opposite elbow, then to your hand.
Drive your hips up and sweep your straight leg back into a lunge.
Stand up fully while keeping the kettlebell locked out overhead.
Reverse the sequence to return to the start.
formCues: Keep your eyes on the kettlebell until you are standing, then look forward.
Move slowly through each step — the get-up is a sequence, not one motion.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Kettlebell Windmills
alternativeNames: Molino de Viento con Pesa Rusa
description: A kettlebell exercise hinging sideways under a locked-out overhead weight, training oblique strength and shoulder stability.
instructions: Stand holding a kettlebell locked out overhead in one hand.
Turn your feet about 45 degrees away from the working arm.
Keeping the kettlebell up, hinge at the hips sideways.
Reach your opposite hand down toward your foot.
Drive your hips back to stand up tall.
Complete reps on one side, then switch.
formCues: Keep your eyes on the kettlebell throughout the movement.
Push your hips out to the side instead of rounding your spine.
Start light until the hinge pattern feels stable and controlled.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Kettlebell Wrist Curl
description: A wrist curl with a kettlebell in each hand, with the offset weight adding extra grip challenge.
instructions: Sit on a bench with your forearms on your thighs, palms up.
Hold a kettlebell by the handle in each hand, with the wrists hanging off the knees.
Let the kettlebells rotate down toward the fingertips.
Curl them up by flexing the wrists, controlling the offset weight.
Lower under control and repeat for the planned reps.
formCues: Hold the handles, not the bells, so the offset weight loads the grip.
Use a lighter load than you would for a dumbbell.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Knee Push Ups
description: A beginner-friendly push-up variation performed from the knees, reducing bodyweight load while building chest and triceps strength.
instructions: Start in a push-up position with your knees on the floor.
Place your hands shoulder-width apart on the ground.
Keep your body in a straight line from knees to shoulders.
Lower your chest toward the floor by bending your elbows.
Press through your hands to return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
formCues: Squeeze your glutes to keep your hips from sagging.
Keep your elbows at roughly a 45-degree angle from your torso.
Lower with control instead of dropping your chest quickly.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Knee-to-Chest Stretch
description: A lying stretch that releases the glutes and lower back by hugging one knee into the chest.
instructions: Lie on your back with both legs straight.
Pull one knee in and hug it to your chest with both hands.
Keep the other leg relaxed on the floor.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
Switch sides and repeat.
formCues: Keep your head and shoulders relaxed on the floor.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Kneeling Cable Row
description: A cable row performed from a tall kneeling position, eliminating hip drive and keeping tension on the upper back throughout.
instructions: Set a cable pulley to about chest height and attach a rope or double-D handle.
Kneel upright facing the stack far enough back that the weight stack doesn't bottom out.
Grab the handle with both hands and hold it out in front at chest height.
Row the handle to the sternum by driving the elbows back and squeezing the shoulder blades together.
Return under control to the stretched starting position.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.
formCues: Stay tall — no leaning back to finish the rep.
The tall-kneeling stance forces the core to resist rotation on every pull.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Kneeling Hip Flexor Stretch
alternativeNames: Estiramiento de Flexores de Cadera Arrodillado
description: A half-kneeling stretch that opens the hip flexors of the rear leg by pressing the hips forward.
instructions: Kneel on one knee with the other foot flat in front.
Keep your torso upright and core gently braced.
Press your hips forward until the front of the rear hip stretches.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
Switch sides and repeat.
formCues: Squeeze the glute of the kneeling leg to protect the lower back.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Kneeling Wrist Stretch
description: A kneeling stretch for the forearm flexors and wrists, with palms down and fingers pointing back.
instructions: Kneel on all fours and place your palms flat on the floor.
Turn your hands so the fingers point back toward your knees.
Keep your palms down and rock your weight back gently.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
formCues: Keep your palms flat as you lean back.
Stretch to mild tension, never to pain.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: L Sit
description: An advanced static hold with legs extended parallel to the floor, demanding hip flexor and core strength.
instructions: Sit on the floor or press up on parallel bars with arms straight.
Lock your elbows and depress your shoulders.
Lift your legs straight out in front of you parallel to the floor.
Form an L shape with your body.
Hold the position for the prescribed duration.
Lower your legs with control to exit.
formCues: Bend your knees into a tuck position if the full hold is too hard.
Point your toes and squeeze your quads to keep legs straight.
Breathe steadily during the hold rather than holding your breath.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Landmine Press
description: A two-handed shoulder press using one end of a barbell anchored in a landmine attachment, allowing a natural arc that is easier on the shoulder joint.
instructions: Load one end of a barbell into a landmine attachment and load the other end with a plate.
Stand in a staggered or square stance and cup the sleeve end of the barbell in both hands at chest height.
Brace your core and press the bar forward and upward along its natural arc.
Fully extend your arms without locking the elbows, then lower the bar back under control.
Keep both hands on the bar throughout and repeat for the desired number of reps.
formCues: Keep your torso upright and avoid leaning excessively into the press.
The angled path makes it more shoulder-friendly than a strict overhead press.
Use a push-press leg drive for heavier loads.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Landmine Single-Arm Overhead Hold
alternativeNames: Sostén Landmine a Un Brazo sobre la Cabeza
description: A one-arm isometric hold at the top of the landmine press: you press the end of the barbell overhead and stay locked out. The shoulder, the chest and the serratus keep the bar steady while the trunk resists the sideways pull of the angled bar.
instructions: Set one end of a barbell in a landmine post or in a corner and stand facing the free end in a staggered stance, feet about shoulder-width apart.
Hold the end of the bar with one hand at the shoulder and keep your other hand on your hip.
Press the bar up and forward until your arm is straight and your hand is above and slightly in front of your shoulder.
Lock out your elbow and push your shoulder blade around your ribs without shrugging.
Hold the bar steady for the planned time, with your trunk braced so that you do not lean to the side.
Lower the bar to your shoulder under control and switch arms.
formCues: Keep the ribs down and the glutes squeezed so that you do not arch your lower back as you hold.
Push the shoulder away from your ear at the top; do not let it shrug up toward your neck.
Use a lighter load than for the press; holding for time is harder than a single repetition.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Lat Pulldown
description: A cable machine exercise targeting the latissimus dorsi.
instructions: Sit at the lat pulldown machine with thighs secured under the pads.
Grip the wide bar with an overhand grip.
Pull the bar down to your upper chest, squeezing your lats.
Slowly return the bar to the starting position.
Repeat.
formCues: Drive your elbows down and back rather than pulling with your hands.
Avoid leaning far back or using momentum to move the weight.
Keep your chest lifted and shoulders down away from your ears.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Lateral Leg Swing
description: A dynamic hip-mobility drill in which one leg swings across the body and out to the side while the standing leg and trunk remain controlled.
instructions: Stand tall and brace the trunk, using a stable support if needed.
Shift the weight onto one leg and lift the other foot slightly from the floor.
Swing the free leg across the front of the body.
Reverse the motion and swing it out to the side through a comfortable range.
Continue smoothly, then change legs.
formCues: Keep the pelvis facing forward instead of rotating with the swinging leg.
Use a range you can control without leaning the torso.
Let the movement grow gradually rather than forcing the first repetition.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Lean-Back 90/90 Hold
description: A gentler version of the 90/90 hip hold: from the same 90/90 leg position, you lean your trunk back and support it on your hands behind you. Leaning back takes some load off the hips while keeping the front leg turned out and the back leg turned in.
instructions: Sit on the floor with your front leg bent in front of you to about 90 degrees and your back leg out to the side, also bent to about 90 degrees.
Place your hands on the floor behind your hips, fingers pointing back or to the side.
Lean your trunk back onto your hands, keeping your arms straight and your chest open.
Let both knees settle toward the floor without forcing them.
Hold the position, breathing slowly, feeling a mild stretch in the outer hip of the front leg and the front of the hip of the back leg.
Hold for the planned time, then switch the legs and hold on the other side.
formCues: Use this version when the upright 90/90 is too intense; lean further back on your hands to ease the stretch.
Keep your shoulders down and away from your ears rather than hanging on your arms.
Move slowly into the position and keep it pain-free, especially at the knees.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Lying Leg Curl
description: An isolation exercise for the hamstrings using a leg curl machine.
instructions: Lie face down on the leg curl machine with ankles under the pad.
Curl your heels toward your glutes.
Squeeze your hamstrings at the top.
Lower with control.
Repeat.
formCues: Keep your hips pressed into the bench throughout the set.
Avoid jerking the weight up with your lower back.
Use a full range of motion without letting the stack slam down.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Leg Extension
description: An isolation exercise for the quadriceps using a machine.
instructions: Sit in the leg extension machine with ankles behind the pad.
Extend your legs until they are straight.
Squeeze your quads at the top.
Lower with control.
Repeat.
formCues: Adjust the seat so your knees align with the machine's pivot point.
Keep your back pressed against the pad throughout.
Avoid swinging the weight up with momentum.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Leg Press
description: A machine-based compound movement for the quads and glutes.
instructions: Sit in the leg press machine with feet shoulder-width apart on the platform.
Release the safety catches and lower the platform by bending your knees.
Push the platform back up until legs are nearly straight.
Do not lock your knees at the top.
Repeat.
formCues: Keep your lower back and hips pressed into the seat.
Lower only as far as you can without your hips tucking under.
Drive evenly through your whole foot, not just your toes.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Front-to-Back Leg Swing
alternativeNames: Balanceo de Pierna Adelante y Atrás
description: A dynamic hip-mobility drill that swings one straight or softly bent leg forwards and backwards while the standing side stabilises the pelvis.
instructions: Stand tall beside a stable support and shift the weight onto the inside leg.
Brace the trunk and lift the outside foot slightly from the floor.
Swing the free leg forwards through a comfortable range.
Let it travel back behind the body without arching the lower back.
Continue smoothly, then repeat with the other leg.
formCues: Keep the torso tall and let the movement come from the hip.
Use a small range first and increase it as the hip warms up.
Keep the standing foot planted and the pelvis facing forward.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Legs-Up-the-Wall Pose
