description: A restorative position with the hips close to a wall and the legs resting vertically against it, used for recovery rather than for effort.
instructions: Sit sideways next to a wall with one hip touching it.
Swing the legs up the wall as you lie back, so the hips end close to the base of the wall.
Let the legs rest against the wall with the feet relaxed and the arms open at the sides.
Stay for the prescribed time, breathing slowly.
Bend the knees and roll to one side to come out.
formCues: Slide the hips a few centimetres away from the wall if the hamstrings feel pulled.
Place a folded blanket under the pelvis for a gentler, more supported version.
Keep the legs passive; this position is meant to cost no effort.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Lizard Stretch
description: A deep lunge stretch that opens the hip flexors, groin and glutes with the forearms lowered toward the floor.
instructions: Step one foot forward into a deep lunge, foot placed wide.
Lower both forearms toward the floor inside the front foot.
Extend the back leg straight and let the hips sink.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
Switch sides and repeat.
formCues: Rest on your hands instead of forearms for an easier version.
Stretch to mild tension, never to pain.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Locust Pose
description: A prone hold in which the chest, arms and legs lift away from the floor, so the whole back line works isometrically without any load.
instructions: Lie face down with the arms alongside the body and the forehead on the mat.
Lengthen the back of the neck and reach the fingertips towards the feet.
Lift the chest, arms and both legs off the floor at the same time.
Hold the lifted position for the prescribed time, keeping the gaze down.
Lower everything down together and rest.
formCues: Lift with the length of the spine rather than cranking the head up.
Keep the legs about hip-width apart and the knees straight.
Start with the legs only, then add the chest, if the full lift is too much.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Low Lunge
description: A kneeling split-stance stretch: the back knee rests on the floor while the hips sink forward, lengthening the hip flexor of the rear leg.
instructions: From kneeling, step one foot forward so the knee stacks over the ankle.
Lower the back knee to the floor and untuck that foot.
Tuck the tailbone slightly and press the hips forward until you feel the front of the back thigh lengthen.
Lift the chest, raise the arms if it feels good, and hold for the prescribed time.
Step back and repeat on the other side.
formCues: Pad the back knee with a folded mat if the floor is hard.
Squeeze the back glute to deepen the stretch without arching the lower back.
Keep the front knee above the ankle rather than letting it slide forward.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Low Lunge to Half Split
description: A moving hamstring and hip-flexor sequence: from a low lunge the hips shift back over the rear knee and the front leg straightens into a half split, then the hips travel forward into the lunge again.
instructions: Start in a low lunge with the back knee on the floor and the front knee over the ankle.
Press the hands into the floor or onto blocks either side of the front foot.
Shift the hips back over the back knee and straighten the front leg, flexing that foot.
Hold the half split briefly, then glide the hips forward into the low lunge again.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions and change sides.
formCues: Keep the back of the front leg long: bend the knee slightly rather than rounding the spine to reach.
Move the hips, not the front foot; the foot stays where it started.
Pad the back knee and use blocks under the hands if the floor is out of reach.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Lunge
description: A bodyweight forward lunge stepping into a long stride, training the quads, glutes, and balance one leg at a time.
instructions: Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart.
Step forward with one leg into a long stride.
Lower your back knee toward the floor until both knees form 90-degree angles.
Drive through your front heel to return to standing.
Complete reps on one side, then switch.
formCues: Take a stride long enough for both knees to reach about 90 degrees.
Keep your torso upright and eyes forward.
Push through the front heel to return in one strong motion.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Lying Quad Stretch
description: A floor stretch for the front of the thigh: lying on your side, you bend the top knee and pull the heel toward your glute with your hand. Lying down takes balance out of the stretch, so you can relax and let the quadriceps lengthen.
instructions: Lie on your side with your legs straight and your head resting on your lower arm.
Bend your top knee and take hold of that foot or ankle with your top hand.
Gently pull your heel toward your glute, keeping your knees close together.
Tuck your pelvis slightly so your lower back does not arch.
Hold the stretch for the planned time while breathing slowly.
Release the foot, roll to the other side and repeat.
formCues: Keep the knees side by side; letting the top knee drift forward turns it into a hip stretch.
Do not pull the heel hard; ease into a stretch you feel in the front of the thigh, not in the knee.
If you cannot reach the foot, loop a towel or strap around the ankle and pull on that.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Lying Tricep Extension
description: A lying triceps isolation exercise: one dumbbell held in both hands is lowered behind the head by bending the elbows, then pressed back up.
instructions: Lie flat on a bench and hold one dumbbell in both hands straight above your chest.
Keep your upper arms close to vertical, elbows pointing up toward the ceiling.
Lower the dumbbell behind your head by bending your elbows.
Extend your arms back to the starting position.
Squeeze your triceps at the top.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
formCues: Keep your elbows pointing up and tucked in rather than flaring out to the sides.
Move only at the elbows, not the shoulders.
Lower the weight under control rather than dropping it.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Machine Back Extension
description: A seated machine isolation exercise for the lower back: with the hips and legs held in place, the torso is driven backwards against a padded lever to extend the spine against a weight stack.
instructions: Sit in the back extension machine with your feet flat on the foot platform and the roller pad set behind your upper back, just below the shoulder blades.
Grip the handles at your sides and let your torso come forward into a slight flexion — this is the starting position.
Push back against the pad by extending your spine until your torso is leaning back and your lower back is fully contracted.
Pause briefly at full extension, then return to the starting position under control, resisting the weight stack on the way back.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
formCues: Set the pad across your upper back just below the shoulder blades — too high and it presses on your neck, too low and you lose range of motion.
Extend with your lower back rather than throwing your head and shoulders backwards, and keep both directions slow.
Stop at a neutral, fully extended trunk instead of forcing the spine past it, and start light — the lower back responds better to controlled reps than to heavy loads.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Machine Bicep Curl
description: A machine-based bicep curl for isolated arm training.
instructions: Sit in the machine and adjust the pad to your arm length.
Grip the handles with an underhand grip.
Curl the handles toward your shoulders.
Lower with control.
Repeat.
formCues: Keep your upper arms pressed into the pad throughout the set.
Avoid shrugging your shoulders as you curl.
Extend your arms fully at the bottom without bouncing.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Machine Calf Raise
description: A standing machine exercise isolating the calves through a full stretch and rise onto the toes.
instructions: Stand in the calf raise machine with the balls of your feet on the platform.
Position the shoulder pads firmly.
Lower your heels below the platform for a full stretch.
Push through the balls of your feet to rise onto your toes.
Squeeze your calves at the top.
Lower with control and repeat.
formCues: Keep your knees straight but not locked throughout the movement.
Pause briefly in the stretched position instead of bouncing.
Avoid cutting the range of motion short as fatigue sets in.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Machine Chest Fly
description: A chest isolation exercise performed on a machine that arcs the handles together in front of the body.
instructions: Sit in the chest fly machine and adjust the seat so the handles align with your chest.
Grip the handles with a slight bend in your elbows.
Bring the handles together in front of your chest in a smooth arc.
Squeeze your pectorals at the point of peak contraction.
Return under control to the starting position without slamming the weight.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
formCues: Keep a slight, fixed bend in your elbows throughout.
Focus on squeezing the chest rather than pushing with the arms.
Control the return instead of letting the weight stack slam.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Machine Preacher Curl
description: A preacher curl performed on a plate-loaded or selectorized machine, locking the elbows on a pad and providing a fixed strength curve.
instructions: Sit at a preacher curl machine and adjust the seat so your armpits sit at the top of the pad.
Place the upper arms flat on the pad and grip the handles.
Start with the arms extended — but not locked — at the bottom.
Curl the handles up by flexing the elbows; squeeze hard at the top.
Lower slowly back to the starting position and repeat.
formCues: Do not let the elbows lift off the pad at the top.
Stop just short of full extension at the bottom to protect the elbow tendons.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Machine Reverse Fly
description: A seated machine exercise for the rear deltoids, also known as the reverse pec deck: facing the pad, you sweep the two handles out and back in a wide arc against the weight stack. The pad keeps the torso still, so the work stays on the back of the shoulders and the muscles between the shoulder blades.
instructions: Adjust the seat so the handles are at shoulder height, then sit facing the machine with your chest against the pad.
Grip the handles with your arms reaching forward and a slight bend in the elbows.
Keep your shoulders down and away from your ears and brace your trunk.
Sweep the handles out and back in a wide arc, leading with the elbows, until your arms are roughly in line with your shoulders.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together briefly without leaning back off the pad.
Return the handles forward slowly and repeat for the planned repetitions.
formCues: Lead with the elbows rather than pulling with the hands, so the rear deltoids do the work and not the biceps.
Keep the chest on the pad and the neck relaxed; leaning back or shrugging moves the load to the upper trapezius.
Choose a weight you can lower under control; a lighter load with a slow return works the rear deltoids better than a heavy swing.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Machine Seated Crunch
description: An abdominal isolation exercise performed on a seated machine that flexes the spine against resistance.
instructions: Sit in the abdominal crunch machine and grip the handles.
Position the chest pad against your upper body.
Contract your abs to crunch your torso forward and down.
Squeeze at the bottom of the movement.
Return to the starting position with control.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
formCues: Initiate the movement with your abs, not your arms.
Avoid using momentum by rocking your body.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Machine Shoulder Press
description: A machine-based overhead pressing movement for the shoulders.
instructions: Sit in the machine with your back against the pad.
Grip the handles at shoulder level.
Press the handles overhead until arms are fully extended.
Lower with control to the starting position.
Repeat.
formCues: Keep your lower back pressed into the pad without overarching.
Keep your wrists stacked directly over your elbows as you press.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Machine Triceps Extension
description: A seated machine isolation exercise in which the upper arms stay supported on a pad while the elbows extend against two handles, loading the triceps along a fixed path without help from the shoulders or torso.
instructions: Sit in the tricep extension machine with your back against the seat pad and your upper arms resting flat on the arm pad in front of your chest.
Take a handle in each hand with your elbows bent and your hands up near shoulder height.
Keeping your upper arms pressed into the pad, extend your elbows to drive the handles down and away until your arms are straight.
Squeeze your triceps at full extension, then bend your elbows to return to the start under control.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
formCues: Set the seat height so your upper arms lie flat on the pad and your elbows line up with the machine's pivot — that alignment is what keeps the work on the triceps.
Keep your upper arms glued to the pad; letting them lift turns the movement into a press and takes the triceps out of it.
Straighten your arms fully without snapping the elbows, and resist on the way back instead of letting the weight stack drop.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Medicine Ball Side Throw
description: A rotational power exercise: standing side-on with a medicine ball held at your hip, you turn your hips and torso and throw the ball out to the side with both hands. The obliques and the rest of the trunk turn the body, and the hips start the rotation.
instructions: Stand with your feet a little wider than shoulder-width, holding a medicine ball with both hands in front of your torso.
Turn your torso and the ball toward your back hip, bending your knees slightly and keeping your chest up.
Start the throw by turning your back hip forward and pivoting on the ball of your back foot.
Let your torso and arms follow, throwing the ball out to the side with both hands.
Finish facing the direction of the throw with your arms extended.
Retrieve the ball, reset, and repeat for the planned repetitions, then switch sides.
formCues: Start the throw from the hips, not the arms; the trunk and arms should follow the hip turn.
Throw explosively, but keep your back neutral as you rotate rather than bending sideways.
Use a ball light enough to throw fast; a heavy ball slows the rotation and turns it into a push.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Medicine Ball Slam
description: An explosive full-body exercise where a soft slam ball is lifted overhead and driven into the floor with maximum force.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a slam ball in front of your hips.
Lift the ball overhead by extending the hips and reaching tall.
Forcefully slam the ball into the floor between your feet, crunching through the core.
Catch the ball on the bounce or pick it up from the floor.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.
formCues: Use a dead-bounce slam ball, not a traditional medicine ball — regular balls will bounce back into your face.
Finish with the whole body — it is a full swing, not just an arm throw.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Mountain Climbers
description: A dynamic bodyweight exercise combining core work with cardio.
instructions: Start in a high plank position.
Drive one knee toward your chest.
Quickly switch legs, driving the other knee forward.
Continue alternating at a brisk pace.
Repeat.
formCues: Keep your hips level and low rather than piking upward.
Keep your shoulders stacked directly over your wrists.
Maintain a steady breathing rhythm as the pace increases.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Mountain Pose
description: The basic standing posture: feet grounded, legs active, spine tall and shoulders relaxed. It is the reference alignment every other standing pose is measured against.
instructions: Stand with the feet hip-width apart and spread the weight evenly across both feet.
Engage the thighs lightly and let the tailbone drop so the pelvis is neutral.
Stack the ribs over the pelvis and the head over the ribs, arms relaxed by the sides.
Hold the posture for the prescribed time, breathing evenly.
Notice where the weight sits and rebalance it towards the middle of each foot.
formCues: Lift and spread the toes once, then set them down; it resets the arch of the foot.
Keep the knees soft rather than locked back.
Let the shoulders roll back and down without pinning the shoulder blades together.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Muscle Snatch
description: A snatch variation pulling the barbell overhead without dropping under it, building pulling power and lockout strength.
instructions: Stand with feet hip-width apart and grip the bar wide with a hook grip.
Pull the bar explosively from the floor, keeping it close to your body.
Shrug hard and pull the bar overhead without dipping under.
Lock out the bar overhead with straight arms.
Lower the bar under control to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
formCues: Shrug hard and keep pulling the bar up high.
Stay tall; do not dip under the bar to catch it.
Keep the bar close to your body throughout the pull.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Muscle Ups
description: An advanced bar movement combining an explosive pull-up with a dip transition to finish above the bar.
instructions: Hang from a pull-up bar with a false grip.
Pull yourself up explosively toward the bar.
As your chest reaches the bar, rotate your elbows over and transition into a dip.
Press your body up until your arms are fully extended above the bar.
Lower back down with control through the same path.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
formCues: Use a false grip so your wrists are already over the bar for the transition.
Pull explosively toward your sternum, not just your chin.
Drill the transition on low rings or with bands before full reps.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Negative Pull Ups
description: A pull-up regression emphasizing the slow lowering phase, building back and grip strength toward a full pull-up.
instructions: Use a box or jump to position yourself at the top of a pull-up.
Grip the bar with hands shoulder-width apart.
Hold your chin above the bar briefly.
Lower yourself slowly over 3-5 seconds with control.
Fully extend your arms at the bottom.
Reset and repeat for the desired number of reps.
formCues: Fight for control during the final third of the descent.
Keep your shoulder blades engaged instead of hanging passively.
Stop the set once you can no longer lower slowly.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Neutral Grip Pull Ups
description: A pull-up variation on parallel handles with palms facing each other, recruiting the lats with strong brachialis assistance.
instructions: Grip parallel bars with palms facing each other.
Hang with your arms fully extended.
Pull yourself up until your chin clears the bar.
Squeeze your lats at the top of the movement.
Lower yourself with control to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
formCues: Initiate each rep by pulling your shoulder blades down and back.
Drive your elbows down toward your ribs as you pull.
Avoid kipping or swinging your legs for momentum.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Nordic Hamstring Curl
description: A knee-flexion exercise lowering the torso forward from a kneeling position, working the hamstrings eccentrically.
instructions: Kneel on a pad with your ankles anchored under a fixed support.
Keep your torso upright and your hips extended.
Slowly lower your body forward by resisting with your hamstrings.
Catch yourself with your hands just before hitting the floor.
Push back up and pull yourself to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
formCues: Lower as slowly as possible — the eccentric is the point.
Keep your hips extended; do not fold at the waist.
Catch yourself with your hands and push off lightly while building strength.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Barbell Overhead Press
description: A compound overhead pressing movement targeting the shoulders and triceps.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, bar at collarbone level.
Brace your core and press the bar overhead.
Lock out at the top with the bar over your mid-foot.
Lower the bar back to collarbone height.
Repeat.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: One Arm Dumbbell Preacher Curl
alternativeNames: Curl Predicador con Mancuerna a Un Brazo
description: A unilateral biceps curl performed seated at a preacher bench with the upper arm supported on the pad. Training one arm at a time keeps the elbow fixed and isolates the biceps.
instructions: Sit at a preacher bench and rest the back of one upper arm flat on the pad.
Hold a dumbbell in that hand with the palm facing up and the arm almost fully extended.
Curl the dumbbell toward the shoulder without lifting the elbow off the pad.
Squeeze the biceps at the top of the movement.
Lower the dumbbell slowly until the arm is almost straight.
Complete the repetitions, then switch arms.
formCues: Stop just short of lockout at the bottom to keep tension on the biceps and spare the elbow.
Keep the shoulder relaxed and the chest against the pad.
Lower the weight more slowly than you lift it.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: One-Arm Dumbbell Push Press
alternativeNames: Push Press con Mancuerna a Un Brazo
description: A unilateral push press using a single dumbbell. Leg drive lets you punch heavier loads overhead than a strict one-arm press, and the asymmetric load forces strong anti-lateral-flexion bracing.
instructions: Stand holding a dumbbell at one shoulder, palm facing inward (neutral).
Feet shoulder-width, core braced, free arm out to the side for balance.
Dip by bending the knees slightly, keeping the torso vertical.
Explosively extend the legs and press the dumbbell overhead in one motion.
Lock out overhead, then lower back to the shoulder under control.
Complete all reps on one side, then switch.
formCues: Drive from the legs — the arm finishes, it does not start.
The torso must stay upright and square; do not side-bend away from the load.
Lighter weight and cleaner leg drive beat heavy with a leaning torso.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: One Arm Dumbbell Shoulder Press
alternativeNames: Press de Hombros con Mancuerna a Un Brazo
description: A standing overhead press performed with a single dumbbell. Working one side at a time loads the shoulder and triceps and makes the trunk resist leaning toward the empty hand.
instructions: Stand with the feet hip-width apart and hold a dumbbell at one shoulder with the palm facing forward.
Brace the abdominals and keep the free arm relaxed at your side.
Press the dumbbell straight overhead until the arm is fully extended.
Pause briefly at the top with the upper arm next to the ear.
Lower the dumbbell back to the shoulder under control.
Complete the repetitions on one arm, then switch sides.
formCues: Keep the ribs down and the glutes tight; do not lean sideways to push the weight up.
Press in a straight line close to the head, not out in front.
Start lighter than you would with two dumbbells; the trunk has to stabilise the load.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: One-Arm Dumbbell Swing
alternativeNames: Swing con Mancuerna a un Brazo
description: This dynamic exercise builds explosive power in the glutes and hamstrings through a powerful hip hinge, engaging the core and shoulders for a full-body workout.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, a dumbbell on the floor slightly in front of you.
Hinge at your hips, keeping a flat back, and grasp the dumbbell with one hand.
Hike the dumbbell back between your legs, then explosively drive your hips forward.
Swing the dumbbell up to chest height, keeping your arm relaxed and straight.
Allow the dumbbell to swing back down, hinging at the hips as it descends.
Repeat for desired reps per side, maintaining control.
formCues: Focus on driving with your hips, not pulling with your arm.
Keep your core braced throughout the movement for stability.
Maintain a neutral spine; avoid rounding your back.
Control the eccentric phase as the dumbbell swings down.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: One Arm Kettlebell Bicep Curl
alternativeNames: Curl de Bíceps con Pesa Rusa a Un Brazo
description: A unilateral kettlebell exercise isolating the biceps, with the offset load adding forearm and grip demand.
instructions: Stand tall holding a kettlebell in one hand.
Keep your elbow pinned to your side.
Curl the kettlebell toward your shoulder by flexing your bicep.
Squeeze at the top of the movement.
Lower the kettlebell with control.
Complete reps on one side, then switch.
formCues: Keep your wrist straight as the offset weight shifts through the curl.
Brace your core to resist leaning away from the working side.
Avoid swinging the kettlebell up with your hips.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: One-Arm Kettlebell Bottoms-Up Press
alternativeNames: Press Strict con Pesa Rusa Invertida a Un Brazo
description: A strict overhead press with the kettlebell held upside-down — bell on top, handle at the palm. The inverted load demands heavy grip, perfect shoulder stability, and ruthless bar-path discipline.
instructions: Clean a light kettlebell to the rack position, then tilt it so the bell points up and the handle is at the palm.
Grip the handle hard; wrist absolutely straight and vertical.
Brace the core and press the bell straight up without letting it tip.
Lock out overhead with the bell still perfectly upright.
Lower slowly back to the rack position keeping the bell vertical the entire descent.
Complete all reps on one side, then switch.
formCues: If the bell tips, the set is over — do not fight it down.
Start with a very light weight; this is a skill and stability lift, not a heavy press.
Grip hard throughout — any loosening and the bell falls.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: One Arm Kettlebell Floor Glute Bridge Press
alternativeNames: Press en Puente de Glúteos en Suelo con Pesa Rusa a Un Brazo
description: A combined glute bridge and single-arm floor press, training the glutes and chest in one movement.
instructions: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor.
Hold a kettlebell in one hand at your shoulder.
Drive your hips up into a glute bridge.
Press the kettlebell straight up toward the ceiling.
Lower the kettlebell and your hips with control.
Complete reps on one side, then switch.
formCues: Hold the bridge steady at the top while pressing.
Keep your wrist straight and stacked under the kettlebell.
Extend your free arm along the floor for extra stability.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: One Arm Kettlebell Floor Press
alternativeNames: Press en Suelo con Pesa Rusa a Un Brazo
description: A unilateral kettlebell press performed lying on the floor, where the limited range reduces shoulder strain.
instructions: Lie flat on the floor with knees bent.
Hold a kettlebell at your shoulder with one hand.
Press the kettlebell straight up until your arm is fully extended.
Lower the kettlebell until your upper arm touches the floor.
Keep your core braced throughout.
Complete reps on one side, then switch.
formCues: Keep your forearm vertical throughout the press.
Tuck your elbow to roughly 45 degrees from your torso.
Let your upper arm touch down gently rather than bouncing off the floor.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: One Arm Kettlebell Front Squat
alternativeNames: Sentadilla Frontal con Pesa Rusa a Un Brazo
description: A unilateral front squat with one kettlebell racked at the shoulder, challenging the legs and core against the offset load.
instructions: Hold a kettlebell in the racked position at one shoulder.
Stand with feet shoulder-width apart.
Squat down by bending your knees and hips.
Keep your chest up and torso upright throughout.
Drive through your heels to stand back up.
Complete reps on one side, then switch.
formCues: Keep the rack position tight against your chest and forearm.
Resist twisting or leaning toward the loaded side.
Spread the floor with your feet to keep your knees tracking outward.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: One Arm Kettlebell Push Press
alternativeNames: Push Press con Pesa Rusa a Un Brazo
description: An explosive single-arm overhead press using leg drive to launch the kettlebell, allowing heavier loads than a strict press.
instructions: Hold a kettlebell in the racked position at one shoulder.
Stand with feet shoulder-width apart.
Dip by bending your knees slightly.
Drive explosively through your legs and press the kettlebell overhead.
Lock out your arm at the top.
Lower the kettlebell to your shoulder with control.
Complete reps on one side, then switch.
formCues: Keep your torso upright during the dip, not tipping forward.
Time the press so your arm extends as your legs finish driving.
Keep the dip shallow and quick rather than a half squat.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: One Arm Kettlebell Row
alternativeNames: Remo con Pesa Rusa a Un Brazo
description: A unilateral rowing exercise with bench support, building the lats and mid-back one side at a time.
instructions: Place one hand and knee on a bench for support.
Hold a kettlebell in the opposite hand with your arm extended.
Pull the kettlebell toward your hip by driving your elbow back.
Squeeze your back at the top of the movement.
Lower the kettlebell with control.
Complete reps on one side, then switch.
formCues: Keep your torso square to the floor throughout the set.
Pull with your back muscles rather than just your arm.
Keep your neck neutral, eyes on the floor just ahead.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: One Arm Kettlebell Shoulder Press
alternativeNames: Press de Hombro con Pesa Rusa a Un Brazo
description: A strict single-arm overhead press from the rack position, training the shoulders while the core resists side-bending.
instructions: Hold a kettlebell in the racked position at one shoulder.
Stand tall with feet hip-width apart.
Press the kettlebell straight overhead until your arm is locked out.
Keep your core tight throughout.
Lower the kettlebell back to the rack position with control.
Complete reps on one side, then switch.
formCues: Avoid leaning away from the kettlebell as it travels overhead.
Finish with your biceps close to your ear at lockout.
Squeeze your glutes to keep your ribs from flaring.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: One Arm Kettlebell Swing
alternativeNames: Swing con Pesa Rusa a Un Brazo
description: A single-arm variation of the kettlebell swing, adding grip and anti-rotation demands to the explosive hip hinge.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and a kettlebell on the floor in front of you.
Hinge at the hips and grip the kettlebell with one hand.
Hike the kettlebell back between your legs.
Drive your hips forward to swing the kettlebell to chest height.
Let gravity bring the kettlebell back between your legs.
Complete reps on one side, then switch.
formCues: Keep your shoulders square as the offset load tries to rotate you.
Power the movement with your hips, not by lifting with your arm.
Hinge with a flat back rather than squatting the swing.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: One-Arm Kettlebell Tricep Kickback
alternativeNames: Extensión de Tríceps a Un Brazo con Pesa Rusa
description: A unilateral tricep isolation done with a kettlebell instead of a dumbbell. Hinge over, pin the upper arm to the side parallel to the floor, and extend the elbow back. The offset bell mass adds rotational tension at the bottom of every rep.
instructions: Hinge forward at the hips with a flat back, knees softly bent.
Hold a kettlebell by the handle in one hand, palm facing the body.
Pin the upper arm to the side so it is parallel to the floor; the forearm hangs straight down.
Extend the elbow back to straighten the arm fully behind you, keeping the upper arm motionless.
Squeeze the tricep at lockout, then return under control to the starting position.
Complete all reps on one side, then switch hands.
formCues: The upper arm does not move — only the forearm. Any shoulder swing is a cheat.
Lock the bell briefly at full extension; the bottom of the bell wants to dip the wrist.
Use a lighter bell than you would for a dumbbell kickback — the offset load is harder to stabilize.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: One-Arm Landmine Press
description: A unilateral overhead press variation using a landmine setup that follows a natural arc, reducing shoulder impingement risk while building pressing strength.
instructions: Anchor one end of a barbell in a landmine attachment and load the free end.
Kneel on one knee or stand and grip the sleeve end at shoulder height with one hand.
Press the bar upward and forward along its arc until the arm is fully extended.
Lower the bar back to shoulder height under control.
Complete all reps before switching sides.
formCues: Engage your core to prevent the torso from rotating toward the working arm.
The arc motion is more joint-friendly than a vertical overhead press.
Kneeling on the knee on the same side as the pressing arm, with the other foot planted in front, increases the core's anti-rotation demand.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: One-Arm Lat Pulldown
alternativeNames: Jalón al Pecho con Un Brazo
description: A unilateral cable pulldown that targets the latissimus dorsi with a single-arm handle, allowing a greater range of motion and bilateral strength imbalances to be addressed.
instructions: Attach a single-handle to the cable pulldown station and sit with your thighs secured under the pad.
Reach up and grasp the handle with one hand, arm fully extended.
Pull the handle down toward your shoulder, driving your elbow toward your hip.
Pause briefly at full contraction, then return to the starting position with control.
Complete all reps on one side before switching.
formCues: Lean slightly away from the cable to increase lat stretch at the top.
Focus on pulling with your elbow, not your hand, to keep the lat engaged.
Control the eccentric to maximize lat tension throughout the range.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: One-Arm Seated Cable Row
description: A unilateral seated cable row that trains the lats and upper back while the torso stays square and the working shoulder blade moves through a controlled reach and pull.
instructions: Sit at the cable row station and hold one handle with the working arm extended.
Plant the feet, sit tall and brace the trunk without leaning back.
Pull the handle towards the lower ribs while drawing the shoulder blade back.
Pause briefly without rotating the torso or shrugging the shoulder.
Extend the arm under control, finish the set and repeat on the other side.
formCues: Keep both shoulders facing forward throughout the repetition.
Drive the elbow back close to the body rather than curling the handle.
Let the shoulder blade reach forward at the start without rounding the lower back.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: One-Arm Single-Leg Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
alternativeNames: Peso Muerto Rumano a Una Pierna con Mancuerna a Un Brazo
description: A single-leg RDL holding a dumbbell in one hand — usually the hand opposite the working leg (contralateral). Loads the hamstrings and glutes of the standing leg while demanding heavy anti-rotation from the core.
instructions: Stand on one leg holding a dumbbell in the opposite hand.
Free arm out to the side for balance, free leg hovering just off the floor.
Hinge at the standing hip, pushing it back while the free leg extends behind to counterbalance.
Keep the hips square to the floor — do not open them to the side.
Lower the dumbbell toward the foot of the standing leg, feeling a deep hamstring stretch.
Drive the hip forward to return to standing under control.
Complete all reps on one side, then switch.
formCues: Start lighter than you think — balance and anti-rotation demands are the limit, not hamstring strength.
If you rotate open, pause and reset; a shorter clean ROM beats a full ROM with rotation.
Eyes on a fixed spot on the floor a few feet in front helps balance.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: One-Arm Single-Leg Kettlebell Romanian Deadlift
alternativeNames: Peso Muerto Rumano a Una Pierna con Pesa Rusa a Un Brazo
description: The kettlebell version of the one-arm single-leg RDL. The offset mass of the kettlebell and the lower hanging centre make this a subtly different challenge to the dumbbell variant — excellent for posterior-chain strength and balance under asymmetric load.
instructions: Stand on one leg holding a kettlebell in the opposite hand by the handle.
Free arm out to the side for balance, free leg hovering behind.
Hinge at the standing hip, pushing it back while the free leg extends to counterbalance.
Keep hips square to the floor; the kettlebell tracks straight down the shin.
Feel a deep hamstring stretch on the standing leg at the bottom.
Drive the hip forward to return to standing.
Complete all reps on one side, then switch.
formCues: The kettlebell hangs lower than a dumbbell — shorten the ROM slightly to keep the back flat.
If the bell swings, you are moving too fast. Slow the eccentric.
Build up from the two-arm (dumbbell) single-leg RDL first.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Overhead Squat
description: A squat with a barbell locked out overhead in a wide snatch grip, demanding mobility, stability, and a strong core.
instructions: Hold a barbell overhead with a wide snatch grip and arms locked out.
Stand with feet slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Squat down by pushing your hips back and bending your knees.
Keep the bar directly over the middle of your feet.
Drive through your heels to stand back up.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
formCues: Keep your armpits facing forward to lock the bar in place.
Keep the bar over mid-foot with a more upright torso than a back squat.
Work on shoulder and ankle mobility before adding load.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Overhead Tricep Extension
alternativeNames: Extensión de Tríceps por Encima de la Cabeza
description: An isolation exercise for the triceps emphasizing the long head.
instructions: Stand or sit holding a dumbbell overhead with both hands.
Lower the dumbbell behind your head by bending your elbows.
Extend your arms back to the starting position.
Keep your elbows close to your head throughout.
Repeat.
formCues: Keep your ribs down and avoid arching your lower back.
Lower until you feel a deep stretch in your triceps.
Check your grip is secure before lowering the dumbbell behind your head.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Pause Deadlift
description: A deadlift variation with a deliberate pause just above the knees, building strength and position through the upper half of the pull.
instructions: Set up for a conventional deadlift.
Pull the bar off the floor and pause when it passes your knees.
Hold for 2–3 seconds, then complete the lift.
Lower under control.
Repeat.
formCues: The pause removes momentum and builds strength and control from the knees to lockout.
Keep your back flat during the pause.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Pause Pull-Up
description: A pull-up variation that adds a brief isometric hold at the top of the movement, with the chin over the bar, before lowering back down.
instructions: Hang from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip, arms fully extended.
Pull yourself up until your chin clears the bar.
Pause and hold that top position for a moment.
Lower yourself back down under control to a full hang.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
formCues: The pause removes momentum, so the pull is harder than a regular pull-up -- expect fewer reps.
Keep your shoulders engaged during the hold instead of relaxing into the bar.
Lower slowly instead of dropping straight into the next rep.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Pause Squat
description: A barbell squat variation with a deliberate pause at the bottom, eliminating the stretch reflex to build strength from a dead stop.
instructions: Unrack a barbell and rest it across your upper back.
Stand with feet shoulder-width apart.
Squat down until your thighs are parallel to the floor.
Hold the bottom position for 2-3 seconds.
Drive through your heels to stand back up.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
formCues: Stay braced and tight during the pause rather than relaxing.
Avoid collapsing forward or rocking as you hold the bottom.
Use lighter loads than your regular squat to maintain crisp form.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Paused Bench Press
description: A bench press variation pausing the bar on the chest, removing momentum to build strict pressing strength.
instructions: Lie on a flat bench and grip the barbell slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Unrack the bar and lower it to your chest.
Pause on your chest for 1-2 seconds.
Press the bar back up until your arms are fully extended.
Control the descent on every rep.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
formCues: Stay tight during the pause instead of letting the bar sink.
Keep your shoulder blades pinched and your feet planted throughout.
Touch the bar to the same spot on your chest every rep.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Paused Incline Bench Press
description: An incline bench press with a pause on the upper chest, emphasizing strict control and upper-pec strength.
instructions: Lie on an incline bench and grip the barbell slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Unrack the bar and lower it to your upper chest.
Pause on your chest for 1-2 seconds.
Press the bar back up until your arms are fully extended.
Keep your shoulder blades retracted throughout.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
formCues: Keep your wrists stacked over your elbows during the pause.
Maintain full-body tension while the bar rests on your chest.
Avoid bouncing the bar off your chest after the pause.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Paused Overhead Press
description: An overhead press variation that pauses the bar at the shoulders, removing momentum to build strict pressing strength and overhead stability.
instructions: Set up with a barbell racked at shoulder height, feet shoulder-width apart, and the core braced.
Press the bar straight overhead until the elbows are fully locked out.
Lower the bar under control back down to the front of the shoulders.
Hold a full one-second pause at the shoulders, keeping tension and eliminating any bounce.
Press back up from the dead stop without using leg drive.
formCues: Keep the pause strict -- no rebounding the bar off the shoulders.
Brace hard and keep the bar path vertical over the mid-foot.
Use a weight you can control through the dead-stop start.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Pec Deck
description: A chest isolation machine with swinging handles that targets the pectorals through horizontal adduction.
instructions: Sit in the pec deck machine and grip the handles with your arms out to the sides, elbows slightly bent.
Adjust the seat so the handles align with mid-chest height.
Squeeze the handles together in front of your chest.
Hold the contraction briefly at the center.
Return under control to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
formCues: Keep your shoulders down and back against the seat.
Avoid letting the handles fly back past a comfortable stretch.
Focus on squeezing your chest rather than pressing with your arms.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Pendlay Row
description: A strict barbell row performed from a dead stop on the floor between reps, torso parallel to the ground. Popularized by coach Glenn Pendlay.
instructions: Load a barbell and set it on the floor.
Hinge at the hips until your torso is parallel to the ground, knees slightly bent.
Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width with an overhand grip.
Explosively pull the bar to your lower chest.
Lower the bar back to the floor under control and pause before the next rep.
Repeat.
formCues: Dead-stop each rep on the floor — no touch-and-go.
Keep your torso locked at roughly 90 degrees; do not use body english.
Drive the elbows up and back, not out to the sides.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Pigeon Stretch
description: A seated floor stretch that targets the glutes and outer hip with the front shin folded across the body.
instructions: From all fours, bring one knee forward and lay the shin across in front.
Extend the other leg straight back, top of the foot down.
Sink your hips toward the floor and keep them square.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
Switch sides and repeat.
formCues: Place a cushion under the hip if it does not reach the floor.
Walk your hands forward to deepen the stretch.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Pike Push Ups
description: A push-up performed with hips high in a pike position, pressing at a steep angle to load the shoulders.
instructions: Start in a downward dog position with hips high and hands shoulder-width apart.
Walk your feet closer to your hands.
Bend your elbows and lower your head toward the floor.
Keep your hips high throughout.
Press back up until your arms are fully extended.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
formCues: The higher your hips, the more the shoulders work.
Lower your head toward a spot slightly ahead of your hands.
Walk your feet closer to your hands to progress toward handstand push-ups.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Pilates Kneeling Side Kick
alternativeNames: Patada Lateral de Rodillas de Pilates
description: A Pilates mat exercise: kneeling on one knee with one hand on the floor for support and the other on the hip, the top leg lifts out to the side up to hip height and lowers again while the trunk holds still.
instructions: Kneel on one knee and place the same-side hand on the floor under the shoulder, the other hand on the hip.
Extend the top leg out to the side, the foot a little below hip height.
Keeping the trunk perfectly still, lift the leg up to hip height.
Lower it back down under control without letting the pelvis tip or the lower back arch.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions and change sides.
formCues: The trunk is the exercise: if it rocks with the leg, make the lift smaller.
Keep the supporting shoulder pushed away from the ear.
Move at a controlled tempo instead of throwing the leg.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Pilates Leg Pull Back
description: A reverse plank with alternating leg lifts: the hips stay high while one leg at a time is raised, so the glutes and the back of the trunk work against the shifting support.
instructions: Sit with the legs straight and the hands on the floor behind the hips, fingers pointing forward.
Press into the hands and heels and lift the hips into a reverse plank.
Keeping the hips level and high, lift one straight leg as far as the pelvis stays still.
Lower the leg under control and repeat with the other one.
Finish the set and lower the hips to the floor.
formCues: Stop the leg lift where the hips start to drop; height is not the point.
Keep the chest open and the shoulders away from the ears.
Bend the knees slightly if the straight-leg version pulls at the hamstrings.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Pilates Leg Pull Front
description: A high plank with alternating leg lifts: the shoulders stay stacked over the wrists while one leg at a time lifts, adding an anti-rotation demand to the plank.
instructions: Set up in a high plank with the hands under the shoulders and the body in one line.
Brace the trunk and squeeze the glutes so the hips cannot rotate.
Lift one straight leg a few centimetres above hip height without letting the pelvis tilt.
Lower it under control and repeat with the other leg.
Keep alternating for the desired number of repetitions.
formCues: Lift the leg from the glute rather than by arching the lower back.
Keep the weight even in both hands; the tendency is to lean away from the lifted side.
Reduce the lift height until the hips stay perfectly level.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Pilates Roll Down
description: A standing articulation of the spine: the head leads a vertebra-by-vertebra roll towards the floor and back up, mobilising the whole back while the legs stay steady.
instructions: Stand tall with the feet hip-width apart and the arms hanging at the sides.
Drop the chin to the chest and start rolling down one vertebra at a time.
Let the arms and head hang heavy once the spine is fully rolled down.
Roll back up the same way, stacking the vertebrae one by one, head last.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
formCues: Keep the knees soft so the movement comes from the spine, not the hamstrings.
Move slowly enough to feel each segment; speed defeats the purpose.
Keep the weight in the middle of the feet as you roll down.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Pilates Roll Over
description: A controlled inversion from the mat: with the arms pressing down, the straight legs travel overhead until the toes reach towards the floor, then the spine rolls back down one segment at a time.
instructions: Lie on your back with the legs straight and the arms pressed into the mat beside you.
Lift both legs to vertical without letting the lower back arch.
Press the arms down and take the legs overhead until they are parallel to the floor behind you.
Open the legs slightly, flex the feet, and roll the spine down one vertebra at a time.
Return the legs to vertical and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
formCues: Drive the movement with the abdominals, not by throwing the legs.
Keep the weight off the neck: the roll stops at the shoulder blades.
Skip this exercise if you have neck complaints, and build it up with smaller curls first.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Pilates Saw
description: A seated twist and reach: sitting tall with the legs wide, the torso rotates and then folds over the opposite leg so the reaching hand passes the little toe like a saw.
instructions: Sit tall with the legs straight and slightly wider than the hips, arms out to the sides.
Rotate the torso to one side, keeping both sit bones on the floor.
Fold forward over that leg and reach the opposite hand past the little toe.
Roll back up through the spine and return to the centre.
Repeat to the other side and continue alternating.
formCues: Anchor both sit bones; lifting one of them turns the twist into a lean.
Rotate first, then fold - the order is what makes the exercise work.
Sit on a folded blanket if the pelvis cannot stay upright.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Pilates Side Bend
description: A lateral trunk exercise from a side-supported position: the hips lift and the top arm reaches overhead, bending the body sideways over the supporting arm.
instructions: Sit on one hip with the legs bent to the side and the supporting hand on the floor under the shoulder.
Press into the hand and the lower leg to lift the hips off the floor.
Reach the top arm overhead so the body forms a long arc from the hand to the feet.
Lower the hips under control back towards the mat.
Complete the repetitions and change sides.
formCues: Push the floor away so the supporting shoulder stays stacked and stable.
Reach the top arm long rather than collapsing sideways.
Keep the movement smooth; the lift and the lower take the same time.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Pilates Spine Stretch Forward
description: A seated articulation: sitting tall with the legs apart, the spine curls forward segment by segment over the legs and then restacks vertebra by vertebra.
instructions: Sit tall with the legs straight and slightly wider than the hips, feet flexed.
Reach the arms forward at shoulder height.
Drop the chin and curl the spine forward one vertebra at a time, reaching past the toes.
Restack the spine from the base upwards until you are sitting tall again.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
formCues: Keep the pelvis upright: the curl comes from the spine, not from tipping the hips.
Press the heels away throughout so the legs stay active.
Sit on a folded blanket if sitting upright already rounds the lower back.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Pilates Spine Twist
description: A seated rotation with the legs together and the arms wide: the trunk turns to each side in a controlled pulse while the pelvis and legs stay completely still.
instructions: Sit tall with the legs straight and together, feet flexed, arms out to the sides at shoulder height.
Grow tall through the spine and press both sit bones into the floor.
Rotate the trunk to one side as far as the hips stay square, then return to the centre.
Rotate to the other side in the same way.
Keep alternating for the desired number of repetitions.
formCues: The legs are the anchor: if one foot slides forward, the pelvis has moved.
Lengthen upwards before each rotation instead of sinking into it.
Turn the head with the trunk rather than leading with it.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Pistol Squat
description: A single-leg squat performed with the non-working leg extended forward, demanding strength and balance.
instructions: Stand on one leg with the other extended forward, arms out for balance.
Hinge at the hips and bend the standing knee, keeping the chest up.
Descend slowly until the back of the thigh touches the calf.
Drive through the standing heel to return to standing.
Complete reps per side, then switch legs.
formCues: Hold a light counterweight at the chest if balance is hard.
Build the strength with box-assisted pistols first.
Keep the working heel flat on the floor.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Planche
description: An advanced calisthenics hold requiring exceptional upper body and core strength to hold the body parallel to the ground.
instructions: Begin in a push-up position with your hands turned outward on the floor, or on parallettes.
Lean forward until your center of mass is over your hands.
Lift your feet off the ground keeping the body horizontal.
Hold the position.
Return to the floor with control.
formCues: Progress through tuck, straddle, and full planche.
Build wrist and shoulder strength before attempting.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Planche Lean
description: A floor progression toward the planche: from a high plank position, you lean your shoulders forward past your hands and hold, so that more of your bodyweight loads the shoulders and chest. It builds the straight-arm strength needed for the full planche.
instructions: Start in a high plank with your hands on the floor, a little below your hips and turned out slightly.
Lock your elbows and protract your shoulder blades so your upper back is slightly rounded and strong.
Lean your body forward until your shoulders are well in front of your hands.
Keep your whole body in a straight line, with your glutes squeezed and your core braced.
Hold the lean for the planned time while breathing steadily.
Shift back to the neutral plank to finish.
formCues: Keep your arms straight; bending the elbows turns the hold into a push-up.
Push the floor away so your shoulder blades stay wide rather than sinking between the shoulders.
Lean only as far as you can keep the hold for several seconds; increase the lean gradually over weeks.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Plank
description: An isometric core exercise that strengthens the entire midsection.
instructions: Place your forearms on the floor with elbows under your shoulders.
Extend your legs back and rise onto your toes.
Keep your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Brace your core and squeeze your glutes.
Hold the position for the desired duration.
Lower your knees to exit the hold.
formCues: Do not let your hips sag or pike up.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Plank Knee Tuck
description: A moving core drill performed from a high plank: the body holds its straight line while one knee is drawn in under the chest and sent back, alternating sides. Slower and more controlled than a mountain climber, it trains the abdominals and hip flexors while the shoulders and trunk stay braced.
instructions: Set up in a high plank with the hands under the shoulders and the body in a straight line from head to heels.
Press the floor away and brace the trunk so the hips neither sag nor pike.
Draw one knee in towards the chest without letting the hips rise.
Extend the leg back to the starting position under control.
Repeat with the other leg and keep alternating for the desired number of repetitions.
formCues: Keep the hips level with the shoulders; letting them lift turns this into a pike.
Pull the knee in with the abdominals rather than by hopping off the supporting foot.
Keep the shoulders stacked over the wrists and push the floor away so the upper body does not sink.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Plate-Loaded Donkey Calf Raise
alternativeNames: Elevación de Pantorrilla a la Burra en Máquina
description: A donkey calf raise on a plate-loaded machine, with a pad across the hips and the torso hinged forward so the calves are stretched at the bottom of every repetition.
instructions: Load the plate horns and step onto the platform with the balls of your feet on the edge and your heels hanging free.
Bend forward at the hips and settle the pad across your hips, then rest your forearms on the support in front of you.
Keep your knees straight and your back flat, with your torso close to parallel to the floor.
Push through the balls of your feet and raise your heels as high as you can, pausing briefly at the top.
Lower your heels below the platform until you feel a strong calf stretch, and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
formCues: The forward hinge is the exercise. Standing up straight turns this into an ordinary standing calf raise and gives away the extra stretch you came for.
Keep the knees straight throughout. Bending them shifts the work from the gastrocnemius to the soleus, which is the seated calf raise, not this one.
Let the heels drop all the way below the platform edge. The bottom of the range is where this machine earns its place, and cutting it short wastes the setup.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Plate-Loaded Glute Drive
alternativeNames: Empuje de Glúteo en Máquina de Discos
description: A machine hip thrust performed on a plate-loaded glute drive, where the built-in back pad and foot platform set the position so the hips can extend against the load without setting up a bench.
instructions: Load the plate horns evenly and sit into the machine with your upper back against the pad and your feet flat on the platform.
Pull the hip pad or lap bar across your hips and adjust it so it sits on the crease of the hips, not on your stomach.
Set your feet so that your shins will be roughly vertical when your hips are at the top, and take hold of the handles.
Drive your hips up by squeezing the glutes until your thighs are level with your torso, and hold briefly at the top.
Lower under control until your hips are just short of the bottom of the range, and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
formCues: Get the pad on the hip crease. Sitting it up on the stomach is the only genuinely uncomfortable thing this machine does, and it is fixed by moving the pad, not by adding padding.
Finish with the hips, not the lower back. If the ribs flare at the top you have run out of hip extension and started arching, which is where the machine stops training the glutes.
This is the hip thrust to reach for when the bench and barbell are taken -- the back pad and platform are part of the frame, so there is no setup to get wrong.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Plate-Loaded Lateral Raise
alternativeNames: Elevación Lateral en Máquina de Discos
description: A seated lateral raise on a plate-loaded machine, where pads bear against the upper arms so the side deltoids lift the load without the hands gripping it.
instructions: Set the seat height so that the pivot of the arm pads lines up with the point of your shoulders when you sit down.
Load the plate horns evenly on both sides and sit with your back flat against the pad.
Place the outside of your upper arms against the pads with your elbows bent and your arms hanging down.
Push out and up against the pads until your upper arms are roughly level with your shoulders.
Lower under control until your arms are back at your sides, and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
formCues: Set the seat first. If the pivot sits below your shoulder the pads drive your arm across your body instead of out to the side, and the side deltoid stops being the muscle doing the work.
Push with the arm, not the hand. The handles are there to stop your arms sliding off the pads -- gripping hard pulls the biceps and forearms into a raise that should be all deltoid.
Stop at shoulder height. Going higher hands the last part of the rep to the traps, and the machine will happily let you.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Plate-Loaded Seated Dip Machine
alternativeNames: Máquina de Fondos Sentado con Discos
description: A plate-loaded version of the seated dip machine: you sit with your back against the pad and press two lever arms down by your sides against weight plates loaded on a sleeve behind you. It trains the triceps along the same pressing path as the selectorized dip machine, with the resistance set by the plates you load.
instructions: Load the plates evenly on the sleeve and adjust the seat so the handles are at about shoulder height when you are seated.
Sit upright with your back against the pad and grip the handles at your sides with your elbows bent.
Keep your shoulders down and your chest up, then press the handles down by straightening your elbows.
Squeeze your triceps at the bottom, with your arms straight but not locked out hard.
Let the handles rise back up under control until your elbows are bent to about 90 degrees.
Repeat for the planned repetitions, then return the lever to its safety stop before you stand up.
formCues: Start light and add plates gradually; if the handles stop short of full extension the load is too heavy.
Keep the elbows close to your sides and your back against the pad so the work stays on the triceps.
Do not let the shoulders roll forward or shrug as the handles rise; stop where the stretch in the chest and shoulders is comfortable.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Plate-Loaded Shrug
alternativeNames: Encogimiento de Hombros en Máquina de Discos
description: A standing shrug on a plate-loaded machine, lifting handles that hang at your sides so the traps work without a bar in front of or behind the legs.
instructions: Load the plate horns evenly and stand on the machine platform, facing away from the frame.
Take a handle in each hand with your arms hanging straight down at your sides and your shoulders relaxed.
Stand tall with your chest up, your chin level and your knees soft.
Shrug your shoulders straight up toward your ears as high as they will go, and hold for a moment at the top.
Lower under control until your shoulders are fully down, and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
formCues: Shrug straight up. Rolling the shoulders adds travel but no extra trap work, and it takes the shoulder joint through a loaded circle for nothing.
Keep the arms straight and passive. Bending the elbows turns the movement into a short upright row and takes the load off the traps.
The handles hanging at your sides are what this machine is for -- there is no bar to clear your thighs, so you can stand upright and use a full range without shortening the top.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Plate Pinch
description: A grip-training staple: pinch a weight plate by its rim and hold it for time, loading the thumb and finger flexors in sustained isometric work.
instructions: Stand a weight plate on its edge on the floor.
Squat down and pinch the plate by its rim between the fingers and thumb of one hand — no handles, just pinch.
Stand up and hold the plate at the side for time, keeping the arm straight.
Set it back down under control.
Repeat on the other hand.
formCues: Start with a 5 kg / 10 lb plate and build up; pinching two plates together smooth-side out is a harder variation.
Chalk on the hands makes a huge difference; sweaty pinches fail fast.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Plate Pullover
description: A pullover holding a weight plate, working the lats, chest, and serratus.
instructions: Lie flat on a bench holding a plate with both hands.
Press the plate over the chest with arms nearly straight.
Lower the plate back in an arc behind the head until you feel a stretch.
Pull the plate back over the chest along the same arc.
Repeat for the prescribed reps.
formCues: Keep the elbows soft but locked at the same angle.
Stop at the bottom of your clean range — no excessive shoulder stretch.
Plant the feet firmly for stability.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Plow Pose
description: An inversion in which the legs pass overhead until the toes reach the floor behind the head, lengthening the whole back of the body.
instructions: Lie on your back with the arms alongside the body, palms down.
Lift both legs overhead and support the lower back with the hands.
Lower the toes towards the floor behind the head, keeping the legs as straight as comfort allows.
Hold the position for the prescribed time, breathing steadily and keeping the head still.
Roll down one vertebra at a time with the hands supporting the back.
formCues: Never turn the head while you are in the pose; the neck is loaded and must stay neutral.
Rest the toes on a chair or a stack of cushions if the floor is out of reach.
Skip this pose entirely if you have any neck complaints.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Plyo Lunge
description: An explosive split-stance jump that switches the legs in mid-air, alternating each rep.
instructions: Start in a forward lunge with one foot ahead of the other.
Drop into a deep lunge with the back knee almost touching the floor.
Drive both feet off the floor, switching legs in mid-air.
Land softly in a lunge with the opposite leg forward.
Continue alternating without pausing.
formCues: Land softly with bent knees to absorb impact.
Switch the leg position fully — do not just hop in place.
Keep the torso upright — do not pitch forward.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Preacher Curl
description: A curl variation using a preacher bench to isolate the biceps.
instructions: Sit at a preacher bench with your upper arms resting on the pad.
Hold an EZ-bar with an underhand grip.
Curl the bar up toward your shoulders.
Lower with control until arms are nearly straight.
Repeat.
formCues: Avoid bouncing at the bottom to protect the biceps tendon.
Keep your wrists neutral rather than letting them bend back.
Don't shrug your shoulders as the bar rises.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Preacher Hammer Curl
description: A biceps curl performed on a preacher bench with a neutral, hammer grip to emphasize the brachialis and forearms.
instructions: Sit at a preacher bench with a dumbbell in each hand.
Rest your upper arms on the pad with palms facing each other.
Curl the dumbbells up while keeping your wrists neutral.
Squeeze your biceps at the top of the movement.
Lower the dumbbells with control.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
formCues: Keep your upper arms flat against the pad.
Avoid locking out the elbows completely at the bottom.
Control the lowering phase rather than dropping the weight.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Pseudo Planche Push Ups
description: A push-up with hands turned back and shoulders leaned far past the wrists, mimicking planche loading.
instructions: Start in a push-up position with your hands turned so fingers point back.
Lean your shoulders forward past your wrists.
Lower your chest toward the floor by bending your elbows.
Keep your body in a straight line.
Press back up while maintaining the forward lean.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
formCues: The further you lean forward, the harder each rep becomes.
Keep your elbows close to your body as you lower.
Keep your shoulder blades protracted and your body rigid.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Puppy Pose
description: A kneeling pose halfway between child's pose and downward dog: the hips stay over the knees while the chest melts towards the floor, opening the shoulders and the upper back.
instructions: Kneel on all fours with the hips over the knees and the hands under the shoulders.
Walk the hands forward and lower the chest towards the floor, keeping the hips high.
Rest the forehead or the chin on the mat and let the armpits soften downwards.
Hold the position for the prescribed time, breathing into the upper back.
Walk the hands back and sit onto the heels to come out.
formCues: Keep the hips stacked over the knees; sitting back turns this into child's pose.
Press the palms down and lift the elbows off the floor to keep the arms working.
Rest the forehead on a block if the chest does not reach comfortably.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Push Jerk
description: An overhead lift using a leg dip and drive to launch the barbell overhead, caught in a quarter squat.
instructions: Hold a barbell in the front rack position at your shoulders.
Stand with feet hip-width apart.
Dip by bending your knees slightly.
Drive explosively through your legs and press the bar overhead.
Drop into a quarter-squat under the bar and lock out your arms.
Stand up fully and lower the bar to repeat.
formCues: Keep your torso upright during the dip.
Drive with your legs before pressing with your arms.
Lock your arms out as you drop under the bar.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Push Press
description: A barbell overhead press using leg drive to press heavier loads overhead.
instructions: Stand with a barbell racked on your front deltoids.
Dip slightly at the knees.
Drive up with your legs and press the bar overhead.
Lock out fully.
Lower to the start.
Repeat.
formCues: Use leg drive only to initiate — finish with the shoulders.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Pyramid Pose
description: A standing forward fold over a straight front leg in a short split stance, which isolates the hamstring of the front leg while both hips stay square.
instructions: Step one foot back about a leg's length and turn the back foot out slightly.
Square both hip points towards the front of the mat and keep both legs straight.
Hinge from the hips and fold over the front leg, bringing the hands to the floor, blocks or the shin.
Hold the fold for the prescribed time with the spine long rather than rounded.
Press into the feet to come up and repeat on the other side.
formCues: Shorten the stance until both hips can face forward; length is worth less than square hips.
Use blocks under the hands so the chest can keep reaching towards the shin.
Micro-bend the front knee if the hamstring grips.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Rack Pull
description: A partial-range deadlift variation performed from pins set at knee height, emphasizing the upper back, traps, and lockout strength with heavier-than-deadlift loads.
instructions: Set the safety pins in a power rack at knee height and place a loaded barbell on them.
Stand with feet hip-width apart and grip the bar just outside your legs.
Brace your core, retract your shoulder blades, and drive through your legs to lift the bar.
Lock out your hips and knees fully at the top.
Return the bar to the pins under control and reset before the next rep.
formCues: Use a hip-hinge pattern — keep the bar close to your body throughout.
Rack pulls allow loads well above your full deadlift max to overload the lockout.
Focus on upper back tightness to prevent rounding at heavy weights.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Rear Delt Fly
description: An isolation movement targeting the posterior deltoids and upper back.
instructions: Hold dumbbells and hinge forward at the hips.
With a slight bend in elbows, raise the dumbbells out to the sides.
Squeeze your shoulder blades at the top.
Lower with control.
Repeat.
formCues: Choose a light weight to keep the movement strict.
Avoid using momentum from the torso to swing the weights up.
Lead with your elbows rather than your hands.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Reclined Butterfly
description: A restful version of the butterfly stretch: lying back with the soles of your feet together and your knees dropped out to the sides, you open the inner thighs and hips under gravity. Resting your back and arms on the floor lets the legs relax into the stretch.
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent and the soles of your feet flat on the floor.
Bring the soles of your feet together and let both knees fall out to the sides.
Rest your arms on the floor with your palms up, or place your hands on your belly.
Keep your lower back resting on the floor and your shoulders relaxed.
Breathe slowly and let your knees sink toward the floor for the planned time.
Bring your knees together with your hands to finish.
formCues: Do not push the knees down with your hands; let gravity do the work so the inner thighs relax.
Slide your feet further from the hips to ease the stretch, or closer to deepen it.
Put a pillow or folded blanket under each knee if the stretch feels too strong.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Renegade Row
description: A plank-based rowing exercise in which a dumbbell in each hand is rowed alternately toward the hip while the other hand stays planted. It trains the back and arms while the trunk resists rotation.
instructions: Start in a high plank with a hand on each of two dumbbells, shoulder-width apart, and the feet set wide for stability.
Brace the trunk so the body forms a straight line from head to heels.
Row one dumbbell up toward the hip, driving the elbow back along the ribs.
Keep the hips square to the floor and do not let the body twist.
Lower the dumbbell to the floor under control.
Repeat on the other side and keep alternating.
formCues: Use hexagonal dumbbells so they do not roll, and start light.
Set the feet wider to make it easier to keep the hips level.
Do not shrug or twist; pause briefly at the top of each row to prove control.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Reverse Crunches
description: An abdominal exercise curling the hips off the floor to emphasize the lower portion of the abs.
instructions: Lie on your back with your arms at your sides.
Raise your legs with knees bent to 90 degrees.
Curl your hips off the floor by contracting your lower abs.
Bring your knees toward your chest.
Lower your hips with control.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
formCues: Curl your pelvis rather than swinging your legs for momentum.
Exhale as your hips lift to deepen the abdominal contraction.
Press your arms into the floor for added stability.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Reverse Curl
description: A barbell curl with an overhand grip targeting the brachialis and forearm extensors.
instructions: Stand and hold a barbell with an overhand grip.
Curl the bar up toward your shoulders.
Lower under control.
Repeat.
formCues: Move through a full range of motion.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Reverse Grip Bent Over Row
description: A barbell row performed with an underhand grip, shifting emphasis toward the lower lats and biceps.
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and grip a barbell underhand.
Hinge forward at the hips with a slight knee bend.
Let the bar hang with your arms extended.
Pull the bar to your lower abdomen by driving your elbows back.
Squeeze your back at the top.
Lower the bar with control.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
formCues: Keep your back flat and your core braced throughout.
Maintain a fixed torso angle instead of heaving upright as you pull.
Keep the bar close to your legs throughout the movement.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Reverse Grip Lat Pulldown
description: A lat pulldown variation using an underhand grip that increases biceps involvement.
instructions: Attach a straight bar to a lat pulldown machine.
Grip the bar with an underhand grip, shoulder-width apart.
Sit and secure your thighs under the pad.
Pull the bar down to your upper chest.
Squeeze your lats and biceps at the bottom.
Return the bar to the starting position with control.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
formCues: Keep your chest up and avoid leaning back excessively.
Pull with your elbows, not just your hands.
Squeeze your lats at the bottom of the movement.
