breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Reverse Lunge
description: A lunge variation stepping backward for better knee stability.
instructions: Stand holding dumbbells at your sides.
Step one leg back and lower your knee toward the floor.
Lower until your front thigh is parallel to the floor.
Push through your front heel to return to standing.
Repeat on both sides.
formCues: Keep the front knee tracking in line with your toes.
Stay upright through the torso rather than leaning forward.
Lower the back knee softly instead of dropping it to the floor.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Reverse Nordic Curl
description: A bodyweight quadriceps exercise performed kneeling, leaning the torso backward under control while keeping the hips extended.
instructions: Kneel on a pad with your knees hip-width apart, shins and the tops of your feet on the floor, and your torso upright.
Keep your hips extended and core braced.
Slowly lean your torso backward while keeping your body in a straight line.
Lower as far as you can control with your quadriceps.
Pull yourself back up to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
formCues: Keep your hips extended throughout — don't let them fold.
Lower only as far as you can control.
Use a pad under the knees for comfort.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Reverse Plank
description: An isometric hold with the body facing upward, training the glutes, spinal erectors, and shoulder stability.
instructions: Sit on the floor with your legs extended in front of you.
Place your hands behind you with fingers pointing toward your feet.
Lift your hips off the floor to form a straight line from head to heels.
Squeeze your glutes and brace your core.
Hold the position for the desired duration.
Lower your hips with control to exit.
formCues: Don't let your hips sag as the hold progresses.
Keep your gaze up to maintain a neutral neck.
Press evenly through your palms to reduce wrist strain.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Reverse Plank Dips
description: Triceps dips from a straight-leg reverse plank: the legs stay extended and the hips high while the elbows bend and straighten.
instructions: Sit with the legs straight and the hands on the floor behind the hips, fingers pointing forward.
Press into the hands and heels and lift the hips into a straight-leg reverse plank.
Bend the elbows straight back and lower the hips a short way towards the floor.
Push back up until the arms lock out, keeping the hips high.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
formCues: Keep the hips lifted at the bottom; sitting down between reps removes the load.
Keep the elbows tracking straight back rather than flaring outwards.
Bend the knees if the straight-leg version is too demanding on the hamstrings.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Reverse Tabletop Hip Pulses
alternativeNames: Pulsos de Cadera en Mesa Invertida
description: Glute pulses from the reverse tabletop position: the arms stay straight and only the hips drop and lift, which keeps the work in the glutes rather than the triceps.
instructions: Sit with the knees bent, the feet flat and the hands on the floor behind you.
Press into the hands and feet and lift the hips until the trunk is level with the knees.
Keeping the elbows straight, lower the hips a few centimetres.
Squeeze the glutes to lift them back to level.
Pulse for the desired number of repetitions and lower down.
formCues: Keep the arms locked: bending the elbows turns this into a dip.
Drive the lift from the heels and the glutes, not from the lower back.
Keep the chest open and the shoulders down away from the ears.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Reverse Tabletop Hold
description: A static reverse tabletop: knees bent, hands under the shoulders behind the body, hips lifted level with the knees and held, so the glutes and the whole back of the trunk work isometrically.
instructions: Sit with the knees bent, the feet flat and the hands on the floor behind you, fingers pointing towards the heels.
Press into the hands and feet and lift the hips until the trunk is level with the knees.
Open the chest, draw the shoulders away from the ears and look straight ahead.
Hold the position for the prescribed time with the hips high.
Lower the hips under control to finish.
formCues: Push the floor away rather than hanging on the shoulders.
Keep the knees stacked over the ankles and pointing straight ahead.
Let the head follow the line of the spine instead of dropping it back.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Revolved Chair Pose
description: Chair pose with a closed twist: the hips stay level and low while the chest rotates and one elbow hooks outside the opposite thigh.
instructions: Set up in chair pose with the knees bent, the hips back and the palms together at the chest.
Keep the knees level with each other so the hips do not open into the twist.
Rotate the chest to one side and hook the opposite elbow outside that thigh.
Press the palms together and hold for the prescribed time, lengthening the spine on each inhale.
Come back to centre and repeat on the other side.
formCues: Line the knees up before you twist; a knee sliding forward fakes most of the rotation.
Rotate from the mid-back rather than pulling with the arm against the leg.
Keep the weight in the heels so the position stays a squat, not a lean.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Revolved Crescent Lunge
description: A high lunge with a closed twist: the back heel stays lifted, the hips face forward and the chest rotates over the front thigh.
instructions: Step into a high lunge with the front knee over the ankle and the back heel lifted.
Bring the palms together at the chest and square both hips towards the front of the mat.
Rotate the chest towards the front leg and hook the opposite elbow outside the thigh.
Hold the twist for the prescribed time, pressing the back heel towards the wall behind you.
Unwind and repeat on the other side.
formCues: Keep the back leg straight and long; it is what stops the twist collapsing into the hips.
Drop the back knee to the floor for an easier version with the same rotation.
Lengthen the spine first, then rotate — twisting a rounded back gets you nowhere.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Ring Dead Hang
description: A passive hang from gymnastic rings. The free-rotating grip recruits more stabilisers in the hands, forearms, and shoulder girdle than a fixed bar.
instructions: Grip a pair of gymnastic rings with a neutral grip, palms facing each other.
Hang with your arms fully extended and feet off the ground.
Let the rings rotate naturally; do not fight the grip.
Keep your shoulders engaged (no shrug to the ears) and core lightly braced.
Hold for the desired duration.
formCues: Breathe steadily rather than holding your breath.
Build hold duration gradually as your grip strengthens.
Step down under control before your grip fails completely.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Ring Face Pull
description: A face pull using gymnastic rings for adjustable resistance and improved shoulder health.
instructions: Grip the rings and lean back so your body is at an angle.
Pull the rings toward your face, flaring elbows to the sides.
Hold briefly, then return.
Repeat.
formCues: Adjust your body angle to control difficulty.
Externally rotate your arms at the top.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Ring L-Sit
description: A static L-sit performed in the support position on gymnastic rings: the arms are locked, the body is held off the floor and the legs reach straight forward. The unstable rings make it a demanding test of core, shoulder and arm strength.
instructions: Set the rings at about hip height and grip them with the arms straight beside the body.
Press down on the rings and lift the body into the support position, with the shoulders pushed down and away from the ears.
Turn the rings out slightly, brace the abdominals and raise the straight legs until they are parallel to the floor.
Hold the position, keeping the rings steady and the knees locked.
Lower the legs, then the body, under control.
formCues: Keep the arms locked and the shoulders pushed down; do not sag between the rings.
Build up from tucked holds, and from parallettes or a dip station, before moving to rings.
Point the toes and squeeze the legs together.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Ring Muscle-Up
description: An advanced calisthenics movement combining a pull-up and a dip on gymnastic rings.
instructions: Hang from the rings with a false grip, palms facing each other.
Pull explosively, driving the chest up to the rings.
Transition the elbows over the rings as the chest rises.
Press to full arm extension at the top.
Lower under control through the transition back to the hang.
formCues: A false grip is essential for the transition.
Drive the elbows down hard during the transition.
Build the strength with negatives and band-assisted reps first.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Ring Plank
description: A plank held with the hands in gymnastic rings and the feet on the floor. The rings move freely, so the shoulders and trunk have to work harder to keep the body in a straight line.
instructions: Set the rings at about knee height and take hold of them with the arms straight under the shoulders.
Step the feet back into a plank, with the body in a straight line from head to heels.
Brace the abdominals and glutes and press the rings down and slightly out to keep them steady.
Hold the position without letting the hips sag or the rings drift apart.
Step the feet in and stand up to finish.
formCues: Keep the rings directly under the shoulders; if they swing, place the feet wider.
Push the floor away through the rings so the shoulder blades stay wide.
Raise the rings to make the hold easier and lower them to make it harder.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Ring Push-Up
description: A push-up performed on gymnastic rings, increasing the demand on stabilizers in the chest, shoulders, and core.
instructions: Set the rings just above floor height.
Grip the rings and assume a plank position with arms straight.
Lower the chest toward the rings, keeping the elbows close to the body.
Press back up to full arm extension.
Repeat for the prescribed reps.
formCues: Keep the rings turned out at the top to engage the chest.
Brace the core — the rings will magnify any wobble.
Drop to knees to scale the difficulty.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Ring Row
description: A bodyweight row on gymnastic rings, performed at an angle for back and biceps work.
instructions: Set the rings at hip to chest height.
Grip the rings with palms facing each other, lean back at an angle with arms straight.
Brace the core and pull the chest toward the rings.
Squeeze the shoulder blades together at the top.
Lower under control to a full-arm extension.
formCues: The lower the body angle, the harder the row.
Keep the body in a straight line — do not let the hips sag.
Pull the elbows back, not flared out, for more lat involvement.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Ring Support Hold
description: The basic gymnastic rings position: you hold yourself above the rings with your arms locked and your body tall. The unstable rings force the shoulders, chest and triceps to keep the arms steady, and it is the foundation for ring dips and many other ring skills.
instructions: Hang the rings at about hip height and take one ring in each hand, with your thumbs wrapped around the ring.
Press up so that your arms are straight and your body is lifted off the floor above the rings.
Turn your palms slightly outward so the rings sit beside your hips, with your elbows locked.
Push down on the rings and keep your shoulders away from your ears, with your chest lifted.
Squeeze your glutes and keep your legs together, with your feet pointed.
Hold the position for the planned time, then lower down under control.
formCues: Keep the rings close to your body and still; any wobble tells you which side needs more control.
Press the shoulders down and away from the ears instead of letting them shrug up.
Start with the rings low and your feet on the floor if you cannot hold the position with straight arms.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Rings Inverted Row
description: A bodyweight row on gymnastic rings hung low, pulling the chest up to the rings from a straight, inclined body line; more challenging than a standing ring row.
instructions: Set the rings just above hip height.
Lie under the rings and grip them with palms facing each other.
Walk the feet forward so the body forms a straight line.
Pull the chest toward the rings, squeezing the shoulder blades.
Lower under control to a full-arm extension.
formCues: Keep the body in a straight line — heels through head.
Squeeze the glutes and core to prevent sagging.
Elevate the feet on a box for a harder version.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Romanian Deadlift
description: A hip-hinge movement emphasizing the hamstrings and glutes.
instructions: Stand holding a barbell at hip level with an overhand grip.
Hinge at the hips, pushing them back while keeping legs nearly straight.
Lower the bar along your legs until you feel a hamstring stretch.
Drive your hips forward to return to standing.
Repeat.
formCues: Keep your spine neutral and avoid rounding the lower back.
Maintain the same slight knee bend for the entire rep.
Go only as deep as your hamstring flexibility allows.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Rowing Machine
description: A full-body cardio machine movement in which each stroke drives with the legs, swings the torso back and pulls the handle to the ribs, training the legs, back and arms in one continuous cycle.
instructions: Sit on the rower, strap your feet into the footplates and take the handle with an overhand grip.
Slide forward into the catch: shins vertical, torso leaning slightly ahead of the hips, arms straight out toward the flywheel.
Drive through your legs first, pushing the seat back until your knees are almost straight.
Swing your torso back past vertical, then pull the handle in to your lower ribs with your elbows travelling past your sides.
Reverse the order on the recovery — arms away, torso forward, then bend the knees — and slide back to the catch for the next stroke.
Continue for the desired time, distance or number of strokes.
formCues: Keep the order: legs, then body, then arms on the drive, and arms, body, legs on the recovery. Breaking the arms early wastes the strongest part of the stroke.
Row with a flat back and a braced core — rounding the lower back at the catch is what turns rowing into a back ache instead of conditioning.
Let the handle travel in a straight, level line to the lower ribs, and make the recovery about twice as slow as the drive rather than rushing back to the catch.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Sandbag Carry
description: A loaded carry in which you hold a sandbag against your chest in a bear hug and walk with it. The awkward, shifting load makes your legs, trunk and arms work together and challenges your grip and posture over the whole walk.
instructions: Stand over a sandbag, squat down and wrap both arms around it, with your hands or forearms locked together underneath it.
Lift the sandbag by standing up, and hold it tight against your chest.
Brace your trunk and keep your chest tall, with the bag high enough that it does not pull your shoulders forward.
Walk forward with short, controlled steps for the planned distance or time.
Keep squeezing the bag throughout the walk.
Lower the bag to the floor with a straight back by squatting down.
formCues: Hold the bag high on your chest; if it slides down, your lower back takes the load.
Take short steps and keep your hips level rather than swaying with the bag.
Start with a lighter bag until you can walk the full distance with a tall posture.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Corpse Pose
description: The closing rest of a practice: lying flat on the back with the body completely passive, letting the effects of the session settle.
instructions: Lie on your back with the legs a comfortable distance apart and the feet falling open.
Rest the arms slightly away from the body with the palms facing up.
Let the whole body soften into the floor, including the jaw, the eyes and the hands.
Stay for the prescribed time, breathing naturally without controlling the breath.
Bend the knees and roll to one side before sitting up slowly.
formCues: Place a bolster under the knees if the lower back does not settle.
Cover yourself with a blanket; the body cools quickly once it stops moving.
This pose is meant to require no effort at all — resist the urge to adjust constantly.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Scapular Pull Ups
description: A straight-arm hang exercise lifting the chest by depressing and retracting the shoulder blades, building pull-up strength.
instructions: Hang from a pull-up bar with arms fully extended.
Keep your arms straight throughout the movement.
Depress and retract your shoulder blades to lift your chest.
Pause briefly at the top of the movement.
Return to a fully hanging position.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
formCues: Think of pulling your shoulder blades down into your back pockets.
Avoid swinging or kipping to keep the movement strict.
Focus on small, precise movement quality rather than maximum height.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Scissor Kicks
description: A core exercise performed lying on the back, alternating straight-leg crosses to target the lower abdominals and hip flexors.
instructions: Lie flat on your back with your hands under your glutes.
Lift both legs a few inches off the floor.
Alternate crossing one leg over the other in a scissor motion.
Keep your lower back pressed into the floor.
Maintain a steady rhythm throughout.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
formCues: Press your lower back into the floor throughout.
Keep your legs straight and close to the ground.
Move with control rather than speed.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Seated Barbell Overhead Press
alternativeNames: Press de Barra sobre la Cabeza Sentado
description: A strict seated overhead press with a barbell, removing hip drive and isolating the deltoids and triceps.
instructions: Set an upright bench inside a rack with the pins at about shoulder height when seated.
Sit with your back flat against the pad and unrack the barbell at the front of the shoulders.
Press the bar overhead until the arms are fully extended, tucking the head through at the top.
Lower the bar back to the collarbones under control.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.
formCues: Keep the ribs down and glutes tight; do not lean back into a bench press.
Drive the bar straight up, not forward.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Seated Cable Row
description: A back exercise performed on a cable row machine, pulling a handle toward the torso while seated.
instructions: Sit at the cable row station and place your feet on the footrests.
Grip the handle and sit upright with a slight forward lean.
Drive your elbows back and pull the handle toward your lower abdomen.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the end of the pull.
Extend your arms under control back to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
formCues: Keep your torso upright with minimal rocking.
Drive your elbows straight back, not out to the sides.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the end of the pull.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Seated Calf Raise
description: A machine calf raise performed seated to specifically target the soleus muscle.
instructions: Sit at a calf raise machine with the pads resting on your thighs.
Lower your heels as far as possible.
Raise up onto your toes.
Lower under control.
Repeat.
formCues: The bent knee slackens the gastrocnemius, so the soleus does more of the work.
Use a full range of motion.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Seated Dip Machine
description: A selectorized machine version of the dip: seated upright with your back against the pad, you press two lever arms down by your sides until your arms are straight. The movement follows the path of a bodyweight dip, but the load is the weight you select on the stack, and the seat takes your body weight.
instructions: Select your weight on the stack and adjust the seat so the handles are at about shoulder height when you are seated.
Sit upright with your back against the pad and grip the handles at your sides with your elbows bent.
Keep your shoulders down and your chest up, then press the handles down by straightening your elbows.
Squeeze your triceps at the bottom, with your arms straight but not locked out hard.
Let the handles rise back up under control until your elbows are bent to about 90 degrees.
Repeat for the planned repetitions, keeping your back against the pad.
formCues: Keep the elbows close to your sides so the work stays on the triceps.
Do not let the shoulders roll forward or shrug as the handles rise; stop where the stretch in the chest and shoulders is comfortable.
Keep your back against the pad; leaning forward shifts the work toward the chest.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Seated Dumbbell Curl
description: A seated bicep curl with dumbbells, the upright seated position removing body momentum for stricter form.
instructions: Sit on a bench with a dumbbell in each hand.
Let your arms hang at your sides with palms facing forward.
Curl both dumbbells toward your shoulders by flexing your biceps.
Squeeze at the top of the movement.
Lower the dumbbells with control.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
formCues: Keep your elbows pinned at your sides throughout.
Avoid leaning back to help lift the weight.
Straighten your arms fully at the bottom of each rep.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Seated Dumbbell Lateral Raise
description: A seated isolation exercise raising dumbbells out to the sides, targeting the side deltoids without leg drive.
instructions: Sit on a bench with a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
Keep your back upright and core braced.
Raise both dumbbells out to the sides until they reach shoulder height.
Keep a slight bend in your elbows.
Lower the dumbbells with control.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
formCues: Use a light weight to keep the raise strict.
Lead with your elbows rather than your hands.
Raise to shoulder height and lower with control.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Seated Dumbbell Tricep Extension
alternativeNames: Extensión de Tríceps con Mancuerna Sentado
description: A seated overhead extension lowering a dumbbell behind the head, stretching and working the triceps.
instructions: Sit on a bench with a dumbbell held overhead in both hands.
Keep your upper arms vertical next to your ears.
Lower the dumbbell behind your head by bending your elbows.
Extend your arms to press the dumbbell back overhead.
Squeeze your triceps at the top.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
formCues: Keep your upper arms vertical next to your ears.
Move only your forearms, keeping the elbows still.
Brace your core to avoid arching your lower back.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Seated Forward Fold
description: A seated stretch that targets the hamstrings and lower back by reaching the torso over straight legs.
instructions: Sit on the floor with both legs straight out in front.
Keep your back long and hinge forward from the hips.
Reach your hands toward your feet.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
formCues: Lead with your chest, not your head, to keep the back long.
Stretch to mild tension, never to pain.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Seated Leg Curl
description: A machine isolation exercise for the hamstrings performed in a seated position, providing consistent tension and reduced hip flexor involvement compared to the lying variant.
instructions: Adjust the seat back and ankle pad so your knees align with the machine's pivot point.
Sit upright, place the backs of your ankles on top of the pad, and grip the handles.
Curl your lower legs down and back under the seat as far as the machine allows.
Pause at peak contraction, then return the weight slowly to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired reps.
formCues: Keep your back firmly against the backrest throughout the movement.
Point toes slightly toward your shins at peak contraction to increase hamstring activation.
Control the eccentric phase — do not let the weight pull your legs back quickly.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Seated Smith Machine Shoulder Press
alternativeNames: Press de Hombros en Máquina Smith Sentado
description: A seated overhead press on the Smith machine, using the fixed bar path to keep the focus on the deltoids.
instructions: Position a bench inside a Smith machine.
Sit facing forward with the bar at shoulder height.
Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Unrack and press the bar straight up until your arms are extended.
Lower the bar back to shoulder height with control.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
formCues: Align the bench so the bar tracks just in front of your nose.
Brace your core to keep the lower back from over-arching.
Plant your feet firmly on the floor for a stable base.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Seated Spinal Twist
description: A seated rotation that stretches the obliques, mid-back and glutes by twisting toward a bent knee.
instructions: Sit with one leg straight and cross the other foot over it.
Brace the opposite elbow against the outside of the bent knee.
Rotate your torso toward the bent knee and look over your shoulder.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
Switch sides and repeat.
formCues: Sit tall and lengthen your spine before twisting.
Twist from the mid-back, not the lower back.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Seated Straddle Stretch
description: A wide-legged seated stretch for the inner thighs and hamstrings, folding the torso forward between the legs.
instructions: Sit with your legs straight and spread wide in a V.
Keep your back long and hinge forward from the hips.
Walk your hands forward along the floor.
Hold for 20 to 30 seconds, breathing steadily.
formCues: Keep your toes pointing up, not rolled in.
Ease into the stretch slowly — never bounce.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Shrimp Squat
description: An advanced single-leg squat in which you hold the rear foot behind you and lower until your back knee touches the floor. The working leg does all the lifting through a deep range, which makes it a demanding test of quad strength, hip control and balance.
instructions: Stand on one leg, bend the other knee and hold that foot behind you with the same-side hand.
Hold your arms and chest steady and begin to bend the standing knee, sitting your hips down and slightly back.
Lower until the back knee lightly touches the floor behind the standing foot.
Keep your chest up and your standing heel on the floor throughout the descent.
Press through the whole standing foot and straighten that leg to return to standing without letting go of the rear foot.
Complete the planned repetitions, then repeat on the other leg.
formCues: Touch the floor with the knee lightly and do not drop onto it; control the descent with the standing leg.
Lean the trunk forward a little to keep your balance; the front knee tracks over the toes and the heel stays down.
Learn the movement first by holding a support with your free hand or lowering onto a folded mat.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Side Lunge
description: A lateral lunge stepping wide to one side, training the quads, glutes, and inner thighs through a side-to-side pattern.
instructions: Stand with feet hip-width apart and hands at your chest.
Step one leg wide to the side, keeping the other leg straight.
Bend the stepping knee and push your hips back into a lateral squat.
Keep your chest up and the working heel planted.
Drive through the bent leg to return to standing.
Complete reps on one side, then switch.
formCues: Push your hips back as you bend the stepping knee.
Keep your trailing leg straight and both heels planted.
Keep your chest up rather than rounding forward.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Side-Lying Hip Abduction
alternativeNames: Abducción de Cadera Acostado de Lado
description: A bodyweight isolation exercise targeting the gluteus medius and hip abductors.
instructions: Lie on your side with legs stacked.
Keep the bottom leg slightly bent.
Raise the top leg toward the ceiling.
Lower under control.
Repeat on both sides.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Side-Lying Hip Abduction Hold
alternativeNames: Abducción de Cadera Acostado de Lado Isométrica
description: The top of the side-lying leg raise held for time: lying on one side with the top leg lifted and slightly behind the body, loading the glute medius isometrically.
instructions: Lie on one side with the legs stacked and straight, and support the head on the lower arm.
Brace the trunk so the torso stays square and does not roll backwards.
Lift the top leg to about 30 to 45 degrees, keeping the toes pointing forward.
Hold the leg there for the prescribed time, breathing normally.
Lower the leg under control and repeat on the other side.
formCues: Turning the toes towards the ceiling shifts the work to the hip flexor; keep them facing forward.
Take the leg slightly behind the line of the body to bias the glute medius.
Rest the top hand on the floor in front of you if balance is the limiting factor.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Side Lying Hip Adduction
alternativeNames: Aducción de Cadera Acostado de Lado
description: A side-lying exercise raising the bottom leg against gravity, training hip adduction with body weight alone.
instructions: Lie on your side with your bottom leg straight.
Bend your top leg and place its foot flat in front of the bottom thigh.
Support your head with your bottom arm.
Lift the bottom leg upward toward the ceiling.
Lower the leg back down under control.
Complete reps on one side, then switch.
formCues: Keep your hips stacked vertically to avoid rolling backward.
Keep the movement slow and deliberate through the short range of motion.
Pause briefly at the top of each lift.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Side-Lying Hip Adduction Hold
alternativeNames: Aducción de Cadera Acostado de Lado Isométrica
description: The top of the side-lying inner-thigh raise held for time: lying on one side with the top leg crossed over and the bottom leg lifted off the floor by the adductors.
instructions: Lie on one side with the bottom leg straight and the top leg crossed over it, foot flat on the floor.
Support the head on the lower arm and keep the hips stacked vertically.
Lift the bottom leg as high as it will go with the knee straight and the toes pointing forward.
Hold that lifted position for the prescribed time without rolling the hips back.
Lower the leg under control and repeat on the other side.
formCues: The range is short; a few centimetres of lift with a still pelvis beats a big swing.
Keep the lifted leg in line with the torso rather than drifting forward.
Press the top foot lightly into the floor if you need to steady the position.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Side-Lying Lateral Raise
description: A dumbbell lateral deltoid isolation exercise performed lying on one side on a flat bench, providing constant tension and eliminating momentum from the standing position.
instructions: Lie on your side on a flat bench with your bottom arm supporting your head or gripping the bench edge.
Hold a dumbbell in your top hand with your arm resting along your side.
Keeping your elbow slightly bent, raise the dumbbell upward until your arm is perpendicular to the floor.
Pause briefly at the top, then lower the dumbbell slowly back to your side.
Complete all reps on one side before switching.
formCues: Keep your torso still — only the working arm should move.
The lying position removes momentum and isolates the lateral deltoid effectively.
Use a lighter weight than your standing lateral raise — the leverage is more challenging.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Side Plank with Leg Lift
alternativeNames: Plancha Lateral con Elevación de Pierna
description: A side plank with the top leg raising up, combining lateral core work with hip abduction.
instructions: Lie on your side with the forearm on the floor, elbow under the shoulder.
Stack the feet and lift the hips into a side plank.
From this stable side plank, raise the top leg straight up toward the ceiling.
Lower the leg back down with control without dropping the hips.
Complete reps on one side, then switch.
formCues: Keep the hips lifted the entire set — do not let them sag.
Lead the leg lift with the heel, not the toes.
Keep the body in one straight line from head to bottom foot.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Side Plank Leg Lift Hold
alternativeNames: Plancha Lateral con Elevación de Pierna Isométrica
description: A side plank held with the top leg raised: the hips stay lifted and square while the top leg is abducted, adding a glute medius demand to the lateral trunk hold.
instructions: Set up in a side plank on the forearm with the elbow under the shoulder and the feet stacked.
Lift the hips until the body forms a straight line from the ankles to the head.
Raise the top leg to roughly hip height, keeping the toes pointing forward.
Hold the position for the prescribed time, keeping the hips high and the supporting shoulder stacked over the elbow.
Lower the leg and the hips under control and repeat on the other side.
formCues: Push the supporting shoulder away from the ear so the chest does not collapse towards the floor.
Stop the set when the hips start to drop, not when the leg gets tired.
Bend the bottom knee to the floor for an easier version that keeps the leg lift intact.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Single-Arm Chest-Supported Dumbbell Row
alternativeNames: Remo con Mancuerna a Una Mano con Pecho Apoyado
description: A unilateral row performed one arm at a time on a chest-supported incline bench, isolating each side of the back and reducing momentum.
instructions: Lie face-down on an incline bench holding a dumbbell in one hand, arm hanging straight down.
Row the dumbbell up to your side, driving your elbow past your torso.
Squeeze your shoulder blade at the top, then lower under control.
Complete all reps on one side before switching arms.
formCues: Working one side at a time lets you focus on a full contraction without the other arm compensating.
Keep your chest pressed into the bench throughout to avoid using momentum.
Match the rep count on both sides to avoid imbalances.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Single-Arm Dumbbell Row
alternativeNames: Remo con Mancuerna a Un Brazo
description: A unilateral back exercise using a dumbbell for balanced development.
instructions: Place one knee and hand on a bench for support.
Hold a dumbbell in the other hand with arm extended.
Pull the dumbbell up toward your hip, squeezing your shoulder blade.
Lower the dumbbell with control.
Repeat on both sides.
formCues: Avoid rotating the torso to hoist the weight higher.
Let your arm extend fully at the bottom for a complete stretch.
Keep your back flat from head to hips throughout the set.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Single Arm Dumbbell Bench Press
alternativeNames: Press de Banca con Mancuerna a Un Brazo
description: A flat-bench press performed with one dumbbell at a time. The unilateral load trains the chest, shoulder and triceps while the trunk works to keep the body from rotating off the bench.
instructions: Lie back on a flat bench with the feet planted on the floor and a dumbbell held at chest level in one hand.
Rest the free hand on your stomach or hold it out to the side for balance.
Press the dumbbell up over the chest until the arm is straight.
Pause briefly at the top without letting the body roll toward the pressing arm.
Lower the dumbbell slowly to the side of the chest.
Complete the repetitions on one side, then switch arms.
formCues: Squeeze the glutes and keep the shoulder blades pinned to the bench to resist rotation.
Lower to the side of the chest, with the elbow about 45 degrees from the body.
Use a weight you can hold level without twisting; add load only when both sides match.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Single-Arm Dumbbell Overhead Tricep Extension
alternativeNames: Extensión de Tríceps sobre la Cabeza con Mancuerna a Un Brazo
description: A one-arm overhead tricep extension giving a long, unilateral stretch of the long head and training anti-side-bend core stability.
instructions: Stand or sit holding a dumbbell in one hand overhead, arm fully extended.
The palm faces forward; the other hand can hold your waist or an upright for stability.
Bend the elbow to lower the dumbbell behind the head in a controlled arc.
Keep the upper arm vertical and close to the head throughout.
Extend the elbow to return the dumbbell overhead.
Complete all reps on one side, then switch.
formCues: Only the forearm moves — the upper arm stays glued in place.
Don't let the torso lean to the side; this is also a core exercise.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Single-Arm Hammer Curl
description: A unilateral dumbbell curl with a neutral grip that keeps the working elbow close to the torso while the brachialis and brachioradialis flex the elbow.
instructions: Stand with your feet about hip-width apart and hold one dumbbell at your side with the palm facing inward.
Brace your trunk and keep the working upper arm beside your ribs as the arm hangs straight.
Curl the dumbbell toward your shoulder without rotating the palm or swinging the torso.
Squeeze the elbow flexors at the top, then lower the dumbbell under control until the arm is straight.
Complete the repetitions on one side, then switch arms and repeat.
formCues: Let the weaker arm set the repetitions and weight so both sides receive the same work.
Keep the wrist neutral and the shoulder quiet; the movement should come from bending the elbow.
Use a controlled lowering phase instead of dropping the dumbbell from the top.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Single-Arm Machine Shoulder Press
alternativeNames: Press de hombros unilateral en máquina
description: A unilateral seated machine shoulder press that lets one arm press independently while the back stays supported and the machine controls the resistance path.
instructions: Adjust the seat so the working handle starts around shoulder height and sit with your back firmly against the pad.
Grip one handle with the wrist straight and keep the free hand on the support or resting comfortably.
Press the handle upward without leaning away from the back pad or rotating the torso.
Lower the handle under control until the elbow is just below the starting line, then repeat.
Complete the repetitions on one side, adjust the seat if needed, and train the other side.
formCues: Start with the weaker arm and let it set the weight and repetitions for both sides.
Keep the ribs down and the back against the pad instead of leaning away from the working arm.
Stop short of a painful shoulder position; the machine path should feel controlled from bottom to top.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Single-Arm Plank
description: A harder plank in which one hand leaves the floor so you hold the position on a single arm. With one support gone, the trunk has to resist twisting, which works the obliques and deep abdominals far more than a standard plank.
instructions: Set up in a high plank with your hands under your shoulders and your feet a little wider than hip-width.
Brace your trunk and squeeze your glutes to keep your body in one straight line.
Shift your weight onto one arm and lift the other hand off the floor, resting it on your hip or behind your back.
Keep your hips and shoulders level and square to the floor.
Hold for the planned time, then replace the hand and rest.
Repeat on the other arm.
formCues: Place your feet wider than usual to give yourself a more stable base.
Stop the hips from twisting toward the lifted arm; the body should stay as flat as in a normal plank.
Progress by shortening the lift time first, then lengthen it as the trunk gets stronger.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Single-Arm Plate-Loaded Lateral Raise
alternativeNames: Elevación Lateral a Un Brazo en Máquina de Discos
description: The plate-loaded machine lateral raise worked one arm at a time, so each side lifts its own load and the two can be trained to the same standard.
instructions: Set the seat height so the pad pivot lines up with your shoulder, and load only the side you are about to work.
Sit with your back flat against the pad and place the outside of your working upper arm against its pad.
Hold the handle on the free side or rest that hand in your lap, and keep your torso square to the seat.
Push the working arm out and up against the pad until the upper arm is level with your shoulder, then lower it under control.
Complete all the repetitions on that side, then load and work the other side.
formCues: Match the sides on the weaker arm, not the stronger one. Working one side at a time only tells you about an imbalance if you let the weaker side set the number.
Do not let the torso tip toward the working side. With load on one arm only, the machine no longer balances itself and leaning turns the raise into a side bend.
Start with the weaker arm so it sets the target, and give both sides the same rest.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Single Arm Tricep Pushdown
alternativeNames: Extensión de Tríceps a Un Brazo en Polea
description: A triceps isolation exercise performed one arm at a time on a cable machine with a single handle.
instructions: Attach a single handle to a high cable pulley.
Grasp the handle with one hand and keep your elbow pinned to your side.
Press the handle down until your arm is fully extended.
Squeeze the triceps at the bottom.
Slowly return to the start position.
Complete reps on one side, then switch.
formCues: Keep your elbow pinned to your side throughout.
Avoid leaning forward to add momentum.
Fully extend your arm at the bottom for a complete contraction.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Single Dumbbell Svend Press
description: A standing chest press holding one dumbbell upright between the palms, where the inward squeeze rather than the load is what works the pecs.
instructions: Stand tall and hold a single dumbbell upright in front of your sternum, the handle running vertically between your flat palms.
Squeeze your palms hard into the dumbbell so the chest takes the tension and the weight cannot slip.
Press the dumbbell straight forward until your arms are almost straight, keeping it at chest height the whole way out.
Pause briefly without letting the squeeze go, then draw the dumbbell back to your chest under control.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.
formCues: The squeeze on the dumbbell is what makes the exercise. If you are gripping the handle instead of crushing the weight between flat palms, the chest is not working.
Use a light dumbbell. Your palms hold it up on friction alone, so the grip sets the ceiling long before the chest does.
Keep the elbows slightly bent at the lockout and the dumbbell at sternum height throughout; letting it sag toward the hips takes the pecs out of it.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Single-Leg Box Squat
alternativeNames: Sentadilla en Caja a Una Pierna
description: A single-leg squat in which you sit back onto a box and stand up again on the same leg, with the other leg held out in front of you. The box limits the depth and gives you a target to reach, so it is a controlled way to build toward the pistol squat.
instructions: Stand in front of a sturdy box or bench that is about knee height, with your back to it.
Shift your weight onto one leg and lift the other leg out in front of you, with your arms stretched forward for balance.
Push your hips back and bend the standing knee, lowering yourself under control toward the box.
Sit lightly on the box without dropping onto it, keeping your chest up and the free leg off the floor.
Press through the whole standing foot and straighten that leg to stand up again.
Complete the planned repetitions, then repeat on the other leg.
formCues: Choose a higher box to start; lower it as your strength and control improve.
Keep the knee of the standing leg tracking over your toes and your heel on the floor.
Touch the box with your hips rather than relaxing onto it, and use the arms as a counterweight.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Single Leg Calf Raise
alternativeNames: Elevación de Pantorrilla a Una Pierna
description: A unilateral calf raise that loads one calf at a time, exposing strength imbalances side to side.
instructions: Stand on one foot on the floor and lift the other foot off the ground, knee bent.
Keep the arms relaxed at your sides and brace your core to hold your balance.
Drive up onto the ball of the foot as high as possible.
Lower the heel back to the floor under control.
Complete all reps on one side, then switch.
formCues: Pause at the top to maximize the contraction.
Lower slowly instead of dropping onto the heel.
Hold a dumbbell on the working side once bodyweight is too easy.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Single Leg Extension
alternativeNames: Extensión de Cuádriceps a Una Pierna
description: A quadriceps isolation exercise performed on a leg extension machine, working one leg at a time.
instructions: Sit on a leg extension machine and place one foot under the pad.
Rest the other foot on the floor or let it hang.
Extend the working leg until it is nearly straight.
Squeeze the quadriceps at the top.
Lower the leg back down under control.
Complete reps on one side, then switch.
formCues: Squeeze the quadriceps hard at the top of the movement.
Lower the weight under control rather than letting it drop.
Keep your back flat against the pad.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Single Leg Glute Bridge
alternativeNames: Puente de Glúteo a Una Pierna
description: A unilateral glute bridge that loads one glute at a time and helps even out side-to-side imbalances.
instructions: Lie on your back with one knee bent, foot flat, the other leg extended straight.
Brace the core and squeeze the glute on the working side.
Drive the hips up by pressing through the working heel.
Pause at the top with the body in a straight line from shoulders to knee.
Lower under control. Complete reps per side, then switch.
formCues: Keep the extended leg in line with the working thigh.
Squeeze the glute hard at the top — do not push with the lower back.
Slow the lowering phase for more stimulus.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Single-Leg Glute Bridge Hold
alternativeNames: Puente de Glúteo a Una Pierna Isométrico
description: The top of the single-leg glute bridge held for time: hips extended and level while one leg is lifted, so one glute carries the whole position.
instructions: Lie on your back with one knee bent and that foot flat, and lift the other leg so the thigh is roughly vertical.
Push through the heel of the planted foot and lift the hips until the body is straight from the knee to the shoulders.
Level the pelvis so the lifted side does not drop, and tuck the ribs down.
Hold the top position for the prescribed time, keeping the lifted knee still.
Lower the hips under control and repeat on the other side.
formCues: Watch the pelvis rather than the height: a level hip at a lower position beats a high, twisted one.
Keep the planted heel close to the glute so the hamstring does not cramp.
Extend the free leg straight if the position feels easy, but only while the pelvis stays level.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Single-Leg Hip Thrust
alternativeNames: Empuje de Cadera a Una Pierna
description: A hip thrust done on one leg: with your upper back resting on a flat bench and one foot planted on the floor, you drive your hips up until your body is level, holding the other knee raised. Working one side at a time isolates the glute and shows up any difference between the legs.
instructions: Sit on the floor with your back to a flat bench and rest your upper back against its edge, just below your shoulder blades.
Plant both feet flat on the floor with your knees bent, then lift one knee toward your chest and keep it there.
Keep your chin tucked toward your chest and your arms resting along the bench.
Drive through the heel of the planted foot and push your hips up until your body is level from your shoulders to your knee.
Squeeze your glute at the top without arching your lower back, then lower your hips under control.
Complete the planned repetitions, then switch legs.
formCues: Keep the planted shin close to vertical at the top so the glute, rather than the hamstring, does most of the work.
Do not let your hips twist toward the lifted leg; keep your pelvis level throughout.
Anchor the bench against a wall so it cannot slide, and start with the two-leg hip thrust until the movement is smooth.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Single-Leg Hip Thrust Hold
alternativeNames: Empuje de Cadera a Una Pierna Isométrico
description: A held top position of the hip thrust on one leg: with your upper back on a bench and one foot on the floor, you lift your hips until your body is flat and keep the other knee raised. Holding it loads the glute of the working leg through the full contraction.
instructions: Sit on the floor with your back to a flat bench and rest your upper back against its edge, just below your shoulder blades.
Plant both feet flat on the floor with your knees bent, then lift one knee toward your chest.
Keep the other foot planted under that knee and your chin tucked toward your chest.
Drive through the planted heel and push your hips up until your body is flat from shoulders to knee.
Keep your ribs down and hold the top position for the planned time.
Lower your hips under control and repeat on the other leg.
formCues: Do not arch the lower back at the top; finish the lift by squeezing the glute rather than thrusting the ribs up.
Keep the working shin close to vertical so the glute, not the hamstring, does most of the effort.
Anchor the bench against a wall so it cannot slide as you push.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Single Leg Lying Leg Curl
alternativeNames: Curl de Pierna Tumbado a Una Pierna
description: A unilateral hamstring isolation on the lying leg curl machine, addressing strength imbalances between legs.
instructions: Lie face down on a lying leg curl machine.
Position one ankle under the pad, keeping the other foot off the machine.
Curl the working leg by bringing your heel toward your glute.
Squeeze the hamstring at the top.
Lower the leg back down under control.
Complete reps on one side, then switch.
formCues: Keep your hips pressed into the bench throughout the curl.
Avoid jerking the pad up with momentum.
Start with the weaker leg and match its reps on the other side.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Single Leg Press
alternativeNames: Prensa de Piernas a Una Pierna
description: A lower-body exercise performed on a leg press machine, pressing the platform with one leg at a time.
instructions: Sit in a leg press machine with one foot placed on the platform.
Keep the other leg off the platform, resting to the side.
Release the safeties and lower the platform by bending your knee.
Stop when your knee is near a 90-degree angle.
Drive through the heel to press the platform back up.
Complete reps on one side, then switch.
formCues: Keep your foot flat and centered on the platform.
Avoid letting your knee cave inward.
Don't lock out the knee forcefully at the top.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Single Leg RDL Hold
alternativeNames: Peso Muerto Rumano a Una Pierna Isométrico
description: A balance hold at the bottom of a single-leg Romanian deadlift: standing on one leg, the torso is hinged forward and the other leg extends back in line with the body. It trains the hamstrings, glutes and trunk while challenging balance.
instructions: Stand on one leg with a slight bend in the knee and the arms hanging in front of you.
Hinge at the hip, sending the free leg straight back as the torso tips forward.
Keep the back flat and the hips square to the floor.
Stop when the torso and the free leg are roughly parallel to the floor and hold the position.
Return to standing under control, then switch legs.
formCues: Think of a seesaw: the torso and the free leg move together.
Keep the hips level; do not let the free hip rotate upward.
Fix your gaze on a point on the floor ahead to help your balance.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Single Leg Romanian Deadlift
alternativeNames: Peso Muerto Rumano a Una Pierna
description: A single-leg hip hinge with dumbbells, training the hamstrings and glutes while challenging balance and hip stability.
instructions: Stand on one leg holding a dumbbell in each hand in front of your thighs.
Keep a slight bend in the standing knee.
Hinge at the hip while extending the free leg behind you.
Lower the dumbbells along your standing leg until you feel a hamstring stretch.
Drive through the heel to return to upright.
Complete reps on one side, then switch.
formCues: Keep your hips square to the floor as you hinge.
Fix your eyes on a spot ahead to help balance.
Reach the rear heel straight back rather than letting the leg swing wide.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Sit-Ups
description: A classic abdominal exercise with a full range of motion.
instructions: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet anchored.
Cross your arms over your chest or place hands behind your head.
Sit all the way up until your torso is upright.
Lower back down with control.
Repeat.
formCues: Avoid pulling on your neck when your hands are behind your head.
Roll up through the spine rather than jerking with momentum.
Exhale on the way up to reinforce the abdominal contraction.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Six Inch Hold
description: A static core hold lying on the back with the head, shoulders and straight legs lifted about six inches off the floor. It trains the lower abdominals and hip flexors.
instructions: Lie on your back with the legs straight and the arms resting along your sides.
Press the lower back into the floor and brace the abdominals.
Lift the head, shoulders and straight legs about six inches off the floor.
Hold the position while breathing steadily.
Lower slowly to rest.
formCues: Keep the lower back flat; if it arches, raise the legs a little higher or bend the knees.
Keep the neck relaxed and the chin slightly tucked.
Build up with short holds and rest in between.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: SkiErg
description: A standing cardio exercise on a ski ergometer that combines a forceful double-pole pull with a small hip hinge to train full-body power and endurance.
instructions: Stand facing the SkiErg with the handles overhead and the feet about hip-width apart.
Brace the trunk and drive the handles down by pulling with the lats while hinging slightly at the hips.
Finish with the hands beside the thighs and the knees softly bent.
Let the cords retract as you return the arms overhead and stand tall.
Repeat smoothly while keeping the heels planted and the torso controlled.
formCues: Lead the pull with the lats instead of turning it into an arm-only movement.
Keep the hinge compact; do not collapse into a deep squat.
Allow the handles to return under control so the cords stay taut.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Skull Crusher
description: A lying triceps extension using a barbell to isolate the triceps through a full range of motion.
instructions: Lie on a flat bench holding a barbell over your chest with a narrow grip.
Lower the bar toward your forehead by bending at the elbows.
Extend your arms back to the start.
Repeat.
formCues: Lower slowly to protect the elbows.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Sled Push
description: A conditioning and leg-strength exercise: leaning into the uprights of a loaded sled, you drive it across the floor with short, powerful steps. The legs and glutes push the load while the arms and trunk stay braced, and there is no weight on the spine.
instructions: Load the sled and stand behind it, holding the uprights with your hands at about chest height.
Lean forward so your body forms a straight diagonal line from your head to your back heel, with your arms extended.
Brace your trunk and drive one knee forward, pushing the floor away with the ball of your back foot.
Keep taking short, powerful steps, driving each leg back hard to move the sled forward.
Keep your hips low and your back flat, and look a short distance ahead of the sled.
Push for the planned distance or time, then stop under control and rest before the next push.
formCues: Stay low with your arms locked or slightly bent; standing up tall makes you lose drive and push the sled with your arms.
Push through the balls of the feet with short, quick steps rather than long strides.
Pick a load you can keep moving at a steady pace; if the sled stops, the load is too heavy for the set.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Sled Row
description: A loaded carry-and-pull performed by holding a sled's strap handles and rowing it toward you as you walk backwards, training the back through a continuous drag rather than discrete reps.
instructions: Load a sled with two straps attached and take one strap handle in each hand.
Stand facing the sled with the arms extended and the torso leaned back slightly against the load.
Pull the sled toward you by driving the elbows back, and take a short step backwards as you do.
Extend the arms again, step back once more, and repeat the pull.
Continue for distance or time, keeping a steady pull-and-step rhythm.
formCues: Keep the chest up and the back flat — let the legs carry you backwards rather than rounding over the sled.
Use a load you can move continuously; the point is a steady drag, not a maximal pull.
No straps? A rope looped around the sled works the same way.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Smith Machine Bench Press
alternativeNames: Press de Banca en Máquina Smith
description: A bench press variation in the Smith machine, where the guided bar path adds stability for the chest.
instructions: Lie on a flat bench set inside a Smith machine.
Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width and unrack it.
Lower the bar under control to your mid-chest.
Pause briefly without bouncing.
Press the bar back up until your arms are fully extended.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
formCues: Align the bench so the bar lands at mid-chest, not the neck.
Keep your shoulder blades pulled back and down against the bench.
Keep your feet planted and your glutes on the bench.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Smith Machine Bent Over Row
description: A bent-over row in the Smith machine, with a fixed bar path that keeps the pull strict for the lats.
instructions: Stand inside a Smith machine with feet shoulder-width apart.
Grip the bar with an overhand grip slightly wider than shoulders.
Hinge at the hips until your torso is roughly 45 degrees.
Pull the bar toward your lower chest by driving your elbows back.
Squeeze your shoulder blades at the top.
Lower the bar under control and repeat.
formCues: Hold your hip hinge steady rather than rising as you fatigue.
Keep your neck neutral by looking at the floor slightly ahead.
Brace your core to protect the lower back throughout.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Smith Machine Bulgarian Split Squat
description: A Bulgarian split squat performed in a Smith machine for added stability and load control.
instructions: Set up a bench behind the Smith machine. Rest the bar on your traps.
Place the rear foot on the bench and front foot forward.
Lower your back knee toward the floor.
Push through the front heel to return.
Repeat on both sides.
formCues: The Smith machine guides the bar path.
Focus on keeping front knee tracking over toes.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Smith Machine Decline Bench Press
alternativeNames: Press de Banca Declinado en Máquina Smith
description: A bench press on a decline bench under the Smith machine, where the head-down angle and the guided bar path put the work on the lower chest.
instructions: Set a decline bench in the machine so the bar lines up with your lower chest when you lie down, and hook your legs under the pads.
Lie back with your head at the low end, take an overhand grip slightly wider than your shoulders and unrack the bar.
Lower the bar under control until it touches your lower chest, keeping your elbows at roughly forty-five degrees from your torso.
Press the bar back up until your arms are extended, without locking the elbows out hard.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then rack the bar before releasing your legs.
formCues: Line the bench up before you load it. The bar only moves in one plane, so if the bench is a few centimetres out the bar will meet your throat or your stomach instead of your lower chest.
Secure your legs under the pads first. Head-down and unsecured, you slide toward the low end of the bench on the first hard rep.
Come down and sit up slowly between sets. Long sets with the head below the heart make people light-headed, and this variation is where it happens.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Smith Machine Front Squat
description: A squat on the Smith machine with the bar racked across the front of the shoulders, where the fixed path and the upright torso keep the work on the quads.
instructions: Set the bar at upper-chest height and step under it so it rests across the front of your shoulders, against your collarbones.
Cross your arms over the bar or take an open front-rack grip, and drive your elbows up until your upper arms are close to parallel with the floor.
Unrack the bar and stand with your feet about shoulder-width apart and slightly forward of it.
Sit straight down, keeping your elbows high and your torso upright, until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor.
Drive through the middle of your feet to stand back up, and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
formCues: High elbows are the whole exercise. As soon as they drop, the bar rolls off your shoulders onto your hands and the rack position collapses.
Set the safety stops just below your deepest squat position before you unrack anything -- on a front squat the fastest way out of a failed rep is to let the bar go.
Standing slightly ahead of the bar lets you keep your torso vertical. Under a fixed path, a stance directly beneath the bar forces you to lean and pushes the bar off the front rack.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Smith Machine Good Morning
description: A hip hinge with the Smith machine bar resting on the upper back, bending forward at the hips against a fixed bar path to load the hamstrings and the spinal erectors.
instructions: Set the bar at upper-back height, step under it and settle it across your traps, then unrack it with your feet about hip-width apart.
Soften your knees slightly and keep them there -- this is a hinge, not a squat.
Push your hips straight back and let your torso tip forward, keeping your back flat and your head in line with your spine.
Stop when you feel a strong stretch in your hamstrings, with your torso somewhere near parallel to the floor.
Drive your hips forward to stand back up, squeezing the glutes at the top, and repeat for the desired reps.
formCues: Use much less weight than you would for a squat. The bar is a long way from your hips at the bottom, and that lever, not the number on the bar, is what the exercise costs you.
Hips back, not chest down. If your torso drops without your hips travelling backwards you are bending your spine instead of hinging at the hip.
Let the range of motion end where your back would start to round. Depth on a good morning is set by your hamstrings, and the machine will happily take you past that point.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Smith Machine Hip Thrust
description: A hip thrust with the bar running in the Smith machine guides, so the load travels in a fixed vertical line across the hips while the shoulders stay supported on a bench.
instructions: Set a flat bench inside the Smith machine, parallel to the bar and positioned so the bar will sit over your hip crease.
Set the bar low enough that you can get under it while seated on the floor, then sit with your upper back against the bench.
Slide your hips under the bar so it sits over your hip crease, pad it if you need to, and unhook it with your feet flat and about hip-width apart.
Drive through your heels and extend your hips until your thighs and torso form a straight line, squeezing the glutes at the top.
Lower your hips under control until they are just off the floor, and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
formCues: Line the bench up before you load the bar. The bar can only move straight up and down, so if the bench is out of place the bar lands on your stomach or your thighs and there is no adjusting mid-set.
Set the safety stops where the bar sits at the bottom of your range. Getting out from under a loaded Smith bar on the floor is awkward, and the stops make it a non-event.
Look at a point in front of you rather than at the ceiling. Keeping the chin tucked stops the movement turning into a lower-back arch at lockout.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Smith Machine Incline Bench Press
description: An incline press in the Smith machine, guiding the bar to target the upper chest and front delts.
instructions: Set an incline bench at 30-45 degrees inside a Smith machine.
Lie back and grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Unrack and lower the bar to your upper chest.
Pause briefly at the bottom.
Press the bar back up until your arms are extended.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
formCues: Position the bench so the bar lands on the upper chest, not the throat.
Stack your wrists directly above your elbows.
Avoid driving your head forward off the bench as you press.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Smith Machine Romanian Deadlift
alternativeNames: Peso Muerto Rumano en Máquina Smith
description: A Romanian deadlift performed on a Smith machine, fixing the bar path so you can focus on the hip hinge and posterior-chain stretch.
instructions: Set the Smith machine bar at mid-thigh height and stand facing it, feet hip-width, close enough that the bar touches your thighs.
Unrack the bar with an overhand grip just outside the hips.
Push the hips back while letting the bar slide down the front of the legs.
Go until you feel a deep hamstring stretch, with a flat back and a soft knee bend.
Drive the hips forward to return to standing, keeping the bar close to the body.
Repeat for the recommended number of repetitions.
formCues: The bar is locked to a straight path — use that to groove the hinge pattern.
Do not round the lower back at the bottom; stop at the end of your hamstring range.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Smith Machine Reverse Grip Bent Over Row
alternativeNames: Smith Machine Reverse Grip Bent Over Row
Remo Inclinado con Agarre Inverso en Máquina Smith
description: An underhand-grip row performed in the Smith machine, biasing the lower lats and biceps on a guided bar path.
instructions: Stand inside a Smith machine and grip the bar with an underhand grip.
Hinge forward at the hips until your torso is about 45 degrees.
Keep your back flat and core braced.
Pull the bar toward your lower abdomen.
Squeeze your lats and shoulder blades at the top.
Lower the bar under control and repeat.
formCues: Keep your wrists straight under the underhand grip.
Drive your elbows back close to your sides.
Avoid rising out of the hinge to cheat the bar up.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Smith Machine Reverse Lunge
description: A reverse lunge under a Smith machine bar, stepping one foot back into the lunge and returning it to standing each repetition while the guided bar holds the load steady.
instructions: Set the bar so it sits across your upper traps when you stand, then unrack it with your feet under your hips.
Step one foot straight back and lower the rear knee toward the floor, keeping the front shin vertical and most of your weight on the front foot.
Stop when the rear knee is just short of the floor and the front thigh is roughly parallel to it.
Push through the front heel and bring the rear foot back to standing under the bar.
Complete all the repetitions on one side, then switch legs, or alternate legs on every repetition.
formCues: Step back far enough. A short step puts the front knee well past the toes, which the fixed bar path will not let you correct once you are loaded.
The stepping foot does the travelling; the front foot does not move at all. If it shifts between reps, your step is too long or too short.
The rack removes the balance, not the load -- keep the trunk braced and stand up out of the bottom rather than leaning back into the bar.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Smith Machine Shoulder Press
alternativeNames: Press de Hombros en Máquina Smith
description: A standing overhead press in the Smith machine, with the guided bar path providing stability for the shoulders.
instructions: Stand inside a Smith machine with your feet hip-width apart and the bar at shoulder level.
Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width at shoulder level.
Unrack the bar and press it overhead until your arms are extended.
Lower the bar back to shoulder level under control.
Keep your core tight throughout.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
formCues: Stand directly under the bar path before unracking.
Tilt your head back slightly as the bar passes your face.
Avoid flaring your ribs as the bar travels overhead.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Smith Machine Shrug
alternativeNames: Encogimiento de Hombros en Máquina Smith
description: A Smith machine isolation exercise elevating the shoulders to target the trapezius with a fixed bar path.
instructions: Stand upright inside a Smith machine with the bar at thigh height.
Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width with an overhand grip.
Unrack the bar and let it hang in front of your thighs.
Shrug your shoulders straight up toward your ears.
Hold the top for a moment, then lower slowly.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
formCues: Keep your arms straight so the traps, not the biceps, do the work.
Lift straight up and down rather than rolling the shoulders.
Keep your neck neutral and avoid jutting the chin forward.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Smith Machine Split Squat
alternativeNames: Sentadilla en Tijera en Máquina Smith
description: A stationary split squat under a Smith machine bar, with the rear foot resting on the floor rather than a bench, so the guided path takes balance out of a single-leg movement.
instructions: Set the bar on the hooks just below shoulder height, then step under it and rest it across your upper traps.
Unrack the bar and take a long stride forward with one foot, leaving the rear foot planted on the floor with the heel lifted.
Check that your front shin will stay roughly vertical when you descend; adjust the stride length before you start loading it.
Lower straight down by bending both knees until the rear knee is just above the floor and the front thigh is close to parallel.
Drive through the front heel to return to the start, keeping both feet in place, and repeat for the desired reps before switching sides.
formCues: Set the stride length first, unloaded. Once the bar is on your back the fixed path will not let you shuffle forward to fix a stance that is too short.
Go straight down rather than forward. The bar can only travel vertically, so pushing the hips forward just jams your front knee past your toes.
Do the same number of reps on each side and start with the weaker leg, since a machine-guided split squat hides a side-to-side difference that a free bar would expose.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Smith Machine Squat
description: A squat performed on the Smith machine, using the fixed bar path for added stability while training quads and glutes.
instructions: Set the Smith machine bar at shoulder height and step under it.
Position the bar across your upper traps and unrack it.
Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, slightly forward of the bar.
Descend until your thighs are parallel to the floor.
Drive through your heels to return to standing.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
formCues: Keep your knees tracking in line with your toes.
Brace your core and keep your chest up throughout the movement.
Set the safety stops just below your lowest squat depth.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Smith Machine Upright Row
alternativeNames: Remo al Mentón en Máquina Smith
description: An upright row on the Smith machine, pulling the guided bar up the front of the torso with the elbows leading, to work the side deltoids and the upper traps.
instructions: Set the bar at hip height, take an overhand grip a little wider than shoulder-width and stand close to it with your arms straight.
Unrack the bar and stand tall with your shoulders back and your core braced.
Pull the bar straight up the front of your body, leading with your elbows and keeping the bar close.
Stop when the bar reaches your lower chest and your elbows are level with your shoulders, then pause briefly.
Lower the bar under control until your arms are straight again, and repeat for the desired reps.
formCues: Stop at chest height. Pulling the bar to the collarbone rotates the shoulder into the position that causes the impingement this exercise is known for.
Lead with the elbows, not the hands. If the wrists come up first the biceps take over and the side deltoids barely work.
Widen the grip if the movement pinches. A narrow grip forces more internal rotation, and the fixed bar path gives you nowhere else to go.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Snatch
description: An Olympic lift pulling a barbell from the floor to overhead in one motion, caught in an overhead squat.
instructions: Stand with feet hip-width apart and grip the bar wide.
Hinge down, keeping your back flat and chest up.
Explosively extend hips, knees, and ankles to drive the bar up.
Pull yourself under the bar into an overhead squat.
Stand up with the bar locked out overhead.
Return the bar to the floor and repeat.
formCues: Keep the bar close to your body as it travels up.
Extend your hips fully before pulling under the bar.
Lock your arms out and stabilize before standing up.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Sphinx Pose
description: A gentle prone backbend on the forearms: the elbows stay under the shoulders and the chest lifts, so the lower back extends without any strain from the arms.
instructions: Lie face down and place the forearms on the floor with the elbows directly under the shoulders.
Press the forearms and the tops of the feet down and lift the chest.
Draw the shoulders away from the ears and lengthen the back of the neck.
Hold the position for the prescribed time, breathing into the front of the chest.
Lower the chest to the floor and rest.
formCues: Slide the elbows slightly forward for a gentler bend, back for a deeper one.
Keep the glutes soft so the lower back does not clench.
Stop where the position feels like a stretch, not like a pinch.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Spider Curl
description: A curl lying face-down on an incline bench with arms hanging vertical, isolating the biceps through a strict range.
instructions: Lie face down on an incline bench with arms hanging straight down.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand with an underhand grip.
Keep your upper arms vertical as you curl the weights up.
Squeeze the biceps hard at the top.
Lower the dumbbells under control to full extension.
Repeat for the desired number of reps.
formCues: Keep your chest glued to the pad for the whole set.
Squeeze at the top without letting the elbows drift backward.
Use the full range — the stretch at the bottom is half the value.
breathingInstructions: Maintain rhythmic breathing throughout.

name: Spiderman Push-Up
description: A push-up in which one knee is drawn up toward the elbow on the same side as the body lowers, like a spider climbing a wall. It trains the chest, shoulders and triceps while the obliques and hip flexors hold the trunk steady.
instructions: Start in a high plank with the hands slightly wider than the shoulders and the body in a straight line.
Begin to lower the chest toward the floor and at the same time lift one foot off the floor.
Draw that knee out and up toward the elbow on the same side, keeping the hips low.
Press back up to the plank while returning the leg to the starting position.
Repeat on the other side and keep alternating.
formCues: Keep the hips level; letting them pike or sag takes the work off the trunk.
